hinglish: "Con" (saath) + "Vention" (vishesh): jab log ek saath milte hain kisi vishesh parampra ke liye, tab vo conventional hota hai. Uski shaadi bahut conventional thi, sab purani paramparao ko follow karte hue.

meaning: a firmly held belief or opinion
mnemonic: "Con" (with) + "Vict" (winner): when you have a strong conviction, you feel like a winner in your beliefs, guiding your actions.
hinglish: "Con" (sath) + "Vikt" (jeet): jab aapke paas ek mazboot conviction hoti hai, toh aap apne vishwas mein jeetne jaise mehsoos karte hain.

meaning: sociable and cheerful; characterized by lively and enjoyable company
mnemonic: Con + Vivial: when you're in a convivial setting, you 'con' (with) 'viv' (life), sharing lively moments with others.
hinglish: Con + Vivial: jab aap kisi party mein hote hain, toh aap 'con' (saath) 'vivial' (jeevan) mahsoos karte hain, jahan sab khush hote hain.

meaning: extremely intricate and complicated
mnemonic: "Con" + "Volute": when you con someone, you twist their understanding; this leads to convoluted arguments that are hard to follow.
hinglish: "Con" + "Volute": jab aap kisi ko con karte hain, toh aap unka samajh twisted kar dete hain, isliye baatein convoluted ban jaati hain.

meaning: abundant in quantity; very large in amount
mnemonic: Co + Pious: a copious amount of pious deeds can fill a whole book; hence, it refers to an abundant quantity.
hinglish: Co + Pious: agar aap bohot saari pious (dharmik) kaam karte hain, toh aapko copious (bahut adhik) laabh milta hai.

meaning: warm and friendly
mnemonic: Cordial -> 'Core Deal': when you have a core deal, you treat each other with warmth and cordiality.
hinglish: Cordial -> 'Kordial': jab aap kisi ko kordial treat karte hain, to aap unhe dosto se bhi zyada apne jaisa mehsoos karte hain.

meaning: relating to the body; physical
mnemonic: Corporeal -> 'Core' + 'Pore': the core of a being is its corporeal body, where all physical attributes are contained.
hinglish: Core + Pore: insaan ka core uski shariarik astitva hai, jo uski corporeal qualities ko darshata hai.

meaning: to show a mutual relationship or connection between two or more things
mnemonic: Core + Relate: when you find the core aspects of two subjects, you can easily correlate them — just like how diet and health are related.
hinglish: Core + Relate: jab aap do cheezon ke core sambandh ko samajhte hain, toh aap unhe correlate kar sakte hain — jaise diet aur health ka sambandh hai.

meaning: to confirm or give support to a statement, theory, or finding
mnemonic: Corroborate -> 'Core' + 'Robber': imagine a core group of friends trying to 'rob' the truth from a story, they must corroborate their claims to ensure they align.
hinglish: Core + Robber: soch lo, agar koi core group mein dosto ko kahin 'rob' karne ki baat kare, toh unhe apne kahani ko corroborate karna padega.

meaning: a person who is familiar with and at ease in many different countries and cultures
mnemonic: Cosmos + Politician: a cosmopolitan is like a politician who knows every corner of the cosmos and can mingle with people from every city and culture.
hinglish: Cosmo + Politician: ek cosmopolitan aisa vyakti hai jo har sheher aur sanskriti se waakif hota hai, jaise ek politician jo har jagah jaata hai.

meaning: A person's face or facial expression; support.
mnemonic: "Count the Nuance": Looking closely at someone's face to count the subtle expressions (nuances) on their countenance.

meaning: A fraudulent imitation of something else; fake.
mnemonic: "Counter + Fit": Giving fake notes at the counter that don't fit the legal standards.

meaning: Not openly acknowledged or displayed; secret.
mnemonic: "Covered": It sounds exactly like covered — a covert operation is completely covered up.

meaning: Yearn to possess or have something belonging to someone else.
mnemonic: "Covertly want it": You look at your friend's new car and covetously wish you could take it for yourself.

meaning: Making a pretense of shyness or modesty that is intended to be alluring.
mnemonic: "Toying": Acting shy and playing with a toy or your hair to look innocent.

meaning: Clever at achieving one's aims by deceitful or evasive methods.
mnemonic: "Craft": Someone who uses their craft (skills) not for art, but to trick people.

meaning: Contemptibly lacking in courage; cowardly.
mnemonic: "Cave in": A soldier who caves in instantly out of fear because he is craven.

meaning: Able to be believed; convincing.
mnemonic: "Credit card": The bank only gives a credit card to someone who is credible (trustworthy).

meaning: A gradual increase in loudness or intensity.
mnemonic: "Increase-endo": Think of a musical beat that starts low and rises to a massive peak.

meaning: Sad and disappointed.
mnemonic: "Crest (Top) + Fallen": You were riding high at the crest of the wave, but then you fell down — totally disappointed.

meaning: Hum or sing in a soft, low voice, especially in a sentimental manner.
mnemonic: "Crow turning into a Peacock": Imagine a bird trying to sing a smooth, romantic melody softly.

meaning: Large or heavy and therefore difficult to carry or use; unwieldy.
mnemonic: "Kamra-some": A piece of furniture so big it takes up the whole kamra (room) and is tough to move.

meaning: Having or showing skill in achieving one's ends by deceit.
mnemonic: "Kan-kaatna": Someone so sharp they can kaat your kaan without you noticing.

meaning: Restrain or keep in check.
mnemonic: "Curb on the road": The concrete curb keeps the cars from driving off the road — it curbs them.

meaning: A bad-tempered or surly person.
mnemonic: "Car + Mud": An old, angry man whose car got stuck in the mud, making him highly irritated.

meaning: Hasty and therefore not thorough or detailed.
mnemonic: "Cursor": Moving your computer cursor lightning-fast across the screen just to skim a page.

meaning: Reduce in extent or quantity.
mnemonic: "Cut the tail": Stripping down resources or time to shorten it.

meaning: Seeming difficult to deal with in anticipation; intimidating.
mnemonic: "Daantna": A task so massive it feels like a strict teacher daant-ing (scolding) you just by looking at it.

meaning: to waste time or be slow in taking action
mnemonic: "Dawdle" -> "Dawdle a Little": if you dawdle, you just waste time instead of completing tasks efficiently.
hinglish: "Dawdle" -> "Dodaal": agar tum dodaal karoge, toh tumhara kaam poora nahi hoga aur tum waqt barbaad karoge.

meaning: a scarcity or lack of something
mnemonic: Dear + Th: when you have a dear friend, you want to share everything, but if there's a dearth of resources, you can't.
hinglish: Dear + Th: jab aapke paas kuch khaas dosto ke liye kuch nahi hai, tab aap kehte hain, 'kya dearth hai resources ki!'

meaning: to lower in value or quality
mnemonic: Debate + Base: if you debate a base issue, you are likely to debase the conversation and lower its quality.
hinglish: Debate + Base: agar aap base topic par debate karte hain, to aap conversation ko debase kar rahe hain.

meaning: causing a severe reduction in strength or ability
mnemonic: Debilitate -> De + Bill + It: if you fail to pay a bill, it can debilitate your finances, leaving you in a weakened position.
hinglish: De + Bill + It: agar aap bill nahi bharenge, toh yeh aapki financial situation ko debilititate karega.

meaning: to expose the falseness or hollowness of (a myth, idea, or belief)
mnemonic: "Debunk" -> "Debunking a Bunk": when you debunk a myth, you're essentially taking apart a 'bunk' idea, revealing it to be false.
hinglish: "Debunk" -> "Debungi a Bunk": jab aap kisi ghalat faisle ko debunk karte hain, toh aap us 'bunk' idea ko sachai se alag karte hain.

meaning: characterized by excessive indulgence in pleasure or luxury
mnemonic: Decay + Dents: a decadent cake is like a cake with decay that has all sorts of dents from overindulgence — it's rich, but too much can spoil the fun.
hinglish: Decay + Dents: ek decadent cake aisa hai jaise khana jismein itna zyada indulgence hota hai ki wo decay ho jata hai — wo rich hai, lekin zyada hona kharab kar sakta hai.

meaning: to interpret or make sense of something difficult to understand
mnemonic: Decide + Cipher: when you decide to decode a secret message (cipher), you need to decipher it to understand its meaning.
hinglish: Decide + Cipher: jab aap kisi secret message ko samjhne ka faisla karte hain, toh aapko usse decipher karna padta hai.

meaning: Behavior in keeping with good taste and propriety.
mnemonic: "Decorate the Room": When guests arrive, you decorate the room and maintain proper, polite manners (decorum).

meaning: Publicly denounce or criticize.
mnemonic: "Deep + Cry": Crying out loud in public to protest against something bad.

meaning: Damage the good reputation of someone.
mnemonic: "De (Down) + Fame": Pulling someone's fame down by spreading rumors.

meaning: Polite submission and respect.
mnemonic: "Respect the Difference": Recognizing the difference in age or rank and showing high respect to an elder.

meaning: Cause something to change direction; turn aside.
mnemonic: "Reflect vs Deflect": Like a mirror reflects light, a shield deflects an incoming arrow away from you.

meaning: Neatly skillful and quick in one's movements.
mnemonic: "Deaf to Distractions": A master craftsman or coder who is so focused and deft with their hands that they are deaf to outside noise.

meaning: Treat or worship someone as a god.
mnemonic: "Deity": Turning a regular human into a deity (God) because you admire them too much.

meaning: Causing harm or damage.
mnemonic: "Delete + Serious": Something so harmful that it causes serious damage, forcing you to delete it from your life.

meaning: Done consciously and intentionally; carefully weighed.
mnemonic: "Daily + Debate": Thinking so carefully that it feels like a daily debate in your mind before making a final choice.

meaning: Describe or portray something precisely.
mnemonic: "De-Line-Ate": Drawing a clear line on paper to show boundaries step-by-step.

meaning: A belief firmly maintained despite being contradicted by reality.
mnemonic: "Illusion in Mind": A permanent illusion stuck in your head making you believe things that aren't real.

meaning: Raise doubts or objections; show reluctance.
mnemonic: "Damn + Mur (Mudna)": Stopping right where you are, turning around (mudna), and saying, "Damn, I object to this!"

meaning: Criticize unfairly; disparage.
mnemonic: "Degrade + Negate": Trying to negate someone's hard work and degrade their value in front of others.

meaning: Publicly declare to be wrong or evil.
mnemonic: "Announce the Crime": Making a loud public announcement that a politician or policy is completely corrupt.

meaning: A person's behavior or manners.
mnemonic: "How you behave at the Airport/Port": Your behavioral etiquette (deportment) matters when you interact with authorities at a port.

meaning: Remove from office suddenly and forcefully; testify.
mnemonic: "De-Position": Kicking a dictator out of his royal position by force.

meaning: Moral corruption; wickedness.
mnemonic: "Deep + Gravity": Someone sinking deep into the gravity of crimes and bad morals.

meaning: Express disapproval of; deplore.
mnemonic: "Depreciate Value": Looking down on an idea or criticizing it, lowering its importance (self-deprecating humor = making fun of yourself).

meaning: Express contempt for; ridicule.
mnemonic: "De-Ride": Making fun of someone so badly that you completely ruin their ride or confidence.

meaning: Imitative of the work of another person, and usually disapproved of for that reason.
mnemonic: "Derived from Calculus": Not original — something derived entirely from an existing formula or idea.

meaning: Remove the moisture from something; cause to become completely dry.
mnemonic: "Desert + Cake": Leaving a cake out in the hot desert sun until it becomes completely dry and crumbly.

meaning: Characteristic of a despot; tyrannical.
mnemonic: "Boss + Dictator": A cruel, absolute ruler who acts like a ruthless boss over everyone.

meaning: Lacking a plan, purpose, or enthusiasm.
mnemonic: "Result-less Story": Jumping from one topic to another without a plan, leading to a result-less story.

meaning: The easing of hostility or strained relations, especially between countries.
mnemonic: "De-Tension": The absolute easing of tension between two warring nations.

meaning: Discourage someone from doing something by instilling doubt or fear of the consequences.
mnemonic: "Detergent bars the dirt": Like soap keeps dirt away, a heavy fine deters people from breaking traffic laws.

meaning: Reduce or take away the worth or value of something.
mnemonic: "De (Down) + Attract": Pulling the attraction or value of an achievement down by pointing out minor flaws.

meaning: Tending to cause harm.
mnemonic: "Nutrient ka Ulta": Nutrients are good for health; something detrimental acts like a poison that ruins health.

meaning: Depart from an established course or standard.
mnemonic: "De-Route via Alternative": Turning away from the main highway to take a side road.

meaning: Showing a skillful use of underhanded tactics to achieve goals; winding.
mnemonic: "Devil-ish": A devious plan is a cunning, devil-ish scheme to trick someone.

meaning: Showing or having skill, especially with the hands.
mnemonic: "Dexter's Laboratory" / "Dexterity": Think of an expert scientist or coder who is incredibly quick and skilled with his hands.

meaning: A forceful and bitter verbal attack against someone or something.
mnemonic: "Die + Tribe": An angry speech wishing a whole tribe would die — a massive verbal teardown.

meaning: A division or contrast between two things represented as being opposed or entirely different.
mnemonic: "Di (Two) + Cut": Literally cutting something cleanly into two completely opposite halves.

meaning: State with authoritative force; command.
mnemonic: "Dictator": Giving orders like an absolute ruler that everyone else must follow without question.

meaning: A formal pronouncement from an authoritative source.
mnemonic: "Dictator's words": An official, wise, or authoritative saying that is treated as law.

meaning: Intended to teach, particularly in having moral instruction as an ulterior motive.
mnemonic: "Didi + Act": Your elder Didi always acting like a school teacher, trying to give you life lessons and moral lectures.

meaning: Modest or shy because of a lack of self-confidence.
mnemonic: "Difficult to Confide": Someone who finds it difficult to talk to people because they lack confidence.

meaning: Spread out over a large area; not concentrated.
mnemonic: "Diffuser": Like a room freshener diffuser that spreads a scent widely across the entire hall.

meaning: A temporary departure from the main subject in speech or writing.
mnemonic: "Diversion on Highway": Leaving the main topic during a lecture to tell a random story, then coming back.

meaning: Slow to act; intended to cause delay.
mnemonic: "Delay-tory": Doing tasks so slowly that you deliberately cause a delay.

meaning: A person who cultivates an area of interest without real commitment or knowledge.
mnemonic: "Dil se thoda sa": Someone who dabbles in coding, photography or music just for fun (dil se), but isn't a serious professional.

meaning: Extremely or unusually small.
mnemonic: "Diminish": Something that has diminished in size so much that it has become tiny.

meaning: A lament for the dead, especially one forming part of a funeral rite.
mnemonic: "Die + Song": A sad song sung when someone has died.

meaning: Able to be discerned; perceptible.
hindi: Saaf dikhne wala / Pehchana jaane yogya
mnemonic: "Discoverable": Clear enough to be noticed or discovered by the eyes or mind.

meaning: A personal follower of a teacher, philosopher, or religious leader.
mnemonic: "Discipline": A student who follows a master with strict discipline.

meaning: Make someone feel uneasy or embarrassed.
mnemonic: "Dis-comfort": Literally putting someone out of their comfort zone and making them blush or sweat.

meaning: Causing one to feel unsettled.
mnemonic: "Dis-concert": If the music stops suddenly during a live concert, the sudden silence is highly disconcerting.

meaning: Regard a possibility or fact as being unworthy of consideration; reduce price.
mnemonic: "Dismiss the Count": Throwing an idea out of calculations because you think it's highly unlikely.

meaning: Careful and circumspect in one's speech or actions, especially to avoid causing offense.
mnemonic: "Secret Keeper": Being quiet and careful so secrets don't leak — the double 'e' looks like two closed eyes keeping a secret, unlike discrete which means separate.

meaning: An illogical or surprising lack of compatibility between two or more facts.
mnemonic: "Difference in Receipt": A mismatch between the money you spent and the amount written on the final bill.

meaning: The feeling that someone or something is unworthy of one's consideration or respect.
mnemonic: "Dis-respect the Stain": Looking down on someone with absolute contempt, treating them like a dirty stain.

meaning: Free something from an entanglement; extricate.
mnemonic: "Dis + Tangle": Untangling a messy knot of wires or a complicated situation.

meaning: Not candid or sincere, typically by pretending that one knows less about something than one really does.
mnemonic: "Dis (Not) + Genuine": Someone who pretends to be innocent but is secretly playing a game.

meaning: Not influenced by considerations of personal advantage; unbiased.
mnemonic: "Distance from Interest": A judge who keeps his personal profits away from a case so he can remain completely fair (not the same as bored/uninterested).

meaning: Take a machine or structure to pieces.
mnemonic: "Mantelpiece nikalna": Taking an entire engine or structure apart piece by piece.

meaning: Essentially different in kind; not allowing comparison.
mnemonic: "Dis-separate": Keeping things completely different and separate because they don't match.

meaning: Distribute or provide a service or information; manage without (dispense with).
mnemonic: "Dispenser": Like a sanitizer dispenser giving out soap, or dispensing with old rules (throwing them away).

meaning: Distribute or spread over a wide area.
mnemonic: "Dis-purse": If a purse snaps open on the street, all the coins disperse (scatter) everywhere.

meaning: Conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.
mnemonic: "Dis-assemble your real self": Hiding your true, angry face behind a fake smile to fool people.

meaning: Spread something, especially information, widely.
mnemonic: "Discuss via Internet": Blasting information, news or knowledge across the web so millions see it.

meaning: The expression or holding of opinions at variance with those officially held.
mnemonic: "Dis-sentiment": Going completely against the popular sentiment, or voting "No" when everyone else votes "Yes".

meaning: A person who opposes official policy, especially that of an authoritarian state.
mnemonic: "Dis-Sident (sidhe baithne ka ulta)": A rebel who refuses to sit down quietly and actively protests against the government.

meaning: Swell or cause to swell by pressure from inside.
mnemonic: "Distance + Extend": A stomach or balloon extending its size and expanding outwards due to gas or water.

meaning: Extract the essential elements of something; purify a liquid.
mnemonic: "Distilled Water": Boiling away the waste to extract only the purest, most concentrated essence of a topic or liquid.

meaning: Pull or twist out of shape; give a misleading account of.
mnemonic: "Dis-torture the truth": Twisting facts or a picture so much that the original shape and meaning is ruined.

meaning: Suffering from anxiety, sorrow, or pain.
mnemonic: "Stress extreme level": Being deeply troubled, heartbroken, or facing a highly stressful emergency.

meaning: Tending to be different or develop in different directions.
hindi: Binn / Alag disha mein jaane wala
mnemonic: "Diverge": Lines or opinions that start at the same point but split up and head in totally opposite directions.

meaning: Separate or disconnected from something.
mnemonic: "Divorce": Permanently separated from reality or from another entity — his theories are completely divorced from reality.

meaning: Make known private or sensitive information.
mnemonic: "Die + Vulg (vulgar secret)": Promising you won't reveal a secret until you die, but then divulging (leaking) it to everyone.

meaning: Seeking to impose a doctrine in all circumstances without regard to practical considerations.
mnemonic: "Doctor of Rules": A rigid person who stubbornly insists on following bookish theories, completely ignoring reality.

meaning: Consisting of official written or printed matter; a factual film.
mnemonic: "Documents": Based entirely on solid, real-life documents and facts rather than fiction.

meaning: Having or showing tenacity and grim persistence.
mnemonic: "Dog-like chase": Chasing a goal relentlessly, like a hunting dog that absolutely refuses to give up the scent.

meaning: Inclined to lay down principles as incontrovertibly true.
mnemonic: "Dog is Must": My way is the only right way — rigidly imposing your beliefs on everyone else.

meaning: Having normal physical functions suspended or slowed down for a period of time.
mnemonic: "Dormitory": Like students sleeping soundly in a university dormitory — a volcano or virus that is currently inactive but alive.

meaning: Unfashionable and without style in appearance.
mnemonic: "Dull + Lady": Dressing in old, sloppy, unfashionable clothes that lack colour or sharpness.

meaning: Excessively harsh and severe.
mnemonic: "Dracula's Laws": Imagine Dracula becoming the prime minister and passing terrifyingly cruel, severe punishments for tiny mistakes.

meaning: amusing in an odd or whimsical way
mnemonic: Droll -> 'Droll' (like 'Troll'): A droll troll tells jokes in a whimsical way that makes everyone laugh.
hinglish: Droll -> 'Droll' (jaise 'Troll'): Ek droll troll aise mazak karta hai ki sab log hasne lagte hain.

meaning: hesitating or doubting; not to be relied upon
mnemonic: "Do you be us?" (questioning reliability): when you ask someone if they are reliable, you're expressing your dubious feelings about them. — She felt dubious about his intentions.
hinglish: "Do you be us?" (questioning reliability): jab aap kisi se poochte hain ki kya woh vishwasniya hain, toh aap apne dubious bhavnaayein vyakt kar rahe hain. — Usne uski kahani par dubious rehkar muskurahat di.

meaning: to deceive or trick someone
mnemonic: "Do" + "Pe": when someone is trying to dupe you, they say 'Do Pe' (two for the price of one) to trick you into believing you're getting a good deal.
hinglish: "Do" + "Pe": jab koi tumhe dhoka dene ki koshish karta hai, woh kehta hai 'Do Pe' (do ka daam ek) taaki tumhe lagay ke tumhe achha deal mil raha hai.

meaning: deceitful, double-dealing
mnemonic: "Duplicate" + "Deceit": a duplicitous person is like someone who is deceitfully duplicating their true intentions — they are not what they seem.
hinglish: "Duplicate" + "Cheat": ek duplicitous aadmi woh hota hai jo apne asli iraadon ko duplicate karke cheat karta hai.

meaning: compulsion by threat or force
mnemonic: Dew + Dress: imagine someone being forced to wear a dress covered in dew — they are under duress to comply.
hinglish: Du + Res: jab koi insaan dusre se darr ke maare kuch karne par majboor hota hai, tab woh duress me hota hai.

meaning: showing a sense of duty or obligation
mnemonic: Duty + Full: being full of duty means you are dutiful in fulfilling your responsibilities.
hinglish: Duty + Full: jab aap apne kartavyon se bhare hote hain, tab aap duty se bhare hote hain, yaani aap dutiful hain.

meaning: gradually decreasing in size, amount, or strength
mnemonic: Dwindle -> 'Dwindle the Candle': as the candle burns down, its wax dwindles away, indicating a decrease in size.
hinglish: Dwindle -> 'Dwindle the Candle': jaisa jaisa candle jalta hai, waisa waisa uska size dwindling hota hai.

meaning: overflowing with enthusiasm or excitement
mnemonic: "Ebullient" -> "Ebullition" (boiling over): When someone is ebullient, they are bubbling over with joy and excitement, just like a pot of water on the stove that ebullitionally spills over.
hinglish: "Ebullient" -> "Ebullition" (ubalta hua): Jab koi insaan ebullient hota hai, to wo itna utsaahi hota hai ki jaise paani ubal kar beh raha ho.

meaning: unconventional and slightly strange in behavior or appearance
mnemonic: "Ex" (out) + "Centric" (center): being eccentric means you are out of the center of normal behavior, making you delightfully odd.
hinglish: "Ex" (bahar) + "Centric" (kendra): eccentric hone ka matlab hai ki aap samanya vyavhaar se bahar hain, jo aapko ajeeb aur anokha banata hai.

meaning: a level or rank in an organization or system
mnemonic: "Echolocation" -> "Echelon Location": in echolocation, animals determine their location in layers; similarly, an echelon indicates a rank or level within a hierarchy.
hinglish: "Echolocation" + "Level": echolocation se jaanwar apne sthal ko pata karte hain, jaise echelon kisi vyakti ya vastu ka level ya rank darshata hai.

meaning: deriving ideas, style, or taste from a broad and diverse range of sources
mnemonic: Eclectic -> E+Collect: when you collect various items from different sources, you develop an eclectic collection.
hinglish: E+Collect: jab aap alag-alag jagahon se cheezein ikattha karte hain, toh aapka taste eclectic ho jaata hai.

meaning: an event where one celestial body moves into the shadow of another celestial body
mnemonic: "Eclipse" -> "Eclipse the Lips": when the moon eclipses the sun, it's like it silences (or eclipses) the sun's brightness, making everything darker.
hinglish: "Eclipse" -> "Eclipse the Lips": jab chand suraj ko eclipse karta hai, tab suraj ki roshni band ho jaati hai, jaise woh sabko chup kar deta hai.

meaning: the system by which goods and services are produced, distributed, and consumed
mnemonic: Echo + Nomie: imagine an 'echoing' term that refers to a system of managing resources; the economy governs how resources are allocated.
hinglish: Echo + Nomi: socho ek 'echo' jo bataata hai kis tarah se saman aur sevaon ka istemal hota hai; economy wahi hai jo resources ka management karti hai.

meaning: to instruct or improve someone morally or intellectually
mnemonic: Edify -> 'Ed' (Education) + 'Ify' (to make): to edify someone is to make them educated and morally better.
hinglish: Ed + Ify: agar aap kisi ko education dena chahte hain, to aap unhe edify karte hain.

meaning: capable of producing a desired effect
mnemonic: Efficient + Cactus: a cactus is a plant that survives efficiently in the desert, much like an efficacious method achieves its goals effectively.
hinglish: Effect + Cactus: ek cactus desert me ache se survive karta hai, waise hi ek efficacious tareeka apne goals ko achieve karta hai.

meaning: shameless boldness or audacity
mnemonic: Effrontery -> 'Fron' (front) + 'Terry' (a name): Terry walked up to the boss and demanded a raise upfront; his effrontery surprised everyone in the office.
hinglish: Fron + Terry: Terry ne boss ke saamne bina kisi sharm ke salary badhane ki maang ki, jo uski effrontery ko dikhata hai.

meaning: the belief in equal rights and opportunities for all individuals
mnemonic: "Eagle" + "Tarzan": imagine an eagle soaring freely while Tarzan swings from vine to vine, symbolizing egalitarian freedom — in an egalitarian society, everyone enjoys the same freedoms.
hinglish: "Eagle" + "Tarzan": socho ek eagle aasman mein udta hai jabki Tarzan jungle mein khush hai, yeh dikhata hai ek egalitarian samaj mein sabko barabar ki azaadi milti hai.

meaning: outstandingly bad; shocking
mnemonic: Egregious -> 'Egregious Grievous': if you commit an egregious act, it's grievous to everyone around you, causing shock and dismay.
hinglish: E + Grievous: agar aap ne koi egregious kaam kiya, to wo sab ke liye khud se zyada bhayanak hota hai.

meaning: to explain in detail or provide additional information
mnemonic: Elaborate -> 'Ella bore a late': imagine a girl named Ella who always gives extensive details about everything; she loves to elaborate.
hinglish: Ella + Bore + A + Late: socho Ella hamesha har cheez ka detail deti hai, woh hamesha elaborate karti hai.

meaning: extremely happy or joyful
mnemonic: "Elation" -> "E-Late": when you arrive late to a party and find it is the best time ever, you feel elated.
hinglish: "Elation" -> "E-Late": jab tum late party pe pahunchte ho aur sab kuch accha hota hai, tab tum elated mehsoos karte ho.

meaning: basic or fundamental; relating to the basic principles of a subject
mnemonic: "Element" + "ary": in an elementary school, children learn the basic elements of various subjects, making education elementary.
hinglish: "Element" + "ary": elementary school mein bachche vibhinn subjects ke basic elements seekhte hain, isliye ye education buniadi hoti hai.

meaning: to draw out a response or reaction
mnemonic: "Elicit" -> "E-Licit": when you 'E' (elect) to 'licit' (ask), you can elicit information from someone easily.
hinglish: "E" (elect) + "Licit" (puchna): jab aap kisi se sawal puchkar jawab 'elic' karte hain.

meaning: a person who believes that a society or system should be led by an elite group
mnemonic: Elite + Ist: an elitist believes only the elite should lead, like a special club that excludes everyone else.
hinglish: Elite + Ist: ek elitist sirf elite logon ko agwaai karne ka hak samajhta hai, jaise sirf khaas logon ka club.

meaning: fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing
mnemonic: Eloquence -> 'Elocution' + 'Fluency': a speaker with elocution and fluency captivates listeners with eloquent speech.
hinglish: Elocution + Fluency: ek speaker ke elocution aur fluency se log prabhavit hote hain, uski baatein eloquent hoti hain.

meaning: to make something clear or easy to understand
mnemonic: "Elu" + "Cide" (to cut): to elucidate is to cut through confusion and clarify a point, making it clear to everyone.
hinglish: "Elu" + "Sid" (saaf karna): jab teacher kisi topic ko saaf saaf samjhata hai, toh woh usse elucidate karta hai.

meaning: difficult to find, catch, or achieve
mnemonic: "Elude" -> "A Looze": when you try to catch a fish and it slips away, it becomes elusive, just like your goal of catching it.
hinglish: "Aloo" (potato) + "Lose": jab aap aloo ko pakadne ki koshish karte hain aur woh haath se chhoot jaata hai, toh woh elusive ho jaata hai.

meaning: to make something more attractive by adding decorative details
mnemonic: "Embellish" -> "Em Bellish" (to make beautiful): Adding a 'bell' to a simple story can embellish it and make it sound more enchanting.
hinglish: "Em Bellish" (sajana): Jab kisi kahani me 'bell' jodte hain, toh woh aur bhi khoobsurat ban jaata hai, jaise hum embellish karte hain.

meaning: having the ability to understand and share the feelings of another
mnemonic: Empathy -> 'Em+Pathy' (Emotional Path): having an emotional path means you can walk alongside someone in their feelings, showing you are empathetic.
hinglish: Em + Pathy: jab aap kisi ke dukh mein saath chal kar unki feelings samajhte hain, tab aap empathetic hote hain.

meaning: based on observation or experience rather than theory or pure logic
mnemonic: "Empiric" -> "Empirical Evidence": empirical evidence refers to information acquired by observation or experimentation; this evidence is the backbone of scientific research.
hinglish: "Empiric" -> "Empirical Saboot": empirical saboot wo hai jo aankh se dekha ya anubhav se mila ho, jaise ek scientist ki research.

meaning: to imitate or copy someone's actions, behavior, or achievements
mnemonic: Emu + Late: an emu that is 'late' to the party tries to emulate the dance moves of others to fit in.
hinglish: Emu + Late: ek emu jo party me 'late' hota hai, dusron ke dance moves ko emulate karne ki koshish karta hai.

meaning: to cast a spell over; to delight greatly
mnemonic: "Enchant" -> "Inchant" (in + chant): Imagine a wizard who begins to chant a spell to enchant the crowd with his magical powers.
hinglish: "Inchant" (in + chant): Jab wizard logon ke liye ek jaadu ka "chant" karta hai, tab voh unhe enchant kar deta hai.

meaning: to intrude gradually on someone's rights or territory
mnemonic: En + Croach: when you 'en' (in) + 'croach' (approach), you are entering someone's space and beginning to encroach on their territory.
hinglish: En + Croach: jab aap 'en' (andar) + 'croach' (nazdeek) aate hain, toh aap kisi ki jagah mein ghus rahe hain aur unke haq par aati hai.

meaning: relating to a comprehensive knowledge of a wide range of subjects
mnemonic: Encyclo- + Pedic: encyclopedia is like a wide 'pedicure' for the mind, treating and beautifying it with a wealth of knowledge, hence someone with encyclopedic knowledge knows a lot.
hinglish: Encyclo- + Pedic: encyclopedia ke jaisa, kisi ke pass encyclopedic knowledge hota hai to voh bohot saare topics par achhe se jaanta hai.

meaning: regularly found among particular people or in a certain area
mnemonic: End + Emic (related to): when something is endemic, it is endearingly related to a specific area, as it exists naturally there.
hinglish: End + Emic: jab koi cheez kisi vishesh kshetra se judi hoti hai, to wo endemic hoti hai, jaise wo wahi ke logon se juda hai.

meaning: to provide with a quality, ability, or asset
mnemonic: End + Dow: if you endow someone, you are giving them a dowry of skills or wealth, enhancing their life.
hinglish: End + Dow: agar aap kisi ko endow karte hain, to aap unhe ek tarah ka dowry dete hain, jo unki zindagi ko behtar banata hai.

meaning: to weaken or reduce the vitality of
mnemonic: Energetic + Vate: when you enervate someone, you drain their energy, making them less energetic.
hinglish: Energy + Vate: jab aap kisi ko enervate karte hain, aap unki energy ko khatam kar dete hain.

meaning: to cause to exist or develop; to produce
mnemonic: Engage + Gender: when we engage with different genders, it can engender new ideas and perspectives in our community.
hinglish: Engage + Gender: jab hum alag-alag gender ke saath engage karte hain, to ye naye vicharon ko engender kar sakta hai.

meaning: mysterious and difficult to understand
mnemonic: Enigma + Tic: an enigmatic riddle is like a puzzle that keeps you ticking in confusion while you solve it.
hinglish: Enigma + Tick: enigma jaisa koi paheli itni rahasyamay hoti hai ki aapka dimaag tick tick karta rehta hai.

meaning: a feeling of hostility or hatred between individuals or groups
mnemonic: "Enemy" + "City": in an enemy city, there is often enmity among the citizens, leading to conflict. The enmity between the two groups escalated into a full-blown feud.
hinglish: "Dushman" + "Tee": dushman tee ke beech kabhi kabhi enmity hoti hai, jo unhe kabhi nahi milne deti. Un dono ke beech enmity bahut gehri thi.

meaning: a feeling of listlessness and dissatisfaction arising from a lack of occupation or excitement
mnemonic: "N" + "Whee": when you feel bored, you might say 'N' (and) 'Whee!' in a sarcastic way, highlighting your ennui during a dull moment.
hinglish: "N" + "Whee": jab aap bore hote hain, aap shayad keh sakte hain 'N' (aur) 'Whee!' mazak mein, jo aapki ennui ko darshata hai.

meaning: to happen as a consequence or result
mnemonic: "Ensue" -> "In-Sue": If you get into a lawsuit (sue), the consequences will ensue, leading to complications.
hinglish: "In" + "Sue": Agar aap kisi ko sue karte hain, toh uske baad kuch complications ensue hoti hain.

meaning: to captivate or hold the attention of someone deeply
mnemonic: Ent + Thrall: when you enthrall someone, you 'entrap' their attention like a magician enthralling his audience.
hinglish: Ent + Thrall: jab aap kisi ko enthrall karte hain, toh aap unka dhyan itna pakad lete hain jaise ek jadugar unki nazar pakad leta hai.

meaning: having a rightful claim to something
mnemonic: "In Title" -> "In Title": if something is in a title, you are entitled to it as your rightful property.
hinglish: "In Title": agar koi cheez title me likhi hai, toh aap uske liye entitled hain.

meaning: to earnestly request or implore someone to do something
mnemonic: Entreat -> 'In Treat': when you are in a treat, you might beg to have more, similar to how you entreat someone for a favor.
hinglish: In + Treat: jab aap kisi se kuch maangte hain jaise kisi treat ke liye, tab aap entreat karte hain.

meaning: firmly established and difficult to change
mnemonic: Enter + Trench: when you enter a trench, you're in a deep, entrenched position that’s hard to escape from.
hinglish: Enter + Trench: jab aap trench me enter karte hain, toh aap ek gehri aur sthayi jagah me jaate hain jo badalna mushkil hota hai.

meaning: lasting for a very short time
mnemonic: Eph + Em + Eral: ephemeral events are like 'eiffel emeral' (short-lived) beauty that doesn't last long, just like the sunset.
hinglish: Eph + Em + Eral: sunset itna khoobsurat tha, lekin woh ephemeral tha, sirf kuch hi minute tak raha.

meaning: a state of mental calmness, stability, and composure, especially in difficult situations
mnemonic: Equal + Animosity: maintaining equanimity means staying calm and even when there is animosity around you.
hinglish: Equal + Nami: jab sab kuch uljhan ho, tab bhi aapko equal rehna hai, yani equanimity ke saath react karna hai.

meaning: fair and impartial
mnemonic: Equity + Table: when you set the table fairly for everyone, it's an equitable arrangement that ensures everyone is treated justly.
hinglish: Equity + Table: jab aap sab ke liye table ko barabar set karte hain, tab yeh ek equitable arrangement hota hai jo sabko sahi tarah se treat karta hai.

meaning: to use ambiguous language to avoid committing oneself
mnemonic: Equi + Vocate: when you 'equivocate,' you are as if saying 'equal voice' — you give equal weight to all sides, avoiding a clear position.
hinglish: Equi + Vocate: jab aap 'equivocate' karte hain, toh aap sab taraf ki baatein ek saman rakhte hain, bina kisi pakki baat ke.

meaning: to completely remove or eliminate something
mnemonic: "Eraser" + "A Dictate": an eraser is used to completely remove mistakes from paper; to eradicate means to completely eliminate something, like erasing a mistake.
hinglish: "Khatam" + "Karna": jab aap kisi cheez ko khatam karte hain, toh aap usse eradicate kar rahe hote hain.

meaning: not even or regular in pattern; unpredictable
mnemonic: "Err" + "At Tick": when you err, you might hit an irregular tick on a clock, making your timing erratic.
hinglish: "Err" + "At Tick": jab aap galti karte hain, toh aapke clock ka tick bhi erratic ho jata hai, bilkul aniyamit.

meaning: former; of an earlier time
mnemonic: "Earth" + "While": imagine a time when the earth was different, during an erstwhile era. The erstwhile champion could not recapture his winning glory.
hinglish: "Aasman" + "Wala": ek waqt tha jab woh erstwhile superstar tha, par ab uska koi naam nahi hai.

meaning: having or showing great knowledge or learning
mnemonic: "Air you tight" (a phrase hinting at being knowledgeable): when you're erudite, your knowledge is so vast that it feels like you have a tight grasp on the air of information around you.
hinglish: "Air you tight": jab aap erudite hote hain, toh aapke paas itna gyaan hota hai ki aap har cheez pe pakad bana kar rakhte hain.

meaning: to increase or intensify
mnemonic: "Escalator" -> "Escalate": as you ride an escalator, you go up, just like tensions can escalate to a higher level.
hinglish: "Escalator" + "Badaana": escalator par chadhte hi aap upar jaate hain, waise hi kabhi-kabhi choti si baat escalate karke badi muskil ban jaati hai.

meaning: to deliberately avoid or abstain from something
mnemonic: "Eschew" -> "Screw": If you 'screw' up and eat junk food, you should eschew it next time by choosing healthy options instead.
hinglish: "Es" + "Chew": jab aap 'chew' nahi karna chahte junk food ka, tab aap usse eschew karte hain.

meaning: intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with specialized knowledge
mnemonic: "Ease" + "O" + "Tears": if you're not careful with esoteric subjects, you might feel like you're learning with ease, but in reality, it's causing you tears from confusion — many find esoteric topics perplexing.
hinglish: "Ease" + "O" + "Tears": agar aap esoteric cheezon ko nahi samjhte toh aap aaram se sochte hain lekin asal mein aapko udaasi hoti hai — bohot log gūḍh vishayon ko samajh nahi paate hain.

meaning: deserving respect or admiration
mnemonic: Estimate + Able: If you estimate someone as able, it's because they are estimable and worthy of respect.
hinglish: Estimate + Able: Agar aap kisi ko capable samajhte ho, toh wo estimable hai aur izzat ke layak hai.

meaning: having lost affection or closeness, often used to describe relationships that have become distant
mnemonic: Estrange -> 'East Range': if you are sent away to the East Range, you become estranged from your home and loved ones.
hinglish: Estrange -> 'Is Strange': jab koi rishta 'strange' ho jaata hai, toh log ek doosre se 'estranged' ho jaate hain.

meaning: a mild or indirect word or expression substituted for one considered to be too harsh or blunt
mnemonic: "You" (a person) + "Fame" (reputation): using a euphemism can help you maintain a good reputation by softening the blow of harsh truths.
hinglish: "You" (aap) + "Fame" (naam): euphemism istamal karke aap khud ko ya dosron ko mushkil sachai se bachane ki koshish karte hain.

meaning: a feeling of intense excitement and happiness
mnemonic: Euphoria -> You 'Fell' into 'Euphoria': when you're euphoric, you feel like you're floating on a cloud of happiness.
hinglish: Euphoria -> 'You' + 'Fell' (aap girte hain): jab aap euphoric hote hain, toh aisa lagta hai jaise aap khushi ke badal par ud rahe hain.

meaning: to avoid or escape from something, especially by cleverness or trickery
mnemonic: "Eve" + "Aid": Eve used her cleverness to aid herself in evading the truth about her late arrival.
hinglish: "Eve" + "Aid": Eve ne apne cleverness se kuchh chhupane ke liye baat ko palat diya aur question se evade kiya.

meaning: quickly fading or disappearing
mnemonic: "Evan" (a name) + "Escent" (ascent): imagine Evan's happiness quickly ascending to the peak, only to vanish into thin air — evanescent feelings fade fast.
hinglish: "Evan" (एक नाम) + "Escent" (उदित होना): सोचो कि एवान की खुशी जल्दी से आसमान पर जा रही है, फिर अचानक गायब हो जाती है — evanescent भावनाएँ जल्दी मिट जाती हैं।

meaning: avoiding giving a direct answer or response
mnemonic: Evasion -> 'Eager to Avoid Vision': when someone is evasive, they are eager to avoid giving a clear vision or answer.
hinglish: Evasion + 'Nazar Churaana': jab koi evasive hota hai, woh seedhe jawab dene se nazar churaata hai.

meaning: to bring a feeling, memory, or image into the mind
mnemonic: Evoke -> 'Evoke' a 'Voke' (voice): when you evoke something, you call forth a feeling or memory like a voice calling you back to the past.
hinglish: Evoke -> 'Evo' (सक्रिय) + 'K' (को): जब आप किसी चीज़ को evoke करते हैं, तो आप एक भावना या याद को सक्रिय करते हैं जैसे कोई आवाज़ आपको वापस बुला रही हो।

meaning: to make a problem or situation worse
mnemonic: "Exacerbate" -> "Examine a Beret": if you examine a beret that was already in bad shape, you might accidentally worsen its condition, thus exacerbate the damage.
hinglish: "Examine" + "Beret": agar aap ek beret ko dekhte hain jo pehle se kharaab hai, to aap uski halat aur bhi bigaad dete hain, jo exacerbate karne jaisa hai.

meaning: demanding a high standard; precise and meticulous
mnemonic: "Exact" -> "Exacting": being exact means you demand precision, just like an exacting teacher who won't accept anything less than perfect.
hinglish: "Exact" + "Kya": jab kisi cheez ka exact hona zaroori ho, tab woh exacting hoti hai, jaise ek exacting teacher jo perfect kaam chahti hai.

meaning: frustrated, annoyed, or irritated
mnemonic: Ex + Asperated: when you are exasperated, you feel like you want to 'ex' (out) 'asperate' (annoy) someone because they are driving you crazy.
hinglish: Ex + Pashtana: jab aap exasperated hote hai, tab aap kisi ko 'ex' (bahar) 'pashtana' (pareshan) karne ka mann karte hain kyunki wo aapko pareshan kar raha hai.

meaning: to criticize severely and publicly
mnemonic: Ex + Coriate: when you 'ex' (out) + 'coriate' (skin), it implies stripping away — critics excoriate by stripping away the pretense in their harsh reviews.
hinglish: Ex + Koriya: jab koi 'ex' (bahar) nikalta hai + 'koriya' (koriya karta hai), toh uska matlab hota hai kisi cheez ko bura kehna — critics film ko excoriate karte hain uski originality ke liye.

meaning: to clear someone from blame or guilt
mnemonic: Ex + Culprit: if you exculpate someone, you are saying that they are not the culprit, thus clearing them from blame.
hinglish: Ex + Culprit: agar aap kisi ko exculpate karte hain, toh aap keh rahe hain ki wo culprit nahi hai, isliye unhe dosh se mukt kar rahe hain.

meaning: a critical interpretation or explanation of a text, especially religious scripture
mnemonic: Examine + Jesus: when conducting an exegesis, you carefully examine religious texts as though you are analyzing teachings related to Jesus.
hinglish: Examine + Jesus: jab aap exegesis karte hain, toh aap dhyan se dharmik likhat ka jaanch karte hain jaise aap Yeshu ki shiksha ko samajh rahe hain.

meaning: thorough and comprehensive; covering all or nearly all elements or aspects
mnemonic: Exhaust + I've: if I've exhausted all possibilities, then my research is exhaustive and covers everything.
hinglish: Exhaust + I've: agar maine sab kuch exhaust kar diya, to mera research exhaustive hai.

meaning: causing great excitement and happiness
mnemonic: "Exhilarate" -> "Exhilaration Rate": the excitement rate of a rollercoaster is so high that it feels exhilarating! — The exhilarating ride made my heart race.
hinglish: "Exhilarate" -> "Exciting Latare": jab kisi cheez ka excitement itna zyada ho ki aap khush ho jao, to wo exhilarating hoti hai! — Wo exhilarating drive ne mujhe khush kar diya.

meaning: to strongly encourage or urge someone to do something
mnemonic: "Ex" (out) + "Hort" (hurt): if you don’t encourage your team, they might get hurt in performance; remember to exhort them to do well.
hinglish: "Ex" (bahar) + "Hort" (short): jab aap kisi ko bahar aane aur accha karne ke liye kehna chahte hain, toh aap unhe exhort karte hain.

meaning: requiring immediate attention or action
mnemonic: Examine + Agent: an exigent agent demands your attention urgently, just like how an exigent situation requires immediate action.
hinglish: Exam + Agent: exam ka agent hamesha exigent hota hai, kyunki usse turant kaam karne ki zaroorat hoti hai.

meaning: to clear from blame or guilt
mnemonic: Exonerate -> 'X' (cross) + 'Honor': when you cross out the false accusations, you restore someone's honor by exonerating them.
hinglish: Ex + Honor: jab aap galat ilzaam ko khatam karte hain, toh kisi ki izzat ko wapas karte hain, yani unhe exonerate karte hain.

meaning: excessively high or unreasonable (as in price)
mnemonic: "Exorbitant" -> "Ex-orbitant": like something that's out of orbit, prices can feel exorbitant when they are way out of reach.
hinglish: "Ex" (exceed) + "Orbitant" (orbit se bahar): jab koi cheez orbit se bahar nikal jaye, uska daam bhi exorbitant ho jata hai.

meaning: to drive out an evil spirit from a person or place
mnemonic: Ex + Or + Size: to make something 'ex' (out) of the 'or' (evil) and 'size' (fit), a priest must exorcise the spirit to make the place fit for the living.
hinglish: Ex + Or + Size: jab kisi jadoo ya bhoot ko 'ex' (bahar) nikaalna ho, to 'or' (aisa bhoot) 'size' (jaga) ke liye exorcise karna padta hai.

meaning: strikingly different or unusual, often in a way that is attractive or interesting
mnemonic: "Ex" (out) + "otic" (like exotic): when you take something out of its usual place, it becomes exotic and fascinating.
hinglish: "Ex" (bahar) + "otic" (jaise): jab aap kuch cheez bahar le aate hain, to vo exotic aur dilchasp ho jaati hai.

meaning: to speak or write at length or in detail
mnemonic: "Expound" + "Ate": when you expatiate, you eat up time by expounding on a topic in detail — the audience may wish you wouldn't expatiate so much.
hinglish: "Explain" + "Tee": jab aap kisi topic ko detail me explain karte hain, toh aap expatiate kar rahe hote hain, lekin kabhi kabhi log chahte hain ki aap itna na karein.

meaning: convenient and practical, although possibly improper or immoral
mnemonic: Expedite + 'ent': to expedite means to speed up, but sometimes the expedient choice isn't the best one.
hinglish: Expedite + 'ent': kisi kaam ko jaldi karne ke liye expedient tareeka lena kabhi kabhi sahi nahi hota.

meaning: to speed up the progress of something
mnemonic: Expedite -> 'Expedite my Date': if you expedite my date with an amazing dinner, I will have more fun, speeding up our evening plans.
hinglish: Expedite -> 'Expedite mera Date': agar tum mera date expedite karoge, toh hum jaldi milenge aur achha waqt bita sakte hain.

meaning: able to be explained or accounted for
mnemonic: "Explain" + "Able": if something is explicable, it is able to be explained clearly and logically.
hinglish: "Explain" + "Able": agar kuch explicable hai, to uska samjhane mein koi dikkat nahi hoti.

meaning: taking unfair advantage of a person or group
mnemonic: Exploit + Hate: when someone exploits, they often create hate and resentment in others; their actions are exploitative and unfair.
hinglish: Exploit + Karo: agar aap kisi ki majboori ka fayda uthaate hain, toh aap exploit kar rahe hain, jo ki shoshankari hai.

meaning: still in existence; not extinct
mnemonic: "Extent" -> "Extent of existence": the extant species are those that have not disappeared from the earth, showing the extent of their existence.
hinglish: "Avasheesh" -> "Ava (remaining) + Sheesh (from the past)": jo prani ab tak hain unhe extant kehte hain, jaise ki kuch avashesh prani ab bhi hain.

meaning: to speak or perform without preparation; improvise
hindi: बिना तैयारी के बोलना या प्रदर्शन करना
mnemonic: "Ex" (out) + "temporize" (time): to extemporize is to speak out without taking time to prepare, like giving a spontaneous speech.
hinglish: "Ex" (bahar) + "temporize" (samay) : extemporize ka matlab hai bina tayyari ke baat karna, jaise kisi debate mein achanak bolna.

meaning: making a crime or offense seem less serious
mnemonic: Extend + You + Naiting: if you extend your understanding of someone's situation, you might find extenuating factors that lessen their guilt.
hinglish: Extend + You + Naiting: agar tum kisi ki muskil halat ko samjho, toh tumhe extenuating wajahen mil sakti hain jo unki galti ko halka karti hain.

meaning: to praise highly
mnemonic: Extol -> 'X' (the letter) + 'Toll': when a great person has passed, we toll the bell and extol their life and achievements.
hinglish: X + Toll: jab kisi mahan vyakti ki yaad aati hai, hum bell bajate hain aur unki sarahna karte hain.

meaning: not essential or relevant; unrelated
mnemonic: "Extra" + "Unnecessary": having extra information that is not needed is considered extraneous, like an extra topping on a pizza that you didn't order.
hinglish: "Extra" + "Nahi chahiye": jab aap kisi report me extra aur zaroori nahi cheezen dekhte hain, woh extraneous hoti hain.

meaning: to infer or estimate by extending or projecting known information
mnemonic: Ex + Trap + Olate: if you 'extrapolate', you're trying to 'trap' additional information 'out' of what you already have, just like adding more layers to a cake.
hinglish: Ex + Trap + Olate: jab aap 'extrapolate' karte hain, toh aap apne paas jo jankari hai usse aur zyada jankari 'trap' karne ki koshish karte hain, jaise ek cake mein aur layers jodna.

meaning: excessively elaborate or luxurious
mnemonic: "Extra" + "Vagant" (vacant): When you have extra money, you might go on a vacation and spend extravagantly on luxury items.
hinglish: "Extra" + "Vagant" (vacant): Jab aapke paas extra paise hote hain, aap kuch bhi kharid sakte hain, jo extravagant hota hai.

meaning: invented, usually with deceitful intent
mnemonic: Fabric -> Fabricate: you weave a tale like fabric from raw threads — a fabricated story.
hinglish: Fabric + Kate: jaise aap kapde se kuch banate hain, waise hi koi jhooti kahani fabricate kar leta hai.

meaning: treating serious issues with deliberately inappropriate humor
hindi: गंभीर मसलों को जानबूझकर अनुचित हंसी में लेना
mnemonic: Face + It + Us: if you face it with humor, you might be facetious about the situation.
hinglish: Face + It + Us: agar aap mazak se samasya ka samna karte hain, to aap facetious hain.

meaning: a place, amenity, or equipment provided for a particular purpose
mnemonic: "Face" + "ility" (facility sounds like): when you want to make your face look good, you go to a beauty facility for treatments that enhance your appearance.
hinglish: "Face" + "ility": jab aapke chehre ko sundar dikhane ki baat aati hai, toh aap beauty facility jaate hain jahan aapki sundarta badh jaati hai.

meaning: causing disagreement or conflict; divisive
mnemonic: "Fact" + "Shus": when facts are disputed, they become factious, leading to arguments rather than agreements.
hinglish: "Fact" + "Shus": jab koi baat facts par nahi, balki jhagde par ho, toh woh factious ban jaate hain.

meaning: based on a mistaken belief; misleading
mnemonic: "Fall" + "Lies": when you fall for lies, you are being deceived by fallacious statements.
hinglish: "Fall" + "Lies": jab aap jhoot par girte hain, tab aap fallacious baatein maante hain.

meaning: capable of making mistakes or being wrong
mnemonic: Fall + Able: if you fall, you're able to make mistakes — just like being fallible.
hinglish: Fall + Able: agar aap girte hain, toh aap galti karne ke liye saksham hote hain — is tarah aap fallible hain.

meaning: land left unplanted to restore its fertility
mnemonic: Fall + Low: when you let the soil 'fall low' by not planting crops, it becomes fallow and regains nutrients.
hinglish: Fall + Low: jab aap zameen ko 'fall low' kar dete hain bina koi beej boya, toh wo khali ho jaati hai, yaani fallow.

meaning: to hesitate or waver in action or purpose
mnemonic: Falter -> Faulty Alter: when you make a faulty alteration in your plan, you might falter and lose your confidence.
hinglish: Faulty + Alter: jab aap apne plan me koi faulty alteration karte hain, to aap ladkhadane lagte hain.

meaning: characterized by or possessing fanciful ideas; imaginative and unrealistic
mnemonic: Fancy -> 'Fancy Full': when you are fanciful, your thoughts are 'fancy full' of imaginative ideas that may not be grounded in reality.
hinglish: Fancy + Full: jab aap fanciful hote hain, aapke vichar 'fancy full' hote hain, jo asli nahi hote.

meaning: very attentive to detail; hard to please
mnemonic: "Fast" + "Tidious" (tedious): when you are so fastidious, even the smallest detail can feel tedious and make you hard to please.
hinglish: "Fast" + "Tedious" (nakhra): jab aap fastidious hain, toh choti choti baatein bhi nakhre ko badal deti hain, aur aap khush nahi hote.

meaning: to understand or grasp the meaning of something
mnemonic: Fathom -> 'Fath' (like 'father') + 'Um': your father always says, 'You must fathom the depths of your issues', meaning you need to fully understand them.
hinglish: Fath + Um: aapko hamesha samajhna chahiye ki aapki samasyaon ki gehrayi ko fathom karna zaroori hai.

meaning: to exhibit affection or attempt to please through flattery
mnemonic: "Fawn" -> "Fawn-tastic": to be fawn-tastic means to show excessive affection, just like a fawn (young deer) that is adorable and seeks your attention.
hinglish: "Fawn" -> "Fawn-tastic": jab aap kisi se fawn-tastic tareeke se pyaar aur chahat dikhate hain, jaise ek chhoti hiran (fawn) aakarshak hoti hai.

meaning: capable of being done or achieved
mnemonic: Feast + Able: if a feast is able to be prepared in time, it is feasible to host the party on short notice.
hinglish: Feast + Able: agar feast ko tayyar karna mumkin hai, to voh party ke liye feasible hai.

meaning: lacking initiative or strength of character; ineffective
mnemonic: Feck + Less: when you have less 'feck' (energy or initiative), you become feckless and ineffective.
hinglish: Feck + Less: jab aap ke paas 'feck' (josh) kam hota hai, tab aap feckless ho jaate hain aur kuch nahi kar paate.

meaning: fruitful and capable of producing offspring or vegetation
mnemonic: Fecund -> 'Fecundity': the quality of being fruitful; a couple's fecundity can lead to a large family.
hinglish: Fecund -> 'Fecundity': jab koi zameen bahut upjaau hoti hai, uski fecundity kafi zyada hoti hai.

meaning: lacking physical strength, especially as a result of age or illness
mnemonic: Feeble -> Feeble Bee: a bee that is too weak to fly away is a feeble bee, just like someone lacking strength.
hinglish: Feeble -> Feeble Beehad: jab koi aadmi itna kamzor ho jaaye ki wo beehad udan nahi kar sake, wo feeble hai.

meaning: to pretend or make a false show of something
mnemonic: Feign -> 'Fame' + 'Gain': to feign is to pretend to gain fame by pretending to be someone you're not, like feigning a talent.
hinglish: Fein -> 'Fake' + 'Gain': agar aap kisi talent ko feign karte hain, toh aap fake gain kar rahe hain, jaise ki kisi aur ki tarah banne ki koshish.

meaning: a deceptive movement or action, especially in sports or combat
mnemonic: "Faint" -> "Feint": when you faint, you might pretend to be weak, just like a feint is a deceptive move to mislead someone.
hinglish: "Faint" + "Karna": jab aap faint karte hain, aap jhooth bolkar kamzor dikhte hain, jaise feint ek dhokha dene wali harkat hoti hai.

meaning: well-chosen or suited to the circumstances
mnemonic: Fell + Is + It + Us: If you fell and it is us helping you, your recovery will be felicitous, as we are well-suited to assist.
hinglish: Fell + Is + It + Us: Agar tum gir gaye ho aur hum hain tumhe sambhalne wale, to tumhara recovery ka process felicitous hoga, kyunki hum sahi log hain madad karne ke liye.

meaning: showing intense and passionate feeling
mnemonic: Fur + Vent: when a dog with thick fur gets hot, it fervently seeks a vent to cool down — just like fervent emotions that seek expression.
hinglish: Fur + Vent: jab ek kutta garmi se pareshan hota hai, wo fervent tareeke se hawa lene ke liye vent dhundta hai.

meaning: intensely passionate or enthusiastic
mnemonic: "Fur" + "Vid" (video): when you watch a fervid video about your favorite topic, you feel intense enthusiasm and passion for it.
hinglish: "Fur" + "Vid" (video): jab aap kisi fervid video ko dekhte hain, toh aapko usme utni hi jazbaat aur junoon mehsoos hota hai.

meaning: intense and passionate feeling
mnemonic: "Fur" + "Vore": imagine a fervent fan wearing a fur coat, passionately cheering for their team. The fervor of their excitement is contagious.
hinglish: "Fur" + "Vore": ek fervent fan fur coat pehne hue apni team ke liye passionately cheer kar raha hai, unka fervor sab par chadh raha hai.

meaning: to become infected or inflamed, often worsening over time
mnemonic: Fester -> Fester Bunny: like a bunny that doesn’t care for its wounds, it lets them fester into something much worse.
hinglish: Fester + Faster: agar aapki ghav ko jaldi nahi theek karte, woh fester karke aur bura ho jayega.

meaning: likely to change, especially in regard to one's loyalties or affections
mnemonic: "Flick" + "El": When you flick away a petal, it can change direction and be fickle like a flower blown by the wind.
hinglish: "Flick" + "El": Jab aap ek patta flick karte hain, woh hawa se udkar disha badal sakta hai, jaise log fickle hote hain.

meaning: not literal; using figures of speech
mnemonic: Figure -> 'Figurative': when you use figures of speech, like metaphors, your language becomes figurative, painting pictures in the mind.
hinglish: Figure + 'ative': jab tum kahte ho 'uska dil toota hai', ye figurative hai, asli nahi, par dil ki bhavna dikhata hai.

meaning: excessively particular or demanding; hard to please
mnemonic: "Fin" + "Nicky" (picky): If you are finicky like Nick, you’re very particular about everything, making friends roll their eyes.
hinglish: "Fin" + "Nikki" (nakhra): Agar Nikki finicky hai, toh woh har cheez mein nakhra karti hai, aur doston ko pareshani hoti hai.

meaning: occurring in irregular bursts or intervals
mnemonic: Fit + Full: if your sleep is not full and consistent, it’s fitful and disrupted. — His fitful sleep left him yawning all day.
hinglish: Fit + Full: jab aapka sota hua waqt full nahi hota, toh wo fitful hota hai. — Uska fitful sleep usay din bhar thaka deta hai.

meaning: extremely noticeable; conspicuously bad or offensive
mnemonic: Flag + Grant: if you see a flagrant violation, it’s as if you are granting permission for outrageous behavior.
hinglish: Flag + Grant: agar aap kisi flagrant galti ko ignore karte hain, toh jaise aap uski permission de rahe hain.

meaning: characterized by extravagance or showiness
mnemonic: Flame + Boy + Ant: a flamboyant boy dressed in bright colors looks like a walking flame, catching everyone's eye.
hinglish: Flame + Boy + Ant: ek chamakdaar ladka jaise aag ki tarah dikhta hai, sabka dhyan kheench leta hai.

meaning: a young bird that has just acquired its feathers
mnemonic: "Fledg" (like 'ledge') + "ling" (small): when a young bird is on the ledge of its nest, it is a fledgling preparing to fly.
hinglish: "Fledg" (ledge) + "ling" (chhota): jab ek chhota parinda apne ghosle ke ledge par hota hai, wahi fledgling hai jo udne ki tayyari kar raha hai.

meaning: elaborately or excessively intricate or ornate
mnemonic: Florid -> 'Floor it' + 'Id': imagine a car speeding (flooring it) with colorful decorations all over it, just like florid language that is often overly ornate.
hinglish: Flora + Id: socho ek garden (floral scene) jahan sab kuch bahut sundar hai, par thoda zyada hai, jaise ki florid likhai.

meaning: to openly disregard a rule or law
mnemonic: "Flout" -> "Shout": when you shout at rules, you flout them by ignoring their authority.
hinglish: "Flout" -> "Loud": jab aap zordaar bolte hain rules ki taraf, tab aap unhe flout kar rahe hain.

meaning: confused or perplexed
mnemonic: Flum + Mix: if you mix up flour and lemons, you’ll be flummoxed about what to bake.
hinglish: Flum + Mix: agar aap aata aur nimbu ko mix kar denge, toh aap flummoxed ho jaayenge ki kya banana hai.

meaning: agitated or confused
mnemonic: Fluster -> 'Flustered Fuster': when you're flustered, it's like being a 'fuster' (someone who fusses) because you're confused and agitated.
hinglish: Fluster -> 'Flustered Fuster': jab aap flustered hote hain, to aap itne ghabraate hain ki aapko har cheez fuster (fuss) karne lagti hai.

meaning: to prevent someone from achieving something; to thwart
mnemonic: "Foil" -> "Fail": when you foil someone's plan, you make it fail — just like when the alarm goes off, the thief's plans are foiled.
hinglish: "Foil" -> "Fail": jab aap kisi ki yojna ko foil karte hain, toh aap usay fail kar dete hain — jaise kisi chori ko rok dena.

meaning: to instigate or stir up (an undesirable or violent sentiment or course of action)
mnemonic: "Foam" + "Ment": when you throw foam (the light and airy material) into a fire, it can foment (stir up) a bigger flame — just like inciting unrest.
hinglish: "Foam" + "Ment": jab tum foam ko aag me daal dete ho, toh vo aag ko aur badhata hai, jaise kisi ko uksana.

meaning: recklessly bold or daring
mnemonic: "Fool" + "Hardy": a fool acts foolishly and boldly, like a foolhardy person who takes unnecessary risks.
hinglish: "Fool" (बेवकूफ) + "Hardy" (हिम्मत वाला): ek bevakoof aadmi hamesha hardi yaani beparwah hota hai, jaise foolhardy insaan.

meaning: to hold back, refrain from, or tolerate
mnemonic: Forbear -> 'Forbearance': by exhibiting forbearance, one shows the ability to hold back frustration.
hinglish: For + Bear: ek bhaloo ko dekhkar log forbear karte hain, kyunki woh unhein dar dete hain.

meaning: to predict or indicate in advance, often with a sense of forewarning
mnemonic: "Fore" (before) + "Bode" (to announce): when you forebode something, it’s like announcing a warning before it happens — the sky forebodes rain with its dark clouds.
hinglish: "Fore" (pehle) + "Bode" (batana): jab aap kisi cheez ka pehle se hi halal dete ho, toh aap forebode kar rahe hote hain, jaise aandhi aane par aasmaan ka rang badalta hai.

meaning: capable of being anticipated or predicted
mnemonic: Foresee -> 'For See': if you can see something coming, it is foreseeable; the consequences were foreseeable to everyone involved.
hinglish: For + See: agar aap kisi cheez ko dekh sakte hain, toh wo cheez foreseeable hai; election ka result sabke liye foreseeable tha.

meaning: to prevent something from happening by taking action in advance
mnemonic: For + Stall: if you 'forestall' a discussion, you prevent it from happening like a stall in a race — you get ahead before it starts.
hinglish: For + Rook: agar aap kisi baat ko 'forestall' karte hain, toh aap us baat ko hone se roakte hain, jaise kisi race mein aap aage nikal jaate hain pehle se.

meaning: to decide not to do or have something
mnemonic: "For" + "Go": If you are going to forgo dessert, you are saying 'for' later, I will 'go' without it. So, she decided to forgo dessert to stay healthy.
hinglish: "For" + "Go": Agar aap dessert ko forgo karte hain, toh aap keh rahe hain 'for' baad mein, main 'go' karunga bina iske. Isliye, usne apne health ke liye dessert forgo kar diya.

meaning: to abandon or give up something or someone
mnemonic: For + Snake: if you see a snake, you might forsake the area and run away!
hinglish: For + Saap: agar aapko saap dikhai de, to aap us jagah ko forsake (tyag) kar denge!

meaning: courage in pain or adversity
mnemonic: Fort + Attitude: having a strong attitude in difficult times reflects fortitude.
hinglish: Fort + Attitude: mushkil waqt me strong attitude rakhne se aapka dhairya dikhai deta hai.

meaning: happening by chance or accident, often in a lucky way
mnemonic: "Fortune" + "ous": when something is fortuitous, it seems like fortune has smiled upon you; the chance event was lucky.
hinglish: "Fortune" + "ous": jab kuch fortuitous hota hai, toh aisa lagta hai jaise kismat ne aap par khushiyan barsi hain.

meaning: irritable and quarrelsome
mnemonic: Fractious -> 'Fracture Us': If you argue too much, it could fracture our friendship, making you fractious in nature.
hinglish: Fractious -> 'Fracture Us': Agar aap zyada jhagde toh hamari dosti fracture ho jayegi, aur aap fractious ban jaoge.

meaning: the condition of being weak or delicate
mnemonic: "Frail" + "Tea": if you spill tea on a frail person, they might fall over, highlighting their frailty.
hinglish: "Frail" (कमज़ोर) + "Tea": agar kisi kamzor insaan par chai gir jaye, to vo gir sakta hai, jo unki कमज़ोरी ko dikhata hai.

meaning: open, honest, and direct in speech or writing
mnemonic: Frank -> Frankly Speaking: if you speak frankly, you are being honest and direct about your feelings.
hinglish: Frank + Kaho: jab aap frank kehte ho, aap khul kar apni baatein kar rahe hote ho.

meaning: filled with or likely to result in (something undesirable)
mnemonic: Fraud -> 'Fraudulent' Situation: negotiations can be fraught with deceit, just like a fraudulent deal that is filled with hidden dangers.
hinglish: Fraud + 'Agar' (अगर): kuch negotations fraud se bhari hoti hain, agar logon ke beech nafrat ho.

meaning: marked by fast and energetic activity
mnemonic: Frenzy + Net: when people are caught in a net of chaos, their actions become frenetic as they struggle to escape.
hinglish: Frenzy + Net: jab log ek jaal me phas jaate hain, tab unka vyavhaar utejak ho jata hai, jo frenetic kehlata hai.

meaning: to worry or be anxious about something
mnemonic: Fret -> 'Fretful Pet': when your pet is fretful, it means it's anxious and worried about something.
hinglish: Fret + 'Fretful Pet': jab tumhara pet pareshan hota hai, to wo chinta karta hai, jaise kisi cheez ki wajah se fret kar raha ho.

meaning: a decorative border or edge
mnemonic: "Fringe" -> "Fringe Benefits": just like additional perks, a fringe adds extra flair to the edge of a garment.
hinglish: "Fringe" -> "Fringe Faaida": jaise extra benefits kisi cheez ko aur behtar banate hain, waise hi fringe dress ke kinare ko sundar banata hai.

meaning: not having any serious purpose or value
mnemonic: "Frivol" + "ous": when someone is frivolous, they seem like they're just 'fooling around' and not taking things seriously.
hinglish: "Frivol" + "ous": jab koi aadmi frivolous hota hai, toh woh serious baatein nahi karta, bas mazak kar raha hota hai.

meaning: producing good results; productive
mnemonic: "Fruit" + "Full": a garden that is full of ripe fruit is fruitful; it yields a bountiful harvest.
hinglish: "Fruit" + "Full": ek bagiche jo pakke phalon se bhara hai, wo fruitful hai; ye bohot saari fasal deta hai.

meaning: a point of support or leverage in a system
mnemonic: "Full Crumb" -> "Full Crumb" (a piece of bread or food): the fulcrum is like the center point of a seesaw, where the full weight of both sides is balanced on a single crumb of support.
hinglish: "Ful" + "Crumb" (पूरी रोटी का टुकड़ा): seesaw ka fulcrum wo center hai jahan dono taraf ka wajan ek hi crumb par balanced hota hai.

meaning: capable of being exchanged or substituted with something of equal value
mnemonic: Fun + Gible: if something is fun, it is easier to exchange (gibe means to exchange banter) — just like how fungible items can be exchanged for one another.
hinglish: Fun + Gible: agar koi cheez mazedaar hai, toh usse asaani se badla ja sakta hai — jaise fungible items ek dusre ke liye badle ja sakte hain.

meaning: secretive or stealthy, often due to guilt or a desire to avoid notice
mnemonic: "Fur" (like animal fur) + "Tive" (like 'active'): if someone is being furtive, they might be as stealthy as a cat with fur, actively sneaking around to avoid detection.
hinglish: "Fur" (kya aaj kal kaise) + "Tive" (jaise active): agar koi furtive hai, toh wo chori chhupke jaise bilkul ek cat ki tarah gupchup hai, chhupte hue nazar aata hai.

meaning: incapable of producing any useful result; pointless
mnemonic: Fool + Tile: If you're a fool trying to lay tiles without knowing how, your effort is futile.
hinglish: Fool + Tile: Agar aap bekaar ke kaam me lage hain, toh aapka effort bekar hai, woh futile hai.

meaning: a socially awkward or tactless act or remark
mnemonic: "Gaff" + "E": if you make a gaffe, you might 'gaff' (catch) an embarrassing moment, like tripping on stage.
hinglish: "Gaff" + "A": agar aap gaffe karte hain, to aapko 'gaff' (catch) karna padta hai apne embarrassing moments ko.

meaning: to deny or contradict
mnemonic: "Gain" + "Say": if you gain something, you might say it with confidence; however, to gainsay is to say the opposite and deny its truth.
hinglish: "Gain" + "Say": agar aapne kuch hasil kiya hai, to aap usse confidently kahenge; lekin 'gainsay' ka matlab hai uss sachai ko inkaar karna.

meaning: to stimulate or excite someone to take action
mnemonic: Galvanize -> 'Gals Van Eyes': imagine a group of girls (gals) in a van, excitedly looking out at a stunning view. That excitement can galvanize them to take a spontaneous adventure.
hinglish: Gals + Van + Eyes: socho ladkiyan ek van mein baithe hain aur bahar ki khoobsurat jagah dekhkar uttejit ho jaati hain, is tarah se unhein galvanize kiya jaata hai.

meaning: excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters
mnemonic: Garry + Rulous: Garry is so chatty that he talks a lot about trivial matters, making him garrulous.
hinglish: Garry + Rulous: Garry itna baatuni hai ki woh har choti baat par garrulous ho jaata hai.

meaning: lacking social grace or sensitivity
mnemonic: "Gouch" (gouching/ouching): when you make a social mistake, it feels like you've gouch'd your way into an awkward situation, making you seem gauche.
hinglish: "Gouch" (gouching/ouching): jab aap social galti karte hain, toh aisa lagta hai jaise aap gouch karke awkward situation mein aa gaye hain, aap ko gauche banata hai.

meaning: awkward in movement or behavior
mnemonic: Gawk -> Gawky: when you gawk at something, you often do it in a clumsy or awkward way, making you look gawky.
hinglish: Gaw + Ki: jab aap gawk karte hain to aap kaafi awkward lagte hain, jaise ki aap gawky ho gaye hain.

meaning: relevant and appropriate to the subject at hand
mnemonic: Germ + Main: if something is relevant, it is the 'germ' (core) of the 'main' topic being discussed, making it germane.
hinglish: Germ + Main: agar kuch baat mukhya vishay se sambandhit hai, toh wo 'germ' (core) hai 'main' topic ka, jo isay germane banata hai.

meaning: smoothly persuasive or insincere
mnemonic: "Glib" -> "Glibberish": when someone talks glibberish, they sound smooth but often lack substance, just like glib expressions.
hinglish: "Glib" -> "Gali Baat": jab koi insaan gali baatein kar raha hota hai, toh wo glib hai, bas baaton se charm karta hai bina sachai ke.

meaning: to take excessive pleasure in one's own success or another's misfortune
mnemonic: Gloat -> 'Globe + Float': imagine a globe floating in the air, as someone proudly gloats about their success, feeling on top of the world.
hinglish: Gloat -> 'Globe + Float': jaise koi globe hawa mein float kar raha ho, aur koi apni jeet par gloat kar raha ho, sab par bhaari mehsoos karte hue.

meaning: sullen or silently unhappy
mnemonic: Gloom -> Glum: when you're in a gloomy mood, you tend to look glum and unhappy.
hinglish: Gloom + Udaas: jab aap ka mood udas hota hai, tab aapka chehra glum lagta hai.

meaning: to provoke or annoy someone so as to stimulate some action or reaction
mnemonic: "Go" + "Ad": if you goad someone, you push them forward (or urge them) to take action, like saying 'go ahead!'
hinglish: "Go" + "Aad": agar aap kisi ko goad karte hain, to aap unhe koi action lene ke liye keh rahe hote hain, jaise 'aage badho!'

meaning: to please or satisfy someone
mnemonic: "Grat" (great) + "ify" (to make): to make someone feel great is to gratify them. For instance, a compliment can gratify a person's efforts.
hinglish: "Grat" (great) + "ify" (karna): jab koi kisi ki mehnat ko tareef karke usse great feel karata hai, tab wo usse gratify karta hai.

meaning: unnecessary or unwarranted; lacking a good reason
mnemonic: "Gratuitous" -> "Gratuity For Us": when something is gratuitous, it's as if a gratuity is given to us without any real reason, making it unnecessary.
hinglish: "Gratuity" + "For Us": jab kuch gratuitous hota hai, tab wo bina kisi zaroorat ke diya jata hai, jaise gratuity jo bina kisi wajah ke milti hai.

meaning: fond of company; sociable
mnemonic: "Greg" + "Gregarious": Greg is so gregarious that he always gathers a flock of friends around him at every gathering.
hinglish: "Greg" + "Gregarious": Greg itna gregarious hai ki har party mein doston ka ek jhund ikattha kar leta hai.

meaning: a complaint or resentment about something perceived as unfair
mnemonic: Grieve + Ants: When you grieve, you might complain like an ant who feels unfairly treated by someone stepping on its home.
hinglish: Shikayat + Ants: Jab aap shikayat karte ho, toh aapki tarah ants bhi us insaan se shikayat karte hain jo unka ghar tod deta hai.

meaning: to act in a subservient manner, often to seek forgiveness
mnemonic: Groan + Level: when you grovel, you groan and lower yourself to a level of humility to seek forgiveness.
hinglish: Grih + Level: jab aap kisi se maafi maangte hain, aap grih se neeche level tak jaate hain, yaani giddh giddh karte hain.

meaning: to complain or express dissatisfaction in a low voice
mnemonic: "Grumble" -> "Grumpy Bubble": when someone is in a grumpy bubble, they often grumble about everything around them. — Her constant grumble about the weather was exhausting to hear.
hinglish: "Grum" + "Bubble": jab koi grumpy bubble mein hota hai, toh woh har baat par grumble karta hai. — Uska baar-baar grumble karna mujhe pareshan kar raha tha.

meaning: easily deceived or tricked
mnemonic: "Gull" + "Ible" (gull + able): If you are able to be fooled like a gull (a bird often tricked), you are gullible.
hinglish: "Gull" + "Ible": agar aap gull (bhoola) ban kar har kisi ki baat maan lete hain, to aap gullible hain.

meaning: lacking significance through having been overused; unoriginal
mnemonic: "Hack" + "Kneed": if you hack at something over and over, your knees will get sore from repetition; hence, it's hackneyed and unoriginal. The presenter’s hackneyed jokes fell flat with the audience.
hinglish: "Hakka" + "Knee": agar aap baar-baar same joke karte hain, toh aapke ghutne thak jayenge; isi tarah se, wo joke hackneyed ho gaya hai. Uska hackneyed mazak sunke sab bore ho gaye.

meaning: to obstruct or impede the progress of something
mnemonic: Ham + Per: when you have too much ham, it can 'per' (impede) your ability to eat, therefore hampering your appetite.
hinglish: Ham + Par: jab aap ke paas zyada ham hota hai, toh yeh aapki appetite ko hamper (rokta) kar sakta hai.

meaning: lacking any obvious principle of organization; random
mnemonic: "Hap" (luck) + "Hazard" (risk): if you leave things to luck, your efforts will be haphazard, like taking random risks.
hinglish: "Hap" (luck) + "Hazard" (khatare): agar aap sab kuch bhagwan par chhod dete hain, toh aapka kaam hamesha haphazard hota hai, jaise khatare uthana.

meaning: unfortunate or unlucky
mnemonic: Hap + Less: if you are hapless, you have less happiness because of your bad luck.
hinglish: Hap + Less: jab aap hapless hote hain, tab aapki khushi kam ho jaati hai kyunki aap bechare hote hain.

meaning: a lengthy and aggressive speech or lecture
mnemonic: Hare + Gang: imagine a hare giving a long, passionate speech to a gang of rabbits — that's a harangue!
hinglish: Hare + Gang: socho ek khargosh apne doston ko lambi baat kar raha hai, yeh ek harangue hai.

meaning: a person or thing that announces or signals the approach of another
mnemonic: Harbinger ->
hinglish: Har + Binger: harbinger ka matlab hai koi cheez jo doosri cheez ke aane ka sanket deta hai.

meaning: extremely distressing or painful
mnemonic: "Harrow" + "ing": when you plow (harrow) the fields, it can be a harrowing experience if something goes wrong while farming.
hinglish: "Harrow" + "ing": jab aap kheti karte hain aur kuch galat hota hai, toh wo ek harrowing anubhav hota hai.

meaning: having an arrogant or disdainful attitude
mnemonic: Haughty -> 'Hot Tea': a person who thinks they're better than everyone else might say, 'I only drink hot tea,' showing their haughty attitude.
hinglish: Haughty -> 'Hoti': jo log khud ko dusron se behtar samajhte hain, kehte hain 'Main toh hamesha haughty hoti hoon.'

meaning: determined to have one's own way; stubborn
mnemonic: Head + Strong: being headstrong means your head is so strong that you refuse to listen to others, like a bull charging ahead regardless of the consequences.
hinglish: Head + Strong: jab aap itne jiddi hote hain ki aap dusron ki baatein nahi sunte, tab aap headstrong hain.

meaning: characterized by strong emotions or excitement
mnemonic: Head + Y: if you drink too much, you can get a heady feeling that makes you giddy with excitement.
hinglish: Head + Y: agar aap zyada pi lete hain, toh aapko heady feelings hoti hain jo aapko dukh se door le jaati hain.

meaning: to pay attention to or take notice of
mnemonic: Heed -> 'He'd' + 'Read': if he'd read the instructions carefully, he would have heeded the advice and avoided mistakes.
hinglish: Heed -> 'He' + 'Deed': agar usne apne deeds ka dhyan diya hota, toh usne bina kisi dikkat ke kaam kiya hota.

meaning: not conforming to accepted beliefs or standards
