mnemonic: Hetero + Dox: heterodox beliefs are like 'hetero' (different) opinions that stand apart from the common 'dox' (beliefs).
hinglish: Hetero + Dox: heterodox vichar woh hote hain jo aam vicharon se alag hote hain.

meaning: composed of different or diverse elements
mnemonic: Hetero + Genius: a genius can't be limited to one type, he/she is a heterogeneous thinker who embraces diverse ideas.
hinglish: Hetero + Janus: ek Janus (दो चेहरे वाला) insaan bohot saare alag-alag logon se milta hai, isliye woh heterogeneous hai.

meaning: narrow-minded or stubbornly conservative
mnemonic: Hide + Bound: if you're hidebound, your ideas are bound to be hidden away in a cave, making you narrow-minded in your beliefs.
hinglish: Hide + Bound: agar aap hidebound hain, toh aapke vichar bandhan me hain aur naye vicharon ko accept nahi karte.

meaning: to create difficulties for someone or something, resulting in a delay or obstruction
mnemonic: Hind + er: when you are hindered, you feel like there's a 'hind' (back) force stopping you from moving forward.
hinglish: Hind + er: jab aap hinder hote hain, toh aapko aage badhne se 'hind' (peeche) force rok raha hota hai.

meaning: excessively theatrical or dramatic in character or style
mnemonic: "Hist" (history) + "Rionic" (irony): in history, some events are so exaggerated they seem almost histrionic, like actors on a stage.
hinglish: "History" (इतिहास) + "Rionic" (नाटक): कभी-कभी इतिहास में घटनाएँ इतनी नाटकीय होती हैं कि वे हिस्त्रियोनिक लगती हैं.

meaning: a confused mixture; a jumble
mnemonic: Hodge + Podge: a hodgepodge is like mixing hodge (a random collection) with podge (a mixture) to create a confusing blend.
hinglish: Hodge + Podge: hodge ka matlab hai gathha hona, isliye hodgepodge mein sab kuch gathha hota hai.

meaning: of the same kind or nature; uniform in composition
mnemonic: "Homo" (same) + "Genius" (kind): a genius chef creates a homogeneous dish where every ingredient is perfectly combined for the same flavor.
hinglish: "Homo" (same) + "Jain" (kind): ek Jain khana banaata hai jo homogeneous hai, sabziyaan ek jaise swad mein mil jaati hain.

meaning: lacking variety; dull and monotonous
mnemonic: "Hum Drum" -> "Hum (us) + Drum (instrument)": life can feel like a dull drumbeat, repetitive and humdrum, without any excitement.
hinglish: "Hum + Drum": humare din ka routine itna dull hota hai, jaise ek boring drum ki dhun, bas humdrum hi reh jaata hai.

meaning: exaggerated statements or claims not meant to be taken literally
mnemonic: "Hyper" (excessive) + "Bole" (to speak): when someone speaks with excessive exaggeration, they are using hyperbole.
hinglish: "Hyper" (zyada) + "Bole" (bolna): jab koi zyada bolta hai ya cheezon ko overstated karta hai, tab wo atishayoikti ka istemal kar raha hota hai.

meaning: a person who pretends to have virtues or beliefs that they do not actually possess
mnemonic: "Hippo" + "Crit": imagine a hippo wearing a critic's hat and pretending to be a sophisticated critic while actually being just a big animal — a hypocrite.
hinglish: "Hippo" + "Critic": ek hippo jo critic ki tarah behave kar raha hai lekin asal mein woh sirf ek bada jaanwar hai — woh ek hypocrite hai.

meaning: excessively emotional or uncontrollable, often in a loud or irrational manner
mnemonic: History + 'cal': history often shows us how people can become hysterical during crises, just like those in a historical meltdown.
hinglish: History + 'kal': history ke pichle dinon mein log itne hysterical ho gaye the ki unke control se baahar ho gaye.

meaning: attacking or rejecting cherished beliefs or institutions
mnemonic: Icon + Clastic: icons represent traditional beliefs, and clastic means broken; thus, iconoclastic refers to breaking away from traditional beliefs.
hinglish: Aaykon + Klassic: aaykon ka matlab hai purani dharanayein, aur klassic ka matlab hai todna; isliye iconoclastic ka matlab hai purani dharanayon ko todna.

meaning: a person who advocates for a particular ideology, especially in a rigid or dogmatic way
mnemonic: Idea + Log: an ideologue is someone who logs or records their ideas and passionately defends them as if they were absolute truth.
hinglish: Idea + Log: ek ideologue woh hai jo apne vicharon ko itna pakka samajhta hai ki wo unhe sabse sahi manta hai.

meaning: a characteristic, habit, or mannerism that is peculiar to an individual
mnemonic: 'Idio' (idiot) + 'Syncratic' (synchronized): an idiot may have idiosyncratic habits that are not in sync with conventional norms, highlighting their uniqueness.
hinglish: 'Idio' (बेवकूफ) + 'Syncratic' (सामंजस्यपूर्ण): एक बेवकूफ ke पास idiosyncratic आदतें hoti hain jo aam logon se alag hoti hain.

meaning: deceptively or illusively attractive; not real
mnemonic: "Illusion" -> "Ill-use-on-a-vision": an illusory sight tricks the mind, making you see something that isn’t really there.
hinglish: "Illusion" -> "I-loser-shun": kabhi kabhi hum sochte hain ki kisi cheez ka haqeeqat hona hai, par woh sirf ek illusion hai, ek ‘I-loser-shun’.

meaning: a complicated and confusing situation
mnemonic: "I'm Broglio" -> (I'm) in a mess: when someone says 'I'm Broglio,' they mean they're caught in an imbroglio of confusion and chaos.
hinglish: "I'm Broglio" -> (I'm) pareshani mein: jab koi kehta hai 'I'm Broglio,' iska matlab hai ki voh ek jatil sthiti mein hai.

meaning: perfectly clean, free from flaws or mistakes
hindi: बिल्कुल साफ, दोष या गलती से मुक्त
mnemonic: "I'm + Maculate" (I'm so perfect): when you say 'I'm immaculate,' it means you're presenting yourself as perfectly clean and flawless.
hinglish: "I'm + Maculate" (main bilkul saaf hoon): jab aap kehte hain 'I'm immaculate,' iska matlab hai aap bilkul clean aur flawless hain.

meaning: about to happen; imminent
mnemonic: "Imminent" -> "I'm in it": if you're in a situation that's about to happen, the outcome is imminent.
hinglish: "I'm in it" (मैं इसमें हूँ): jab aap kisi aise haal mein hain jahan kuch hone wala hai, toh uska hona avashyam bhavi hai.

meaning: to confine someone against their will
mnemonic: Immure -> 'I Am Yours': when someone says 'I am yours' in a possessive way, it implies you are confined or immured to them.
hinglish: I + Muro: jab koi kehata hai 'I Muro' toh samjho woh tumhe kaid kar raha hai, jaise immure karna.

meaning: unchanging over time or unable to be changed
mnemonic: "Im" + "Mootable": when something is 'im' (not) mootable, it means it is immutable — it cannot be changed or debated.
hinglish: "Im" + "Mutability": jab kuch 'im' (nahi) mutability (badalne layak) nahi hai, tab woh immutable hai — woh nahi badal sakta.

meaning: the state of being weakened or damaged
mnemonic: Impair -> Imbalance a Pair: damaging one eye or ear breaks the pair, causing an impairment.
hinglish: Impair -> Imbalance a Pair: ek aankh ya kaan ko kharabi karne se dono me imbalance aata hai, jo impairment hota hai.

meaning: to hinder or obstruct someone's progress
mnemonic: "Im" + "Speed": if you impede someone's speed, you slow them down, just like traffic can impede your journey.
hinglish: "Im" + "Speed": agar aap kisi ki speed ko impede karte hain, toh aap unhe slow kar dete hain, jaise traffic aapke safar ko rok sakta hai.

meaning: a hindrance or obstruction in doing something
mnemonic: "Imped" + "Hindrance": if you impede someone's progress, you put an obstacle in their way, causing an impediment to their success.
hinglish: "Imped" + "Rog": agar aap kisi ka kaam impede karte hain, toh aap unke raste me ek rog (badhak) daal rahe hain, jo unki safalta ke liye ek impediment hai.

meaning: impossible to pass through or enter
mnemonic: "Impen" (impassable) + "etrable" (able to enter): if something is impenetrable, it is not able to be entered or passed through, like a solid wall.
hinglish: "Impen" (abbey) + "etrable" (entry karna): agar kuch impenetrable hai, toh woh entry karne layak nahi hota, jaise ek majboot deewaar.

meaning: of vital importance; crucial
mnemonic: Imperative -> 'Important Pair': when something is of utmost importance, it's imperative to act like a perfect pair in sync, ensuring everything goes smoothly.
hinglish: Impe + Rative: jab kuch bahut zaroori hota hai, toh yeh imperative hota hai ki hum us par dhyaan dein.

meaning: assuming power or authority without justification; arrogant and domineering
mnemonic: Imperious -> 'I'm Peerious': a person who thinks they are a peer of royalty can be very imperious, acting as though they are above everyone else.
hinglish: I'm + Peerious: jab koi apne aap ko sabse ucha samajhta hai, tab voh imperious hota hai, jaise ek raja.

meaning: rude or disrespectful; not showing proper respect
mnemonic: Im + Pertinent: if you are 'im' (not) 'pertinent' (relevant), you are being impertinent by being rude or off-topic in the discussion.
hinglish: Im + Pertinent: agar aap 'im' (nahi) 'pertinent' (maamle se sambandhit) hain, toh aap be-tuka baatein karke sabko naraz kar rahe hain.

meaning: not easily disturbed or excited; calm
mnemonic: "Imperturb" + "able": someone who is able to remain calm and unshaken, no matter what happens, is truly imperturbable.
hinglish: "Imperturb" + "able": jo vyakti har paristhiti mein shant rahe, woh imperturbable hai.

meaning: not allowing fluid to pass through; impenetrable
mnemonic: Im + Pervious: Imagine a wall that is 'im'penetrable and 'per'meable, indicating it is impervious to water, just like his feelings were impervious to insults.
hinglish: Im + Pervious: Socho ek dikhti deewar jo paani ko rok deti hai, jaise wo aadmi ki feelings criticism se 'im'pervious hain.

meaning: acting or done quickly and without thought or care
mnemonic: Impulsive + Pet: an impetuous child might impulsively pet a wild animal without thinking of the danger.
hinglish: Impulsive + Pet: ek avicharpoorn bachcha bagair soch-vichar ke ek jangli jaanwar ko pet karne lagta hai.

meaning: unable to be appeased or placated
mnemonic: Im + Place + Able: if you can't find a place to calm someone down, their anger is implacable.
hinglish: Im + Pluck + Able: agar kisi ka gussa itna zyada hai ki aap unhe pluck (chhedna) nahi kar sakte, to wo implacable hain.

meaning: understood though not directly stated
mnemonic: Im + Plicit: when something is implicit, it is like an unspoken agreement that is understood without being spelled out; implicit trust exists without needing to be stated.
hinglish: Im + Plicit: jab kuch implicit hota hai, to iska matlab hai ki woh baat bina kahay samjhi jaati hai, jaise implicit trust hum sab ke beech hai.

meaning: not politic; unwise or imprudent
mnemonic: "Imp" + "Politic": like an imp (mischievous being) who acts without thinking, making impolitic remarks can get you in trouble.
hinglish: "Imp" + "Politic": ek chhota sa imp jab bina soche samjhe baat kare, toh wo impolitic hoti hai, jaise boss ko saamne criticize karna.

meaning: to create or perform something spontaneously without preparation
mnemonic: Impro + vise: when you have to 'improvise', you might need to 'improve' your ideas quickly, often leading to something unique.
hinglish: Impro + vise: jab aapko 'improvise' karna hota hai, tab aapko apne vichar jaldi se 'improve' karne padte hain, jo aksar kuch naya banata hai.

meaning: showing a lack of respect or boldness; insolent
mnemonic: Impudent -> Impudent Dog: a dog that barks at everyone without fear is impudent in its behavior.
hinglish: Impudent + Dog: ek bada badtameez kutta sab par bhauk raha hai, woh impudent hai.

meaning: to challenge or dispute the truth or validity of something
mnemonic: "Im" (not) + "Pugn" (fight): to impugn someone's words is to not fight against them openly, but to question their validity. The lawyer chose to impugn the witness's statement.
hinglish: "Im" (nahi) + "Pugn" (ladna): jab aap kisi ki baat par sawaal uthate ho, toh aap unki sachai ko impugn karte ho, jaise lawyer ne gawah ki baat par shak kiya.

meaning: acting or done quickly and without thought or care
mnemonic: Impulsive -> Impulse + 'If I impulse buy now, I might face regrets later': acting on a whim without thinking it through is impulsive behavior.
hinglish: Impulse + 'Agar main impulse se kharid loon, toh mujhe baad mein pachtana par sakta hai': bina soche samjhe kharidari karna impulsive hai.

meaning: not transferable to another owner
mnemonic: In + Alien + Able: if something is inalienable, it cannot be alienated or taken away, like an inalienable right.
hinglish: In + Alien + Able: agar koi cheez inalienable hai, toh use koi alien nahi le ja sakta, jaise inalienable haq.

meaning: existing from birth; innate
mnemonic: In + Born: just like a child is born with certain traits, inborn means traits or abilities that come naturally.
hinglish: In + Born: jaise ek bachcha kuch qualities ke saath janm leta hai, waise inborn ka matlab hai wo qualities ya abilities jo naturally hoti hain.

meaning: tending to stir up conflict or provoke anger
mnemonic: "In" + "Cinder" (a type of burning material): incendiary remarks can ignite a firestorm of emotions and conflicts, just like cinders can start a fire.
hinglish: "In" + "Cinder": incendiary baatein kabhi kabhi dusron ko bahut bechain kar deti hain, jaise cinder se aag lag jaati hai.

meaning: continuing without interruption
mnemonic: In + 'cess' (cessation): when something is incessant, it doesn't 'cease', meaning it continues without pause.
hinglish: In + 'cess' (rokna): jab kuch incessant hota hai, wo kabhi nahi rokta, yani wo samay bhar chalta rehta hai.

meaning: not fully formed or developed; rudimentary
mnemonic: "In" + "Coat": when you wear an inchoate coat, it’s still being tailored and not fully ready to wear, just like an inchoate idea.
hinglish: "In" + "Koti": jab aapki koti abhi tayaar nahi hui hai, wo inchoate hai, jaise abhi koi vichar pakka nahi hua hai.

meaning: occurring by chance in connection with something else
mnemonic: "In" + "Cidental" (like 'incident'): an incidental expense is like an unexpected incident that comes up occasionally, not planned for.
hinglish: "In" + "Cidental": project ke saath aane wale additional kharche kabhi kabhi incidental hote hain, jo pehle se nahi sochhe gaye the.

meaning: to provoke or stir up (an action or feeling)
mnemonic: "In" + "Sight": when something is brought into sight, it can incite strong feelings and reactions, just like a rallying cry incites enthusiasm.
hinglish: "In" + "Sight": jab kuch nazar aata hai, toh woh bhavnaon ko uttejit kar sakta hai, jaise ek chuni hui bhashan shroton mein jazbaat bhare.

meaning: having a tendency or preference towards something
mnemonic: In + Clined (kind): when you are kind, you're inclined to help others, just as she is inclined to support environmental causes.
hinglish: In + Kline (line): agar aap kisi cheez ki taraf line banate hain, to aap us cheez ki taraf inclined hain.

meaning: not in harmony or keeping with the surroundings; inappropriate
mnemonic: "Incongruent" -> "In Congruity": when something is not in congruity with its environment, it's incongruous; wearing formal attire at a casual event is incongruous.
hinglish: "In + Congruity": jab kuch cheezein ek dusre se milti nahi hain, tab wo incongruous hain; beach party mein tuxedo pehna incongruous hai.

meaning: not able to be denied or disputed
mnemonic: In + Controversy: when something is incontrovertible, it means there is no controversy around it, as the facts are clear and undeniable.
hinglish: In + Controversy: jab kisi cheez mein koi vivad nahi hota, tab wo cheez incontrovertible hoti hai, kyunki sabhi jaanate hain ki wo sach hai.

meaning: unwilling to believe something; skeptical
mnemonic: "In" + "Credulous": if you're not 'in' the 'credulous' group, you're incredulous, doubting the claims others believe.
hinglish: "In" + "Credulous": agar aap 'in' 'credulous' nahi hain, toh aap incredulous hain, jo doosron ke vishwas par shak karte hain.

meaning: not in keeping with good manners or proper behavior
mnemonic: In + Decorous: think of being 'in' a place where there is no decorum – his indecorous behavior at the ceremony shocked the guests.
hinglish: In + Decorous: jab koi 'in' jagah par aisa behave kare jo decorum se bahar ho, toh woh indecorous hai.

meaning: persisting tirelessly; unable to be fatigued
mnemonic: "In" + "Defeat" + "I" + "Gable": even in the face of defeat, I remain able to work tirelessly, showcasing an indefatigable attitude.
hinglish: "In" + "Deaf" + "I" + "Gable": jab bhi koi mushkil aaye, main deaf (sun nahi sakta) ho kar bhi kaam karta hoon, kyunki main indefatigable hoon.

meaning: not definite or fixed; uncertain
mnemonic: In + Definite: if you say 'in definite', it sounds like something is uncertain — just like an indefinite schedule.
hinglish: In + Nishchit: jab aap kehte hain 'in nishchit', to matlab hai kuch anishchit hai — jaise ek anishchit yatra ka plan.

meaning: a formal charge or accusation of a serious crime
mnemonic: "In" + "Dite" (to say): when you are indicted, it's like someone is saying you did something wrong, formally charging you with a crime.
hinglish: "In" + "Dite" (bolna): jab aap par indictment hota hai, tab aisa lagta hai jaise koi keh raha hai ki aapne kuch galat kiya hai.

meaning: feeling or showing anger or annoyance at what is perceived as unfair treatment
mnemonic: In + Dignant: in (inside) + dignant (dignity): when someone feels their dignity is attacked, they become indignant.
hinglish: In + Dignant: jab kisi ki izzat ko chhota kiya jaata hai, tab usse narazgi hoti hai, yaani woh indignant hota hai.

meaning: done at random or without careful judgment
mnemonic: In + Discriminate: when you are 'in' a state of confusion, you make choices indiscriminately, without judgment.
hinglish: In + Discriminate: jab aap kisi cheez ko 'in' samajh kar bina samjhe lete hain, to wo indiscriminate hota hai.

meaning: absolutely necessary; essential
mnemonic: In + Dispense + Able: something that cannot be dispensed with is indispensable and necessary.
hinglish: In + Dispense + Able: jo cheez aap chhod nahi sakte, wahi indispensable hoti hai.

meaning: disinclined to work or exertion; lazy
mnemonic: In + Dolent (sounds like 'dole out'): if you are indolent, you don't want to 'dole out' effort or work, preferring to be lazy instead.
hinglish: In + Dolent: agar aap indolent hain, toh aap kaam karne ki jagah aaram karna pasand karte hain.

meaning: to cause or bring about
mnemonic: Induce -> In + Juice: if you drink juice, it can induce a refreshing feeling, just like how one can induce a reaction in someone.
hinglish: In + Juice: agar aap juice peete hain, toh yeh aapko fresh feel karne ke liye induce karta hai.

meaning: hardworking and diligent
mnemonic: "In Dust You" -> "In Dust, You": an industrious person works hard and isn't afraid to get their hands dirty, like working in dust.
hinglish: "In Dust You" -> "In Dust, You": industrious log mehnat karte hain aur gande kaam se nahi darte, jaise ki mitti mein kaam karna.

meaning: inevitable; unavoidable
mnemonic: "In" + "Elect" + "Able": when something is in the electoral process, it becomes ineluctable as the results cannot be changed, just like fate is ineluctable.
hinglish: "In" + "Elect" + "Able": jab kuch cheezein electoral process me hoti hain, to voh ineluctable ban jaati hain kyunki parinaam badla nahi ja sakta.

meaning: lacking skill or ability
mnemonic: "Inept" -> "I Nept": I watched a nept (inept) acrobat fall flat on his face during the performance.
hinglish: "Inept" -> "I Nept": Jab maine acrobat ko nept (inept) tarike se perform karte dekha, toh woh seedha zameen par gir gaya.

meaning: a thing that is inappropriate or unfortunate
mnemonic: In + Felicity: when you have no felicity (happiness), you're stuck in infelicity, like the time I awkwardly tripped on stage.
hinglish: In + Felicity: jab aap khushi se door hote hain, tab aap infelicity me hote hain, jaise maine ek baar galti se stage par gir gaya tha.

meaning: to give someone knowledge or information about something
mnemonic: Inform -> 'In Form': when you inform someone, you put them 'in form' about what's going on.
hinglish: In + Form: jab aap kisi ko inform karte hain, to aap unhe 'form' me le aate hain jisse unhe sab kuch pata chal jata hai.

meaning: cleverly inventive or resourceful
mnemonic: "In" + "Genius": an ingenious idea is one that comes from a genius mind, showcasing clever inventiveness — like solving a puzzle in a unique way.
hinglish: "In" + "Genius": ingenious idea ek genius dimaag se aata hai, jo chaturai aur nayaapan dikhata hai — jaise ek paheli ka anokha hal nikalna.

meaning: innocent and unsuspecting
mnemonic: "In" + "Genuine": if someone is genuine, they are often simple and ingenuous, trusting others easily — just like him.
hinglish: "In" + "Genuine": agar koi vyakti genuine hai, toh voh aksar simple aur ingenuous hota hai, doosron par asani se bharosa kar leta hai — jaise usne kiya.

meaning: firmly established and difficult to change
mnemonic: "In" + "Grain": just like grains grow deeply in the soil, some beliefs or habits are ingrained in us from a young age and are hard to change.
hinglish: "In" + "Grain": jaise anaj mitti mein gehra jata hai, waise hi kuch aadatein humare andar gehri hoti hain, jo badalne mein mushkil hoti hain.

meaning: to prevent or restrict the progress or action of something
mnemonic: In + Hibit: 'Inhibit' sounds like 'Inhibit', which means to hold back; the new law might inhibit progress in the industry.
hinglish: In + Hibit: naye kanun se aage badhne ke liye chizhein inhibit (rokna) ho rahi hain.

meaning: hostile or unfriendly
mnemonic: In + Mimic + Al: if someone mimics a person in an inimical way, they are being unfriendly and hostile.
hinglish: In + Mimic + Al: agar koi insaan kisi ko dushman ki tarah mimic karta hai, to wo dosti nahi, balki shatrutapurn hai.

meaning: not harmful or offensive
mnemonic: Innocuous -> 'In no way' + 'Cousin': imagine a cousin who always tells harmless jokes; his innocuous remarks never offend anyone.
hinglish: In + No + Cousin: socho ek cousin jo sirf paagal jokes sunata hai, uski baatein kabhi bhi nuksan nahi deti, bilkul innocuous hai.

meaning: having a strong desire to know or learn things
mnemonic: In + Quiz + Itive: if you are inquisitive, you would want to quiz others and know more about them.
hinglish: In + Quiz + Itive: agar aap jigyasu hain, toh aap doosron se sawal karke unke baare mein jaankari lena chahenge.

meaning: difficult to understand or interpret
mnemonic: "In" + "Scoot" + "Able": when someone scoots away, their intentions become inscrutable, like a mystery.
hinglish: "In" + "Screw" + "Table": jab koi table par screw daal raha ho, uski soch samajhna mushkil hota hai, jaise inscrutable hai.

meaning: proceeding in a gradual, subtle way but with harmful effects
mnemonic: "In" + "Sidious" (like 'sidious' of 'devious'): something that sneaks up and harms you in an insidious way, just like a devious plan that unfolds without you noticing.
hinglish: "In" + "Sidious" (जैसे 'सिदियस' का 'चालाक'): जैसे कोई चालाक योजना धीरे-धीरे आपको नुकसान पहुँचाती है, वैसे ही 'insidious' चीजें होती हैं।

meaning: lacking flavor or interest
mnemonic: In + sip + id: When you take a sip of something insipid, you wish it had more flavor, because it tastes bland.
hinglish: In + sip + id: Jab aap insipid chai ka sip lete hain, toh aap sochte hain ki iska swaad thoda zyada hona chahiye.

meaning: showing a rude and arrogant lack of respect
mnemonic: 'In' + 'Sole' (shoe): if you step on someone's shoe without care, you're being insolent — showing a lack of respect.
hinglish: 'In' + 'Sole' (jooti): agar aap kisi ki jooti par kadam rakhte hain bina izzat kiye, to aap asabhya hain.

meaning: limited in outlook or scope; narrow-minded
mnemonic: Insulate -> Insular: if you insulate a room, you keep it separate from the outside, leading to insular thinking and attitudes.
hinglish: Insulate + Insular: agar aap kisi jagah ko insulate karte hain, toh woh alag ho jaata hai, jisse insular soch aur nazariye bante hain.

meaning: capable of being understood; clear
mnemonic: "Intelligent" + "Able": if you are intelligent, your thoughts are likely intelligible to others; hence you can communicate clearly.
hinglish: "Intelligent" + "Able": agar aap intelligent hain, toh aapki baatein samajhne ke layak hoti hain, yani intelligible hain.

meaning: capable of being exchanged or substituted
mnemonic: "Inter" (between) + "Changeable" (able to change): things that can be exchanged or swapped without any issue are interchangeable.
hinglish: "Inter" (beech me) + "Changeable" (badal sakta hai): aise cheezein jo beech me badli ja sakti hain, wo interchangeable hoti hain.

meaning: a person who acts as a link between parties in a negotiation or transaction
mnemonic: Inter + Mediary: an intermediary is like a middleman who connects two parties, ensuring smooth communication.
hinglish: Inter + Mediary: ek intermediary do parties ke beech mein ek middleman ki tarah kaam karta hai, jo samvaad ko aasaan banata hai.

meaning: endless or seemingly unending
mnemonic: "Inter" (between) + "Terminate" (end): when something is interminable, it feels like the end is always between you and the situation, never actually happening.
hinglish: "Inter" (beech) + "Terminate" (khatam karna): jab koi baat interminable hoti hai, to woh aapko beech mein hi khatam hote hue mehsoos hoti hai, kabhi khatam nahi hoti.

meaning: occurring at irregular intervals; not continuous or steady
mnemonic: "Inter" (between) + "mit" (send): when something is intermittent, it sends rain or events in between dry spells, which can be very unpredictable.
hinglish: "Inter" (बीच) + "mit" (भेजना): जब बारिश अंतरालिक होती है, तब वह बीच-बीच में बारिश भेजती है, जिससे आप योजना बनाने में असमर्थ होते हैं।

meaning: twisted together or closely connected
mnemonic: Inter + Twine: if you intertwine threads, they become tightly twisted together like a braid.
hinglish: Inter + Twine: jab do dhaage ek saath inter karte hain, to wo ek dusre se juda ho jaate hain.

meaning: to make known or communicate something, often subtly
mnemonic: In + Timid: if you're timid, you might prefer to intimate your feelings softly instead of shouting them.
hinglish: In + Timid: agar aap timid hain, to aap apne jazbat intimation ke zariye dhere dhere kehna pasand karte hain.

meaning: unwilling to change one's views or to agree about something
mnemonic: In + Transigent: a person who is inflexible can be seen as someone who won't change their position, like a wall that won't let anything pass.
hinglish: In + Transigent: ek aadmi jo apni soch nahi badalta, wo ek deewar ki tarah hai jo kuch bhi guzarne nahi deta.

meaning: brave and fearless; showing great courage
mnemonic: 'In' + 'Trip' + 'Ed': if you're intrepid, you’re ready to go on a trip and face any adventure without fear.
hinglish: 'In' + 'Trip' + 'Ed': agar aap intrepid hain, toh aap bina kisi dar ke naye safar par jaane ke liye tayyar hain.

meaning: to arouse the curiosity or interest of; fascinate
mnemonic: In + Trigue -> 'Intrigue': when you invite someone in to a secret, you intrigue them with hidden stories.
hinglish: In + Trigue: jab aap kisi ko andar bulaate hain kisi raaz ke liye, to aap unhe intrigue karte hain chhupi kahaniyon se.

meaning: belonging naturally; essential
mnemonic: In + Trinsic: intrinsic means that something is inherently valuable, much like the inner essence of a being.
hinglish: In + Trinsic: intrinsic ka matlab hai kisi cheez ki andar ki asli keemat, jaise kisi insaan ki sachai.

meaning: known or understood without conscious reasoning
mnemonic: In + Two + It: when you are in two minds, you often go with your intuitive feeling, which is the right choice.
hinglish: In + Tiwari: jab Tiwari koi kaam bina soch-vichar ke karte hain, to unki intuitive samajh ka use hota hai.

meaning: to overwhelm or flood with water or a large amount of something
mnemonic: In + Undate: when you 'inundate' a place, you flood it with water, much like pouring water 'in' under a date palm during a storm.
hinglish: In + Undate: jab aap kisi jagah ko 'inundate' karte hain, toh aap us jagah ko paani se bharde hain, jaise baarish ke waqt date ke ped ke neeche paani bharde.

meaning: tending to intrude on a person's space or an ecosystem
mnemonic: In + Vase: think of a plant that invades your vase, taking over and ruining the arrangement — that’s invasive!
hinglish: In + Vase: socho ek paudha tumhare vase me ghus aata hai aur sab kuch kharab kar deta hai — yeh invasive hai!

meaning: to persuade someone to do something by means of deception or flattery
mnemonic: "In" (inside) + "Veil" (cover): when someone tries to bring you 'in' and 'veil' the truth, they are trying to inveigle you into a trap.
hinglish: "In" (andar) + "Vigil" (jaag rakhna): jab koi aapko andar le aakar aapki jaag rakhne ki koshish kare, toh wo aapko fusalane ki koshish kar raha hai.

meaning: habitual, long-established, or deep-rooted
mnemonic: In + Vet + Rate: a veterinarian is known for his inveterate love for animals, always caring for them despite the challenges.
hinglish: In + Vet + Rate: ek veterinarian ka jaanwaron ke liye inveterate pyaar hai, jo hamesha unka khayal rakhta hai, chahe kitne bhi mushkil ho.

meaning: likely to arouse resentment in others
mnemonic: "Invidious" -> "In Video Us": if we were in a video, people might feel envy when they see how happy we are, making comments that are invidious.
hinglish: "In Video Us" (in video hum): agar hum kisi video mein khush dikhai dete hain, toh logon ko invidious baatein karne par majboor kar sakte hain.

meaning: to give strength or energy to something
mnemonic: "In" + "Vigor" (strength): when you invigorate someone, you bring 'in' new 'vigor' to their life, making them feel energetic.
hinglish: "In" + "Vigor" (taqat): jab aap kisi ko invigorate karte hain, to aap unki zindagi mein 'in' nayi 'taqat' laate hain, unhe energetic bana dete hain.

meaning: free from violation; intact
mnemonic: In + Violate: if something is 'in' (inside) and 'violate' (broken), it means it is preserved and inviolate, like a secret garden untouched by outsiders.
hinglish: In + Violate: agar kuch 'in' (andar) hai aur 'violate' (todna) nahi hua, toh wo ek inviolate jagah hai, jaise ek purana khazana jo kabhi nahi chhoda gaya.

meaning: easily provoked to anger
mnemonic: I + Rascal: a rascal is often irascible, easily getting angry over small issues, just like that grumpy neighbor.
hinglish: I + Rascal: ek rascal aadmi aksar chidhchidhana hota hai, choti baaton par gussa ho jata hai.

meaning: intense anger
mnemonic: "I" + "Air": when I can't breathe properly from the anger in the air, that's my ire; intense anger takes my breath away.
hinglish: "I" + "Aire": jab mujhe gusse ke kuchh aira gaira se takleef hoti hai, tab meri ire bahut badh jaati hai.

meaning: annoying or irritating
mnemonic: Irritate + Some: When you annoy someone too much, it becomes irksome and they may ask for some peace.
hinglish: Irritate + Some: Jab aap kisi ko bahut zyada chidhate hain, toh wo irksome ho jata hai aur wo kuch shanti maangte hain.

meaning: strongly built and unassailable; secure
mnemonic: Iron + Clad: an iron-clad ship is so well-protected that it can withstand attacks, just like an ironclad deal is secure and unassailable.
hinglish: Iron + Clad: ek iron-clad samjhauta itna mazboot hota hai ki use todna mushkil hota hai.

meaning: uncertain or indecisive
mnemonic: Irresolute -> 'I' (myself) + 'Resolve': when I lack resolve, I become irresolute about my decisions.
hinglish: I + Resolve: jab main khud ek faisla lene me asamarth hota hoon, tab main irresolute ho jata hoon.

meaning: showing a lack of respect for things that are generally taken seriously
mnemonic: "Irreverent" -> "I Reverent": when you say 'I reverent', you're showing respect, but if you're irreverent, you're doing the opposite by mocking sacred traditions.
hinglish: "I Reverent" -> "I nahi Reverent": jab aap kehte hain 'I nahi reverent', iska matlab hai aap kisi cheez ka mazak uda rahe hain jo logon ke liye serious hai.

meaning: traveling from place to place, especially for work
mnemonic: Itin + Errant: an itinerant person is like someone who is errantly wandering to different locations; he is always on the move.
hinglish: Itin + Rant: ek itinerant aadmi hamesha ghoomte rehta hai aur naye jagahon par rant (baten) karta hai.

meaning: to put something at risk or in danger
mnemonic: Jeopardy -> 'Jep' (a sound) + 'Hard' (difficult): if you play Jeopardy in a hard way, you jeopardize your chances of winning by risking wrong answers.
hinglish: Jep + Hard: agar aap Jeopardy khelte hain bina soche samjhe, toh aap apne jeetne ke mauke ko jeopardize kar rahe hain.

meaning: to discard or throw away something that is no longer wanted
mnemonic: "Jet" + "Sonic": like a jet that is too heavy, it must jettison excess baggage to fly faster and higher, just as a ship does with cargo.
hinglish: "Jet" + "Sonic": jaise ek jet agar bhaari ho jaaye to use kuch saman jettison karna padta hai, waise hi captain ne cargo jettison kiya.

meaning: cheerful and light-hearted
mnemonic: Joke + 'und': when you hear a good joke, you feel jocund — cheerful and happy.
hinglish: Joke + 'und': jab tum ek accha joke sunte ho, tumhara mood khushmizaaz (jocund) ho jaata hai.

meaning: having or showing good judgment; wise
mnemonic: "Juice" + "Decision": when you're making a judicious choice, like choosing the right juice, you're using good judgment. — A judicious decision is one made with careful consideration.
hinglish: "Juice" + "Faisla": jab aap achha juice chunne ke liye judicious faisla karte hain, aap samajhdari dikhate hain. — Ek judicious faisla woh hota hai jo soch samajh kar kiya jata hai.

meaning: having or showing eagerness or enthusiasm
mnemonic: "Key" + "in": finding the key to a door makes you keen to enter a new place full of opportunities.
hinglish: "Kya" + "in": nayi cheezein seekhne ke liye woh hamesha "kya in" karne ke liye utasook thi.

meaning: concise, using few words
mnemonic: Lack + On + It: when you lack words, you say only what's necessary, being laconic in your communication.
hinglish: Lack + On + It: jab aapko baatein chhoti rakhni hoti hain, toh aap sirf zaroori baatein karte hain, jo laconic hota hai.

meaning: to criticize someone or something very harshly
mnemonic: "Lamb" + "Baste": like basting a lamb with sauce, you are criticizing it harshly — to lambaste is to roast someone verbally.
hinglish: "Lamb" + "Baste": ek lamb ko baste karte waqt, aap us par mazak kar rahe hote hain, jisse lambaste ka matlab hai kisi ko bura kehna.

meaning: to express sorrow or regret for something
mnemonic: Lame + Meant: when something is lame, it means it's not meant to be loved, causing you to lament its absence.
hinglish: Lame + Maan: jab kuch lame hota hai, toh dil se maan karte hain, yaani lament karte hain uski kami ko.

meaning: to publicly criticize or mock someone or something in a humorous way
mnemonic: "Lamp" + "Poon": imagine a lamp shining light on a cartoonish balloon of a politician, as the comedian lampoons their silly promises.
hinglish: "Lamp" + "Poon": sochiyega ek lamp jo politician ki funny balloon ko roshni deta hai, jab comedian unhe lampoon karta hai.

meaning: weak or faint from exhaustion or illness
mnemonic: "Lang" (like a weak 'language') + "Guid" (as in 'guide'): if your energy is languid, you might need a guide to help you move forward. — She felt so languid that she could barely keep her eyes open.
hinglish: "Lang" (कमजोर) + "Guid" (मार्गदर्शक): jab aapki energy languid hoti hai, toh aapko kisi guide ki zaroorat hoti hai. — Uski energy itni languid thi ki woh aankhein khuli rakh nahi paa rahi thi.

meaning: to suffer from being forced to remain in an unpleasant situation
mnemonic: Lang + Wish: when you lang (long) for something and can't get it, you may languish in sadness and regret.
hinglish: Lang + Wish: jab aap kisi cheez ki lang (lambi) khwahish karte hain par woh nahi milti, tab aap languish karte hain.

meaning: generosity in giving, especially money or gifts
mnemonic: Large + Yes: when someone says 'yes' to giving large amounts, it shows their largesse in generosity.
hinglish: Large + Yes: jab koi 'yes' kehta hai badi badi daan dene ke liye, toh ye uski udarta yaani largesse ko dikhata hai.

meaning: a state of physical or mental weariness; lack of energy
mnemonic: "Last" + "Attitude": when you have the 'last' bit of energy, your 'attitude' is one of lassitude, showing that you're too tired to care.
hinglish: "Last" + "Aadmi": last aadmi bante bante, wo itna thak gaya ki usse lassitude me chalay gaya.

meaning: the angular distance of a place north or south of the Earth's equator
mnemonic: Latitude -> 'Lattitude' (like a ladder): imagine climbing a ladder that takes you to different latitudes around the world, measuring how far north or south you go.
hinglish: Lattitude -> 'Latt' + 'itude' (like a ladder): socho, tum ladders par chadh rahe ho aur alag-alag latitudes ko measure kar rahe ho, yeh dikhata hai tum kitne north ya south ja rahe ho.

meaning: worthy of praise
mnemonic: "Laud" -> "Loud": when you laud someone, you speak loudly in their praise, making their efforts laudable.
hinglish: "Laud" + "Loud": jab aap kisi ki tarif karte hain, toh aap unhe loud (tez) tarike se sarahte hain, isliye ye kaam laudable hai.

meaning: sumptuously rich, elaborate, or luxurious
mnemonic: Lavish -> 'Lavish' (spend lavishly): the bride's family decided to spend lavishly on her wedding to make it unforgettable.
hinglish: Lavi + Shit: dulhan ki family ne shaadi par itni lavish kharch kiya ki sab dekhte reh gaye.

meaning: not strict or severe; relaxed
mnemonic: Lax -> Lack: if you lack discipline, your rules will be lax, leading to chaos.
hinglish: Lax -> Lack: agar aapki discipline mein lack hai, toh aapke niyam lax honge, jo kaos tak le jayenge.

meaning: a state of sluggishness or inactivity
mnemonic: Lethargy -> 'Let Tar' + 'Gic': when you let a tar-stained object weigh you down, you become lethargic and slow.
hinglish: Let + Tar + Gic: jab aap tar se bhari cheez ko chhod dete hain, tab aap lethargic ho jaate hain aur dheere ho jaate hain.

meaning: lightness of mind, character, or behavior; lack of seriousness
mnemonic: Levity -> 'Levy Tea': if you’re at a tea party where everyone is joking and laughing, there’s a levity in the atmosphere, making the mood light.
hinglish: Levity -> 'Levy T': jab aap chai par baith kar mazak karte hain, tab wahan levity hoti hai, jo mahol ko halka banati hai.

meaning: a state of being legally responsible for something, especially in financial terms
mnemonic: "Liability" -> "Lie Ability": if you have the ability to lie about your debts, you still face the liability of paying them back — a true liability.
hinglish: "Li" + "Ability": agar aapke paas paise chhupane ki ability hai, tab bhi aapki liability aapko pakad legi kaam se kaam — aapko udhar chukana padega.

meaning: a person who behaves without moral principles, especially in sexual matters
hindi: लिबर्टाइन (लैंगिक मामलों में नैतिक सिद्धांतों के बिना व्यवहार करने वाला व्यक्ति)
mnemonic: "Liberty" + "Teen": a teenager who feels free to explore life with no moral boundaries often ends up acting like a libertine, embracing every temptation.
hinglish: "Liberty" + "Teen": ek teenager jo zindagi ko bina kisi niyam ke jeeta hai, woh aksar libertine ki tarah vyavhar karta hai, har pokar ka anand uthata hai.

meaning: clear and transparent; easily understood
mnemonic: 'Limp' + 'Id': when someone is 'limp', they feel weak, but 'limpid' waters are clear and strong, reflecting everything around them.
hinglish: 'Limp' + 'Id': jab paani limp ya kamzor hota hai, tab wo limp nahi hota, par limpid paani hamesha saaf aur spashht hota hai.

meaning: to treat someone as a celebrity or to give excessive praise
mnemonic: Lion + Ize: treat someone like a 'lion' (king of the jungle) by giving them excessive praise, just as people lionize their favorite celebrities.
hinglish: Lion + Ize: kisi ko 'lion' ki tarah (jungle ka raja) samajhkar unhe zyada tareef karte hain, jaise log apne pasandida celebrities ko lionize karte hain.

meaning: to feel intense dislike or disgust for something
mnemonic: Loathe -> Loth (reluctant) + Hate: if you are loth to do something, you loathe it, just like how I loathe doing my chores.
hinglish: Loathe -> Loth (nafrat) + Hate: jab aap kisi cheez se loth hai, tab aap usse nafrat karte hain, jaise mujhe chores karne se loth hai.

meaning: talkative or verbose
mnemonic: "Loco" (crazy) + "Quacious" (talkative): a loco (crazy) person is often very loquacious, chatting away without stopping.
hinglish: "Loco" (pagal) + "Quacious" (bolne wala): ek pagal aadmi aksar loquacious hota hai, bina rukhe baatein karta hai.

meaning: easy to understand; clear
mnemonic: Lucid -> 'Lucid Dream': in a lucid dream, you are aware and can control your actions, just as a lucid explanation is clear and easy to understand.
hinglish: Loo + Sid: jab 'loo' ka paani clear ho, toh usmein sab kuch 'sid' (clear) dikhai deta hai, jaise ek lucid explanation sab kuch samajhane mein madad karta hai.

meaning: producing a great deal of profit
mnemonic: Loot + Crate: if you find a crate full of loot, it’s a lucrative treasure! — a treasure that brings in a lot of profit.
hinglish: Loot + Karna: agar aapko koi lucrative business mile, toh aap usme loot kar sakte hain! — a business that allows you to gain a lot of profit.

meaning: looking or sounding sad and dismal
mnemonic: "Loo" (as in bathroom) + "Gloomy": after using a bathroom, if you feel gloomy about your day, you might wear a lugubrious expression.
hinglish: "Loo" (bathroom) + "Ghamgeen": jab aap restroom se baahar aate hain aur aapka chehra ghamgeen hota hai, tab aap lugubrious dikhte hain.

meaning: to calm or soothe, often leading to sleep
mnemonic: Lull -> 'Lullaby': a soothing song sung to calm a baby to sleep; a lull is like a lullaby that calms you down.
hinglish: Lull + 'Al': lull se khud ko alvida kehkar aap aaraam se so jaate hain.

meaning: gruesome and horrifying; relating to death and the dark side of human nature
mnemonic: "Mac" (like McDonald's) + "Cabre" (like cabaret): imagine a macabre cabaret show where the performers are all ghouls and ghosts, making everything eerie and horrifying.
hinglish: "Makaan" + "Kabre": socho ek makaan hai jisme kabre hain, wahaan ka mausam bahut hi bhayanak hai.

meaning: having an authoritative or commanding quality
mnemonic: Master + Real: a magisterial presence is like a master who commands respect in a real way — his authority is felt by all.
hinglish: Master + Real: ek magisterial vyakti jaise master hota hai, jo sabko apni authority se prabhavit karta hai.

meaning: generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival or less fortunate person
mnemonic: Magna + Animous: a 'magnet' draws people in with its powerful and generous nature, just like a magnanimous person who forgives easily.
hinglish: Magna + Aam: ek 'magnet' logon ko apni taraf kheenchta hai, jaise ki ek magnanimous vyakti jo asaani se maaf karta hai.

meaning: temporary and often improvised solution
mnemonic: Make + Shift: when you need to make a shift in plans quickly, you create a makeshift solution like a temporary fix.
hinglish: Make + Shift: jab aapko kabhi bhi koi asan aur tezi se solution dena ho, tab aap makeshift tarika istemal karte hain.

meaning: having or showing a wish to do evil to others
mnemonic: Male + Volent (violent): a male who is violent is likely to be malevolent, wishing harm on others.
hinglish: Male + Violent: ek male jo violent hai, woh aksar malevolent hota hai, dusron ko nuksan pahunchane ki sochta hai.

meaning: wrongdoing or misconduct, especially by a public official
mnemonic: Mal + Feasance: when something is 'mal' (bad) you can expect 'feasance' (doing) to lead to malfeasance — a public figure engaging in wrongdoing.
hinglish: Mal + Faisance: jab kisi public official ka 'mal' (bura) kaam hota hai, to usay malfeasance kehte hain.

meaning: to speak harmful untruths about; to slander
mnemonic: Mal + Align: when you malign someone, you misalign their reputation by spreading malice and lies.
hinglish: Mal + Aline: jab aap kisi ki ninda karte hain, toh aap uski izzat ko mal ke tarah ganda kar dete hain.

meaning: capable of being shaped or bent without breaking
mnemonic: Mallet + Able: a mallet can shape soft metal, making it malleable and easy to work with.
hinglish: Mallet + Able: ek mallet se naram dhatu ko aise banaya ja sakta hai ki wo malleable hai.

meaning: shackled with handcuffs
mnemonic: Man + Shackle: manacles lock a man's hands so he cannot move.
hinglish: Hath + Kadi: manacles se aadmi ke haath hathkadi me bandh ho jaate hain.

meaning: to display or show clearly
mnemonic: "Man" + "Ifest" (like 'if fest'): if a festival is a celebration, it manifests joy and excitement for everyone involved.
hinglish: "Man" + "Ifest": agar festival khushiyon ka jashn hai, toh yeh khushiyan prakat karti hain.

meaning: to treat a person or group as insignificant or peripheral
mnemonic: Margin + Alize: when you 'alize' or analyze something, you may create a margin that makes others feel left out; hence, to marginalize is to push them to the margins.
hinglish: Margin + Alize: jab aap kisi cheez ko 'alize' karte hain, toh aap kisi ko margin me chhod dete hain; isliye, marginalize karte hain matlab unhe marginal karna.

meaning: a strict disciplinarian, especially in the armed forces
mnemonic: Martini + Net: a martinet is someone who would make you follow strict rules as if you were caught in a net after having one too many martinis.
hinglish: Martini + Net: ek martinet aisa vyakti hota hai jo strict rules ko follow karne ke liye aapko net me band kar deta hai jaise aapne zyada martini pee li ho.

meaning: excessively sentimental, often to the point of being sickening
mnemonic: "Mawk" (mock) + "Ish" (ish): if you mock someone for being overly sentimental, you might call their behavior mawkish — it's just too much.
hinglish: "Mawk" (mock) + "Ish" (ish): jab koi itna sentimental ho jaye ki use mock kiya ja sake, tab uski feelings ko mawkish kaha jaata hai.

meaning: to intervene in a dispute to bring about an agreement or reconciliation
mnemonic: "Meet" + "Eight": when you meet eight different people, you often need to mediate their various opinions to reach a common agreement.
hinglish: "Meet" + "Eight": jab aap aath logon se milte hain, toh aksar aapko unke bich samjhauta karna padta hai.

meaning: the quality of being untruthful; a tendency to lie
mnemonic: Men + Dacity: men often exhibit mendacity when they try to impress others with lies.
hinglish: Men + Dacity: kabhi-kabhi mard apne aap ko achha dikhane ke liye jhoot bolte hain, ye mendacity hoti hai.

meaning: a soldier hired to fight for a foreign army
mnemonic: Mercenary -> 'Mercy' + 'Nary': if you’re fighting for mercenary wages, you have no mercy and care nary for the cause you fight for.
hinglish: Mercy + Nary: agar aap bhade ke liye lad rahe hain, toh aapko kisike liye koi mercy nahi hai.

meaning: characterized by rapid and unpredictable change; fickle
mnemonic: "Mercury" -> "Mercury rises and falls": like the quick changes in temperature, a mercurial person is unpredictable in their emotions and reactions.
hinglish: "Mercury" -> "Mercury ki tarah chanchal": wo ladki mercury ki tarah chanchal hai, kabhi khush kabhi udas.

meaning: deserving praise or recognition for one's actions or qualities
mnemonic: "Merit" + "orious" (full of merits): someone who is meritorious is full of merits and deserves recognition for their good deeds.
hinglish: "Merit" + "orious": jo log meritorious hote hain, unke kaam itne deserving hote hain ki unhe sharmaana nahi chahiye.

meaning: not literal, representing something else abstractly
mnemonic: "Meta" + "Phorical" (like "phoric" in metaphor): when you think of a metaphor, you're using metaphorical language to express ideas in a non-literal way.
hinglish: "Meta" + "Phorical": jab aap kisi baat ko rupak ke roop me vyakt karte hain, to aap metaphorical bhaasha ka istemal kar rahe hain.

meaning: showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise
mnemonic: "Meticulous" -> "Meta Clue Us": when we search for 'meta clues' in a game, we must be meticulous and thorough to find all the hidden hints.
hinglish: "Meticulous" -> "Metti Clue Us": jab hum kisi khiladi ki tarah chhupi hui cheezen dhundte hain, toh humein meticulous hona padta hai, har chhoti baat par dhyan dena padta hai.

meaning: spirited, courageous, and full of energy
mnemonic: Met + Tickle: getting tickled makes you giggle and feel spirited, just like someone who is mettlesome.
hinglish: Met + Tickle: jab aapko koi cheez tickle karti hai, toh aap bechain aur utsaahi ho jaate hain, jaise mettlesome log hote hain.

meaning: to imitate or copy someone's actions or speech
mnemonic: Mimic -> 'Mimicry' + 'Mickey': just like a child might mimic Mickey Mouse's voice, to imitate is to 'mimic' someone's mannerisms.
hinglish: Mimic + Mickey: ek chhota baccha Mickey Mouse ki awaaz ko mimic karta hai, matlab nikal karna kisi ki tarah behave karna.

meaning: extremely small; minor
mnemonic: Minute -> Mini Tube: a mini tube is extremely small; the minute details in your project can make or break it.
hinglish: Mini + Tube: mini tube bahut chhoti hoti hai; koi bhi kaam ke minute details bahut zaroori hote hain.

meaning: disliking humankind and avoiding human society
mnemonic: Mis + Anthropic: when you misjudge people, you become misanthropic and avoid them.
hinglish: Mis + Anthropos: agar aap insaanon se nafrat karte hain, toh aap misanthropic hain.

meaning: a person who behaves badly or unlawfully
mnemonic: "Miss" + "Create": when you miss out on good behavior and create chaos, you become a miscreant — a person behaving badly.
hinglish: "Miss" + "Kriant": jab aap achhe bartav ko miss karte hain aur bura kartay hain, toh aap ek miscreant ban jaate hain.

meaning: stingy or unwilling to spend money
mnemonic: Mice + Early: mice are known for being cautious with crumbs, just like a miserly person hoards their money.
hinglish: Mice + Early: chuhon ki tarah kanjus log hamesha paise kharch karne se pehle sochte hain.

meaning: an incorrect or unsuitable name or term
mnemonic: Miss + Nomer: if you misspell a name, you give it a misnomer, like calling a giant 'Tiny'.
hinglish: Miss + Nomer: agar aap kisi cheez ka galat naam rakhte hain, to woh uska misnomer ban jaata hai, jaise ek bade kutte ko 'Tiny' kehna.

meaning: to make less severe, serious, or painful
mnemonic: Mitigate -> 'Mite' + 'Gate': imagine a tiny 'mite' squeezing through a 'gate' to escape danger, making the situation less severe — just like to mitigate is to lessen something serious.
hinglish: Mite + Gate: chhoti si 'mite' gate se bahar nikal kar mushkil se bach jaati hai, jaise kisi samasya ko mitigate karna, usse kam karna.

meaning: having a moderate or humble estimate of one's abilities or worth
mnemonic: Mod + Est: if you 'mod' (modify) your 'est' (estimate) of yourself, you are being modest by not overestimating your abilities.
hinglish: Mod + Est: agar aap apni 'mod' (sudhar) karte hain aur 'est' (estimate) ko kam rakhte hain, toh aap namr hain.

meaning: fashionable or stylish
mnemonic: Modish -> Mod + Dish: If a dish is mod (modern), it’s stylish like a modish meal at a fancy restaurant.
hinglish: Mod + Dish: Agar koi dish mod hai, to wo fashion mein stylish hai, jaise modish restaurant ka khana.

meaning: to soothe or calm someone's anger or anxiety
mnemonic: Mollify -> 'Molly Fly': Imagine a girl named Molly who calms a buzzing fly by gently guiding it outside; she mollifies the situation.
hinglish: Mollify -> 'Moli Fly': socho Moli ek fly ko shant karti hai jab wo baarish mein udta hai; wo situation ko mollify karti hai.

meaning: lasting for a very short time
mnemonic: "Moment" + "Tarry": if you tarry for just a moment, it means you stayed for a very short time, just like a momentary event.
hinglish: "Moment" + "Tarry": agar aap sirf ek pal ke liye rukte hain, toh wo momentary hai.

meaning: lacking in variety and interest; dull
mnemonic: Mono + Tonous: a single tone (monotone) creates a monotonous sound that makes everything dull.
hinglish: Mono + Tonous: ek hi tone sunne se baatein itni monotonous ho jaati hain ki sunne mein maza nahi aata.

meaning: having a sharp or biting quality; critical or sarcastic
mnemonic: Mordant -> 'More Dant' (teeth): if your humor is mordant, it bites like more teeth, sharp and critical.
hinglish: More + Dant: agar aapka mazak mordant hai, toh yeh aur zyada dant ki tarah kaat-ta hai, teekha aur samajhdar.

meaning: sullen and ill-tempered
mnemonic: Moor + Rose: Imagine a moor (a bleak area) where a rose cannot bloom because the place is too morose to bring joy.
hinglish: Moor + Rose: Ek moor par rose nahi khilta kyunki waha ka mahal bahut morose hai.

meaning: having many different aspects or features
mnemonic: "Multi" (many) + "Facets" (sides): a diamond has many facets, and someone with a multifaceted personality shines in different areas.
hinglish: "Multi" (bahut) + "Facet" (pehlu): uski bahupakarita bhari vyakti ke pehlu har jagah chamakte hain.

meaning: lacking interest or excitement; dull
mnemonic: Mundane -> 'Monday': the feeling many have about Mondays is that they are mundane, marking the start of another dull work week.
hinglish: Mundane -> 'Mundane': kai log sochte hain ki Monday ka din mundane hota hai, kyunki ye kaam ki shuruaat hoti hai.

meaning: generous or giving in an extravagant way
mnemonic: "Money" + "Ficent" (like 'sufficient'): if you have enough money, you can be munificent, generously giving to others.
hinglish: "Maan" + "Ficent" (maan ka matlab hai respect): jab aap kisi ko izzat se kuch dete hain, aap munificent hote hain.

meaning: a rebellion against authority, especially by soldiers or sailors
mnemonic: "Moo" + "Tinny": when you hear the crew go 'moo' loudly like a cow, it signals a mutiny against the captain's orders.
hinglish: "Moo" + "Tin": jab naukaron ne 'moo' ki tarah cheekh maarna shuru kiya, tab unhone mutiny kiya.

meaning: lacking foresight or intellectual insight
mnemonic: My + Opic: if you're myopic, you only see things close up, like looking at a microscopic object, failing to see the bigger picture.
hinglish: My + Opaque: agar aap myopic hain, toh aapki soch itni opaque hai ki aap door ki cheezein nahi dekh sakte hain.

meaning: the lowest point; the lowest stage in a process or situation
mnemonic: "Nay" + "Deer": When a deer is in trouble, it can feel like it's at its nadir — the lowest point of its life.
hinglish: "Nay" + "Deer": Jab ek deer pareshani me hota hai, toh wo apne nadir par hota hai — matlab uski zindagi ka sabse kharaab samay.

meaning: lacking experience or sophistication; innocent
mnemonic: "Nigh" (almost) + "Eve" (evening): a naive person believes that the world is as innocent as a quiet nigh eve, without the harsh realities that exist.
hinglish: "Na" (no) + "Eve" (शाम): ek naadan insaan ko lagta hai ki uski shaam kabhi na ho, woh duniya ko itna bholapan se dekhta hai.

meaning: excessive interest in oneself and one's physical appearance
mnemonic: "Narcissus" (a flower) + "-ism" (condition): a person’s love for themselves is like a Narcissus flower, forever looking at their own reflection in the water, embodying narcissism.
hinglish: "Narcissus" (phool) + "-ism" (bimari): ek aadmi jo sirf apne aap ko dekhta hai, wo Narcissus phool ki tarah apni hi tasveer mein khoya rehta hai, isliye uski narcissism hai.

meaning: just coming into existence; in the early stages of development
mnemonic: Nass + Cent: think of a birth announcement where a 'nass' (new) baby is celebrated with a 'cent' (one hundred) balloons, illustrating that it is nascent and just beginning.
hinglish: Naseem + Chantu: Naseem ka ek naye idea hai jo abhi 'Chantu' ki tarah shuru ho raha hai, yani nascent hai.

meaning: failing to take proper care in doing something
mnemonic: "Neglect" + "Gent": if a gentleman is negligent, he might neglect his duties and responsibilities, leading to trouble.
hinglish: "Neglect" + "Gent": agar ek gentleman laaparwah hai, toh wo apni duties ko neglect karega, jo pareshani ka sabab ban sakta hai.

meaning: a beginner or novice in a particular field or activity
mnemonic: Neo + Phyte: think of 'Neo' (new) in The Matrix, who was a neophyte learning to navigate the complex world of the Matrix.
hinglish: Neo + Phyte: jaise 'Neo' (naya) Matrix me thoda neophyte tha, waise hi naye log kisi bhi kshetra me neophyte hote hain.

meaning: causing annoyance or difficulty
mnemonic: Nettle -> Net + El: imagine a fisherman casting a net to catch an eel, but the eel is nettlesome and keeps slipping away, causing frustration.
hinglish: Nettle + Net: socho ek machhuara jaal se eel pakadne ki koshish kar raha hai, lekin eel itna chanchal hai ki jaal se bachkar jaata hai, yeh nettlesome hai.

meaning: to counteract or make ineffective
mnemonic: Neutral + Eyes: when you neutralize something, it's like closing your eyes to avoid bias — you make things fair and even.
hinglish: Neutral + Aankhein: jab aap kuch neutralize karte hain, toh aap aankhein band karke bias se door rehne ki koshish karte hain — sab kuch barabar kar dete hain.

meaning: quick and light in movement or action
mnemonic: Nimble -> Nimbly Able: someone who is nimble can move nimbly and easily, like a skilled dancer.
hinglish: Nimble -> Nimbly Able: jo log nimble hote hain, wo nimbly aur aasani se harkat karte hain, jaise ek achhe dancer.

meaning: having high moral qualities or ideals
mnemonic: "Noble" -> "Noble is a table": a noble person may be as solid and strong as a noble table that supports others with dignity; thus, exhibiting noble qualities.
hinglish: "Noble" -> "Noble hai ek table": ek noble aadmi ek majboot table ki tarah hota hai jo doosron ki madad karta hai, isliye uska vyavhaar noble hota hai.

meaning: existing in name only; not substantial
mnemonic: "Nom" (name) + "Inal" (like 'inal' in 'final'): a nominal amount is just a name, not the real deal, like someone being a nominal leader with no real power.
hinglish: "Naam" (name) + "Maatra" (only): nominal leader ka matlab hai ki sirf naam ka leader hai, asli had nahi hai.

meaning: calm and relaxed, not displaying anxiety or enthusiasm
mnemonic: "Non" (not) + "Chalant" (challenging): not challenging any situation, he appeared utterly nonchalant about the impending exam.
hinglish: "Non" (na) + "Chalant" (tension): usne exam ke tension ko na samajhte hue bilkul nonchalant rehne ka faisla kiya.

meaning: bewildered or unsure how to react
mnemonic: Non + Plussed: if you are 'non' + 'plussed' (which sounds like 'plus'), you are left without any positive reaction and feel bewildered — he was nonplussed when he heard the news.
hinglish: Non + Plus: jab kisi ko koi aisi baat samajh nahi aati, usse 'non plus' hota hai — woh announcement sun kar aisa hi nonplussed ho gaya.

meaning: harmful or destructive to living beings
mnemonic: Noxious ->
hinglish: Noxious + Toxic: noxious dhuwain aise hain jo insano aur paryavaran ko nuqsan pohanchati hain.

meaning: to make null or void; to invalidate
mnemonic: Null + Ify: when you nullify something, you make it null and void, just like adding 'if' can change a condition and nullify its effect.
hinglish: Null + Ify: jab aap kisi cheez ko nullify karte hain, to aap usse shoonya aur bekaar bana dete hain, jaise 'if' daalne se condition badal jaati hai.

meaning: having a spiritual or supernatural quality
mnemonic: "New Minus" -> "New Minus Potential": when you feel the numinous presence of a divine force, it feels like your troubles become insignificant, or 'new minus' in weight.
hinglish: "Numa" (नम) + "Nus" (नस): जब आप किसी पवित्र स्थान पर जाते हैं, तो वहाँ की नुमिनस (आध्यात्मिक) अनुभूति आपको नम और शांत कर देती है।

meaning: stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action
mnemonic: "Obstinate" + "Durable": someone who is obdurate is as stubborn as they come, standing firm like a durable wall against persuasion.
hinglish: "Ab" + "Dur": jab aap kisi cheez par 'ab' (now) zaroori taur par 'dur' (far) ho jate hain, toh aap obdurate ban jate hain.

meaning: a gesture of respect or obedience
mnemonic: Obey +
hinglish: Obey +

meaning: to deliberately make something unclear or difficult to understand
mnemonic: "Obvious" + "Fate": if you try to make the obvious fate unclear, you obfuscate the truth. — The politician's speech was filled with vague statements that seemed designed to obfuscate the real issues.
hinglish: "Obvious" + "Fate": agar aap obvious kismat ko chhupane ki koshish karte hain, toh aap sachai ko obfuscate karte hain. — Uski baatein itni complex thi ki unhone sabko confuse kar diya, aur woh apne maksad ko obfuscate kar raha tha.

meaning: a harsh reprimand or scolding
mnemonic: Object + Urge: when you object to someone's behavior, you may feel an urge to give them an objurgation about it.
hinglish: Object + Urge: jab aap kisi cheez par object karte hain, to aapko us par kadi fٹkar dene ka urge hota hai.

meaning: unaware or unconcerned about what is happening around one
mnemonic: Oblivious -> 'Oblivious' + 'Li' (like): when you're so lost in your own thoughts, you're oblivious to what's actually happening, like living in a dreamy 'li' land.
hinglish: Oblivious -> 'Obli' (oblique) + 'Vious' (views): jab aap apne hi vichar mein kho jaate hain, tab aap oblivious hote hain, aur doosron ke views ko nahi dekh paate.

meaning: not clearly expressed or easily understood
mnemonic: "Obscure" -> "Obscured Cure": when a medical condition is not clearly diagnosed, the cure remains obscure, leaving patients confused.
hinglish: "Obscure" -> "Obscure Cure": jab ek bimari ka ilaaj clearly nahi pata hota, toh wo obscure reh jata hai aur patients pareshan hote hain.

meaning: excessively obedient or attentive to an excessive degree
mnemonic: "Obey" + "Sequious" (following): the assistant's obsequious behavior made it seem like he was always trying to obey and follow his boss's every whim.
hinglish: "O" (Oh) + "Sequel" (follow-up): uski obsequious baatein sun kar mujhe laga jaise woh sirf apne boss ka follow-up kar raha hai, chahe woh galat hi kyun na ho.

meaning: no longer in use or no longer useful
mnemonic: "Ob" (no) + "solete" (solitary): when something is no longer used, it stands alone and is considered obsolete.
hinglish: "Ob" (nahi) + "solete" (akeli): jab koi cheez istemal nahi hoti, toh woh akeli reh jaati hai aur obsolete ban jaati hai.

meaning: stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or chosen course of action
mnemonic: "Obstinate" -> "Obstacle in A State": when someone is obstinate, they become an obstacle, firmly standing in a state of refusal to change.
hinglish: "Obstinate" -> "Haalat Mein" (in a state): jab koi aadmi haalaton mein ziddi ho jata hai, toh woh obstinate kehlata hai.

meaning: noisy and difficult to control
mnemonic: 'Obstetrician' + 'Reckless': an obstetrician may find her patients obstreperous when they are loud and unmanageable during childbirth — just like obstreperous behavior in general.
hinglish: 'Obstetrician' + 'Reckless': ek obstetrician ko uski patients shor machate hue obstreperous lagte hain jab ve childbirth ke dauran beqarar hoti hain.

meaning: to prevent or make unnecessary
mnemonic: Obvious + Viate (way): if something is obvious, it helps to obviate the need for an alternate way or solution, thus simplifying the situation.
hinglish: Obvious + Raste: agar kuch obvious hai, to yeh dusre raste ko talne me madad karta hai, isliye hum obviate karte hain.

meaning: to block or close off
mnemonic: O + Clue: if you take away the 'clue,' you occlude the truth, hiding the answer.
hinglish: O + Clue: agar aap 'clue' hata dete hain, to aap sachai ko occlude kar rahe hain, matlab chupaa rahe hain.

meaning: extremely unpleasant or repulsive
mnemonic: "Oh, dear!" + "This is odious!": When someone finds something extremely unpleasant, they might exclaim, 'Oh, dear!' because it is truly odious.
hinglish: "Oh dear!" + "Ye kitna naapasand hai!": Jab koi cheez bohot hi naapasand hoti hai, to wo kehta hai, 'Oh dear!' kyunki ye odious hai.

meaning: excessively eager to offer help or advice, often in an annoying way
mnemonic: Office + Us: the officious coworker always acts like he knows everything and butts into everyone else's work discussions, making it feel like he’s running the office for us.
hinglish: Office + Aas: woh dosto ki baaton mein zyada dakhhal deta hai jaise wo office ke liye aas (help) kar raha ho.

meaning: giving the impression that something bad or unpleasant is going to happen
mnemonic: "Ominous" -> "Oh Minos": Oh Minos, the mythical king who presided over the underworld, was often associated with ominous signs of doom.
hinglish: "Oh Minos" (ओ मीनोस) + "Ominous": ओ मीनोस के बारे में कहा जाता है कि वह खतरनाक संकेतों से भरा था, जो बुराई का संकेत देते हैं।

meaning: to leave out or exclude something
mnemonic: "Oh Mit" (oh, miss it): if you forget to mention something, you might say, 'Oh Mit, I forgot to include that point!'
hinglish: "Oh Mit" (oh, miss it): agar aapne kisi zaroori baat ko chhod diya, toh aap kahenge, 'Oh Mit, main yeh point include karna bhool gaya!'

meaning: present everywhere at the same time
mnemonic: "Omni" (all) + "Present" (here): if something is omnipresent, it means it is present everywhere, like the air we breathe.
hinglish: "Omni" (sab) + "Present" (yahan): agar koi cheez omnipresent hai, to iska matlab hai ki wo har jagah maujood hai, jaise hawa.

meaning: having complete or unlimited knowledge
mnemonic: Omni + Scient: 'Omni' means all and 'scient' relates to knowledge; the omniscient narrator knows everything about the plot and characters.
hinglish: Omni + Science: 'Omni' sab kuch aur 'Science' gyaan; ek omniscient narrator sab kuch jaanata hai kahani ke baare mein.

meaning: burdensome; involving a lot of effort or difficulty
mnemonic: Oni + rus (Oni sounds like 'oh no' + rus like 'rusty'): When faced with an onerous job, you might say, 'Oh no, this task is as heavy as rusty old machinery!'
hinglish: Oh no + Rus: Jab kisi kaam ko dekh kar aap keh rahe ho 'Oh no', toh wo kaam kafi onerous hota hai.

meaning: happening or existing only once
mnemonic: One + Time: think of a special event that occurs only one time in your life, like a onetime concert.
hinglish: One + Time: socho ek aisa event jo sirf ek baar hota hai, jaise ek onetime show.

meaning: not able to be seen through; not transparent
mnemonic: Opaque -> 'Oh! Pake': Imagine someone saying 'Oh! Pake!' in surprise when they realize the glass is so thick and opaque that they cannot see through it.
hinglish: Oh! Pake: Jab kisi ne dekha ki glass itna 'oh! pake' hai ki wo dekhtay nahi hai, to wo opaque hai.

meaning: taking advantage of opportunities as they arise, often in a self-serving way
mnemonic: Opportunity + Mystic: an opportunistic person sees every opportunity like a mystic sees the future — he exploits them for personal gain.
hinglish: Opportunity + Mystic: ek opportunistic aadmi har opportunity ko jaise ek mystic bhavishya ko dekhta hai — voh unhein apne faayde ke liye istemal karta hai.

meaning: public disgrace or shame
mnemonic: Oppropriate + Reprimand: if you appropriately reprimand someone, you may face opprobrium from others who disagree.
hinglish: Khal + Ang: jab logon ko koi khilaaf bolta hai, to unhe uska khalang milta hai, yaani opprobrium.

meaning: elaborately decorated
mnemonic: "Ornate" -> "Ornament": the palace was so beautifully decorated like an ornament that it was considered ornate.
hinglish: "Ornament" (sajawat) + "Ate" (khaas): woh mahal itna sajawat se bhara hua tha ki usay ornate kehna sahi hai.

meaning: to turn into bone or bony tissue; to become rigid or fixed in a certain way
mnemonic: "Oss" (like 'ossuary' which means a container for bones) + "ify" (to make): when ideas ossify, they become as rigid as bone, losing their flexibility.
hinglish: "Oss" (jaise 'ossuary' jo haddi rakhne ke liye hota hai) + "ify" (banana): jab vichar ossify hote hain, toh ve haddi ki tarah sakht ho jaate hain, apni lachilapan kho dete hain.

meaning: characterized by vulgar or pretentious display; designed to impress or attract notice
mnemonic: "Osten" + "Tate": when you 'ostentatiously' decorate a room, it feels like you are trying to 'tate' (show off) your wealth; the room was so flashy and over-the-top.
hinglish: "Osten" + "Tate": jab aap kisi cheez ko ostentatiously sajate hain, toh aisa lagta hai jaise aap apni daulat dikhane ki koshish kar rahe hain; us ghar ki sajawat bahut hi dikhawe wali thi.

meaning: to expel or remove from a position or place
mnemonic: Oust -> 'Out' + 'Dust': when you oust someone, you kick them out like dust from a room, making it empty again.
hinglish: Out + Dust: jab aap kisi ko oust karte hain, toh aap usay bahar nikaal dete hain jaise dust ko sweep karke bahar nikaal dete hain.

meaning: bizarre or extremely unconventional
mnemonic: "Out" + "Land" + "Dish": imagine someone serving a dish from a bizarre, faraway land that seems completely outlandish; that’s how weird her outfit was.
hinglish: "Out" + "Land" + "Dish": socho koi aisa dish le aaye jo bilkul ajeeb aur alag ho; waise hi uska outfit outlandish tha.

meaning: to surpass or exceed in performance or achievement
mnemonic: Out + Strip: when you outstrip someone, you 'strip' away their chance to win, leaving you ahead.
hinglish: Out + Strip: jab aap kisi se aage nikal jaate hain, toh aap unka mauka 'strip' kar dete hain, jaise aap aage hain.

meaning: open and observable; not hidden or concealed
mnemonic: Overt -> 'Over' + 'T': when something is over and above the surface, it is overt; you can see it clearly.
hinglish: Over + T: jab kisi cheez ka dikhai dena zyada ho, wo overt hota hai; jaise uski overt enthusiasm sabko impress karti hai.

meaning: to calm or soothe someone who is angry or agitated
mnemonic: Pacify -> 'Paci' (Like 'Paci' in pacifier) + 'fy' (to make): the act of making someone calm, like using a pacifier to pacify a crying baby.
hinglish: Paci + fy: jab chhote bachche ro rahe hote hain, toh unko 'paci' dekar hum unhe 'pacify' karte hain.

meaning: requiring considerable effort and attention to detail
mnemonic: Pain + Taking: taking pain to get the details right means doing painstaking work.
hinglish: Pain + Taking: detail sahi karne ke liye agar aapko dard uthana padta hai, toh aapka kaam painstaking hai.

meaning: able to be touched or felt; easily perceptible
mnemonic: Pal + Pable: if something is 'palpable', it is so obvious that your friend (pal) could feel it without touching; the fear in the air was palpable.
hinglish: Pal + Pable: agar koi cheez 'palpable' hai, toh woh itni spashth hai ki aapke dost (pal) ko woh bina chhuye mehsoos ho sakti hai; uss waqt ka tension palpable tha.

meaning: of little value; insignificant
mnemonic: Pall + Tree: if you saw a paltry tree, you would think it's like a tree that barely grows and has no value, symbolizing insignificance.
hinglish: Pal + Tree: ek paltry (न्यूनतम मूल्य का) tree dekhta hai jo khud mein koi maayne nahi rakhta, yani bahut hi kamzor hai.

meaning: a remedy for all difficulties or diseases
mnemonic: Pan + Asea: a 'pan' full of 'sea' water might seem like a cure-all for hydration, but it's not; just like a panacea isn't a real solution for every problem.
hinglish: Pan + Asea: 'pan' mein 'sea' paani bhara ho, toh wo har bimari ka ilaaj nahi hai; waise hi panacea har samasya ka hal nahi.

meaning: flamboyant confidence or style
mnemonic: Pan + Ash: like a pan that shines brightly with a plume of ash, panache adds flair and confidence to one's presence.
hinglish: Pan + Aash: jaise ek pan aash se chamakta hai, waise panache kisi ki shaan aur atma-vishwas ko dikhata hai.

meaning: serving as a typical example or model
mnemonic: "Para" (for) + "Digmatic" (dogmatic): when something is paradigmatic, it is a dogmatic standard or model for others to follow, just like a guidebook.
hinglish: "Para" (ke liye) + "Dheekmatic" (theek hai): jab koi cheez paradigmatic hoti hai, toh woh ek theek hai, ek udaharan ke roop mein samjhi jaati hai.

meaning: a situation or statement that seems contradictory or opposed to common sense but may still be true
mnemonic: Para + Doxical: 'Para' (against) + 'Doxical' (opinion) — a paradoxical statement goes against common opinion.
hinglish: Para + Doxical: 'Para' (virudh) + 'Doxical' (raay) — ek paradoxical baat aam raay ke virudh hoti hai.

meaning: a model of excellence or perfection
mnemonic: Para + Gone: if a paragon is present, all the flaws are gone, showcasing excellence.
hinglish: Para + Gone: agar paragon hai, toh sab khamiyaan chali gayi hain, ek uttam udaharan dikhata hai.

meaning: limited in scope or outlook; narrow-minded
mnemonic: "Para" (for) + "Occasional" (few): If your thoughts are only occasional and for a small group, they are parochial and narrow.
hinglish: "Par" (for) + "Kiya" (done): Jab aap sirf choti si duniya ke liye sochte hain, toh aapka sochna parochial ho jaata hai.

meaning: excessively frugal or stingy
mnemonic: Parse + Money: when you parse your money too tightly, you become parsimonious and unwilling to spend.
hinglish: Parse + Money: jab aap apne paise ko itna parse karte hain ki kharch karne se katrate hain, tab aap parsimonious ho jaate hain.

meaning: not complete; existing only in part
mnemonic: "Part" + "Shall": if you only cover a part of the task, it shall be considered partial work, not complete.
hinglish: "Part" + "Shall": agar aap sirf kuch part karte hain, toh woh kaam partial hoga, poora nahi.

meaning: acceptable but not outstanding
mnemonic: "Pass" + "Able": even if something is only able to pass, it means it is passable and just good enough. — The exam was passable, allowing the student to move on.
hinglish: "Pass" + "Able": agar kuch sirf pass hone layak hai, toh voh passable hai. — Uska project passable tha, par hamne behtar ummeed ki thi.

meaning: not active; accepting or allowing what happens without taking action
mnemonic: "Pass" + "Sieve": when you pass through a sieve, you let things fall through without any action — just like being passive means not taking action.
hinglish: "Pass" + "Sieve": jab aap chhalni se kuch pass karte hain, toh aap bina kuch kiye cheezein girne dete hain — waise hi passive hone ka matlab hai bina action liye rehna.

meaning: a work that imitates the style of other works, often as a form of satire or homage
mnemonic: Past + Yeast: think of a baker who uses past recipes with yeast to create a new loaf — a pastiche combines different styles to create something new.
hinglish: Past + Yeast: ek baker purani recipes ka istemal karta hai jo yeast se nayi roti banata hai — pastiche alag-alag styles ko milaakar kuch naya banata hai.

meaning: a government authority or legal document granting exclusive rights to an invention or idea
mnemonic: "Patent" -> "Pay Tent": paying for a tent grants you exclusive rights to use it, similar to how a patent secures rights to an invention.
hinglish: "Pay" + "Tent": tent ke liye paise dene se tumhe uska istemal karne ka hak milta hai, jaise patent tumhare invention ka hak deta hai.

meaning: to treat others as if they are less intelligent or knowledgeable
mnemonic: Patron + Eyes: when you patronize someone, it's as if you look at them with patronizing eyes, signaling you see them as lesser.
hinglish: Patron + Aankhein: jab aap kisi ko patronize karte hain, tab aap unhe patron ki tarah aankhein dikhaate hain, jaise ki aap unse behtar hain.

meaning: a minor fault or sin
mnemonic: "Peck" (to lightly tap) + "a dillo" (like a small animal): a small tap of a fault, a peccadillo is merely a minor fault in someone.
hinglish: "Pick" (choosing) + "a dillo" (like a small error): jab aap koi choti si galti karte hain, wo ek peccadillo hota hai.

meaning: having distinctive or unusual characteristics
mnemonic: "Peculiar" -> "Pick a Lure": if you pick a lure that looks strange, it might attract unusual fish — just like something peculiar attracts attention.
hinglish: "Peculiar" -> "Pick a Lure": agar aap ek ajeeb sa lure pick karte hain, toh woh strange machhliyon ko attract kar sakta hai — jaise koi peculiar cheez sabka dhyan kheech leti hai.

meaning: excessively concerned with minor details or rules; overly academic
hindi: बड़ी बारीकी से नियमों का पालन करना
mnemonic: Pedant -> 'Pedal Ant': imagine an ant that keeps adjusting the pedals of a bicycle to perfection, illustrating a pedantic nature that focuses too much on details.
hinglish: Pedant + Ant: ek pedant ke choti-choti baaton par focus karne wale ke tarah, wo har cheez ko sahi karne ki koshish karta hai.

meaning: lacking excitement or uniqueness; dull
mnemonic: "Pedestrian" -> "Pedestal + In": If something is placed on a pedestal, it should stand out, but a pedestrian design is just too ordinary to be elevated.
hinglish: "Pedestrian" -> "Ped + Dastaan": Ek pedestrian kahani wo hai jo bina jadoo ya excitement ke hai — it’s just a simple story.

meaning: a word or phrase that has negative connotations or is derogatory
mnemonic: "Pea" + "Joke": calling someone a 'pea brain' is a pejorative that insults their intelligence.
hinglish: "Pea" + "Joke": 'pea brain' kehna ek pejorative hai jo kisi ki samajh ko neecha dikhata hai.

meaning: translucently clear; easily understood
mnemonic: "Pell" + "Lucid": if you are feeling like a 'pell', your thoughts should be 'lucid' and clear; thus, a presentation is pellucid when it is easy to understand.
hinglish: "Pell" + "Spasht": agar koi cheez 'pell' hai, to wo 'spasht' hai; isliye teacher ne 'pellucid' tarike se samjhaya.

meaning: a strong liking or inclination towards something
mnemonic: Pen + Chant: imagine someone who loves to write with a pen and chant lyrics — she has a penchant for songwriting.
hinglish: Pen + Chant: wo pen se likhne aur gaane ka shauk rakhti hai — isliye uska jhukav music ki taraf hai.

meaning: having the ability to reach or affect deeply
mnemonic: "Pen" + "etrating": Imagine a pen drilling deep into paper to leave a mark; her penetrating questions dug deep into the topic.
hinglish: "Pen" + "etrating": Jaise ek pen kaghaz mein gehra chura kar chhoot jata hai; uski penetrating sawaalon ne topic ko gehra kiya.

meaning: engaged in deep or serious thought
mnemonic: "Pence" + "Sieve": When you think of 'pensive', imagine counting pence through a sieve, deeply lost in thought about money — that's how pensive she looked.
hinglish: "Paisa" + "See": Jab aap paisa dekh rahe hote hain aur bahut ghamgeen hote hain, toh aap pensive hote hain.

meaning: extremely poor; lacking the necessities of life
mnemonic: "Pen" + "Urious" (like 'pen you are us'): if you have only a pen and no money (penurious), you must be extremely poor.
hinglish: "Pen" + "Urious": agar sirf ek pen hai, baaki sab kuch nahi hai, toh aap penurious hain.

meaning: lasting for a long time or indefinitely
mnemonic: Perennial -> 'Perennial Plant': many plants are perennial, meaning they return year after year without needing to be replanted.
hinglish: Perennial + 'Plant': kai paudhe aise hote hain jo har saal aate hain, jaise yeh perennial paudhe.

meaning: deceitfulness; untrustworthiness
mnemonic: "Per" (through) + "Fid" (faith): when you go through someone's faith and betray them, it shows your perfidy.
hinglish: "Per" (par) + "Fid" (vishwas): jab aap kisi ke vishwas par par jate hain aur dhoka dete hain, to ye aapki perfidy hai.

meaning: done without care or enthusiasm
mnemonic: "Perfun" + "Factory" (a place where things are made): when tasks are done in a perfunctory manner, they are like mass-produced items in a factory, made without passion or detail.
