hinglish: "Per" + "Fun" (बिना मजे के): jab koi kaam bina maza aur interest ke kiya jata hai, wo perfunctory hota hai.

meaning: full of danger or risk
mnemonic: "Peril" + "Us": when a situation is perilous, it puts us at risk of danger. — Many explorers have found themselves in perilous situations while seeking new routes.
hinglish: "Peril" + "Hamara": jab koi haalat khatarnaak hoti hai, to wo hamara khatra badhati hai. — Bahut saare yatrai khatarnaak haalon mein padte hain jab naye raste talashte hain.

meaning: related to or located on the edge or periphery.
mnemonic: "Periphery" -> "Periphery Elly": Imagine a girl named Elly who only pays attention to the peripheral things around her, missing out on the main events.
hinglish: "Peri" + "Feri": jab aap periphery ki cheezein dekhte hain, aap sirf khud ke aas-paas hoti hain, jaise aapki aankhein periphery par hain.

meaning: having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way
mnemonic: Pernicious -> 'Per' (through) + 'Nicious' (noxious): something that spreads harmful effects through its subtle presence, like a pernicious influence in your life.
hinglish: Per + Nicious: koi cheez jo dheere dheere aapki zindagi ko kharab kar rahi hai, jaise pernicious vikas.

meaning: to carry out or commit a harmful, illegal, or immoral act
mnemonic: Perpetrate -> 'Perpetual' + 'Trait': a perpetual trait of a criminal is to perpetrate crimes without remorse.
hinglish: Perpetrate -> 'Per' + 'Patrate': jab koi 'per' kehti hai ki wo 'patrate' se crime karega, wo actually crime ko perpetrate kar raha hai.

meaning: to cause something to continue indefinitely
mnemonic: Perpetual -> Perpetuate: when you make something perpetual, you cause it to last forever, just like how they perpetuate the founder's legacy.
hinglish: Perpetual + Patta: jab aap kuch cheezon ko perpetual banaate hain, jaise ki unka patta ya legacy, to aap unhe hamesha zinda rakhte hain.

meaning: the quality of continuing steadily despite problems or difficulties
mnemonic: Persevere + Announce: when you persevere, you announce your determination to keep going despite challenges.
hinglish: Persevere + Announce: jab aap persevere karte hain, toh aap apni mehnat ko announce karte hain, chahe kitni bhi mushkil ho.

meaning: having a ready insight into and understanding of things
mnemonic: "Per" (through) + "Spicacious" (to look): to look through a situation with clarity and insight, just like a perspicacious person does.
hinglish: "Par" (but) + "Spika" (to see): par ye samajhna ki kahan pe dikkat hai, wo hota hai perspicacious.

meaning: holding firmly to an opinion or a course of action
mnemonic: Pertinacious ->
hinglish: Pertinacious ->

meaning: relevant or applicable to a particular matter
mnemonic: "Pert" + "In" + "Ent": if you are part of the 'pert' team, your ideas must be pertinent to succeed.
hinglish: "Pert" (संबंधित) + "In" (में) + "Ent": agar aap kisi pert team ka hissa hai, toh aapke vichar wahin 'pertinent' hone chahiye.

meaning: spreading widely throughout an area or a group of people
mnemonic: Per + Vase: think of a vase filled with water that seeps into every corner of a table — the pervasive nature of the liquid spreads everywhere.
hinglish: Per + Vase: ek vase mein paani hai jo har jagah fail jaata hai — yahi pervasive cheez har jagah hoti hai.

meaning: easily irritated or annoyed
mnemonic: "Pet" + "Ulant": if you don't pet a cat, it may become petulant and scratch you. — Her petulant behavior meant she often lashed out when she felt ignored.
hinglish: "Pet" + "Ulat": agar aapne billi ko pet nahi kiya, to woh chidh jaayegi. — Uska chidhchidhapan aisa tha ki dosto ko uske sath waqt bitana mushkil ho gaya.

meaning: a person who is indifferent to culture and the arts
hindi: संस्कृति और कला के प्रति उदासीन व्यक्ति
mnemonic: "Phil" + "is" + "teen": A teen named Phil who prefers video games over art is a philistine, showing indifference to culture.
hinglish: "Phil" + "is" + "teen": Phil ek teen hai jo art se zyada video games ko pasand karta hai, aur isliye wo philistine hai.

meaning: having a calm, sluggish temperament; not easily excited or animated
mnemonic: "Fleg" (fled) + "matic" (automatic): someone who fled the scene remains automatic and calm, like a phlegmatic person.
hinglish: "Fleg" (bhag gaya) + "matic" (automatic): jo insaan bhag gaya hai, wo phlegmatic ki tarah automatic aur shaant rehta hai.

meaning: not genuine; fraudulent or deceptive
mnemonic: "Phone-y" -> "Faux on the Phone": he was always pretending to be someone else on the phone, creating a phony persona.
hinglish: "Phone-y" -> "Phone pe Nakli": uska phone pe nakli personality kisi ko bhi bekaar laga.

meaning: visually attractive, especially in a quaint or charming way
mnemonic: Picture + Esque: If something looks like a picture, it must be picturesque, capturing beauty in every angle.
hinglish: Picture + Esque: Jab koi jagah picture ki tarah sundar hoti hai, tab wo picturesque kehlaati hai.

meaning: devoutly religious
mnemonic: "Pie" + "Us": when we share a pie with pious people, they remind us to be grateful and share with others, reflecting their devout nature.
hinglish: "Pie" + "Hum": jab hum pious logon ke saath pie share karte hain, toh woh hamesha humein dharmik hone ki yaad dilate hain.

meaning: having a pleasantly sharp taste or appetizing flavor
mnemonic: Piquant -> 'Peak Want': like a peak of a mountain, the flavor reaches its highest point, creating a piquant taste that excites the palate.
hinglish: Piquant -> 'Pee + Want': jab aap kisike khane ka pee chahe, toh wo piquant hota hai kyunki wo taste mein teekha aur flavorful hota hai.

meaning: concise and forcefully expressive
mnemonic: "Pith" (core) + "y" (like): when something is pithy, it gets to the core of the matter quickly and effectively, just like a pithy joke that is funny in few words.
hinglish: "Pith" (gahrayi) + "y": jab kuch pithy hota hai, woh baat ki gahrayi tak jaldi aur asar daari se pohanchta hai, jaise ek pithy joke jo kam shabdon mein hasi laata hai.

meaning: to calm someone down or pacify them
mnemonic: "Place" + "Late": if you place an order too late, you might need to placate an upset customer.
hinglish: "Place" + "Late": agar aap order place karne mein late ho jaate hain, toh aapko upset customer ko placate karna padega.

meaning: calm and peaceful
mnemonic: Place + Sid: imagine a peaceful place where Sid enjoys his tranquil moments, illustrating how placid means calm and undisturbed.
hinglish: Place + Sid: socho ek aisi jagah jahan Sid bahut shant hai, yeh placid ka matlab hai — shanti aur bechaini se pare.

meaning: expressing sorrow or melancholy
mnemonic: "Plain" + "Tive" (like 'active'): a plain, sad cry is often plaintive, expressing deep sorrow.
hinglish: "Plain" + "Tive": ek plain aur sad awaaz ko 'plaintive' kaha jaata hai, jo dukh vyakt karti hai.

meaning: a synthetic material made from polymers, commonly used in various products
mnemonic: Plastic ->
hinglish: Plas + Tic: plastic cheezein itni tikau hoti hain ki lagta hai yeh hamesha rahegi.

meaning: a trite or overused expression or idea
mnemonic: "Plat" (flat) + "Attitude": a flat attitude often leads to platitudes that sound boring and unoriginal in conversations; his speech was nothing but a collection of platitudes.
hinglish: "Plat" (flat) + "Attitude": agar aapka attitude flat hai, toh aap sirf saade platitudes hi kahenge; unki baatein bas platitude thi.

meaning: likely to be true or plausible
mnemonic: Plausible -> "Pause a Little": when you pause a little to think, you find a reason that seems plausible.
hinglish: Pause + Little: jab aap thoda pause karte hain toh aapko ek samjhaanee bataana aasan lagta hai, jo plausible hoti hai.

meaning: flexible and adaptable; easily bent or influenced
mnemonic: Ply + Ant: imagine that an ant can easily navigate through pliant materials, showcasing how pliant things can bend and move effortlessly.
hinglish: Ply + Aant: socho ek aant lacheela sa kapda lehrata hai, jo pliant hota hai aur asani se bend ho sakta hai.

meaning: moving or acting in a slow, laborious manner
mnemonic: Plod + Ding: when you plod along, it feels like every step is a ding of effort, making every movement slow and labored.
hinglish: Plod + Ding: jab aap dhire-dhire chal rahe hote hain, to har kadam ek ding ki tarah hota hai, yani yeh plodding hai.

meaning: a cunning plan or action designed to turn a situation to one's advantage
mnemonic: Play + Ploy: when you play a game, sometimes you need a ploy to trick your opponents and gain the upper hand.
hinglish: Play + Chal: jab aap kisi game mein khilte hain, toh kabhi kabhi aapko chal (ploy) chalni padti hai apne opponents ko chakar mein daalne ke liye.

meaning: having or showing courage, determination, and spirit
mnemonic: Plucky -> 'Lucky Pluck': a lucky person who has the pluck to take risks shows their pluckiness.
hinglish: Plucky -> 'Luck + Key': jab aapko luck aur courage ka key milta hai, tab aap plucky ho jaate hain.

meaning: evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret
mnemonic: "Point" + "Gant": when you point out something painful, it becomes poignant — the news was so poignant that it struck a chord with everyone.
hinglish: "Point" + "Gant": jab aap kisi dukh bhare baat ko point karte hain, to woh poignant ho jati hai — uski kahani itni poignant thi ki sabko rula diya.

meaning: a state of balance or equilibrium
mnemonic: "Poised" -> "Pose": when you pose gracefully, you show poise, standing tall and balanced even under pressure.
hinglish: "Pose" (अवस्था) + "Is" (है): jab aap kisi tarah se pose karte hain, toh aap poise dikhate hain, hamesha balanced aur confident rehte hain.

meaning: to cause to divide into opposing factions or groups
mnemonic: Polar + Eyes: when you polarize, you create opposing views (like North and South poles) that cause people to see things very differently.
hinglish: Polar + Aankhein: jab aap kisi vishay par polarization karte hain, logon ki aankhein do alag nazariye dekhne lagti hain, jaise North aur South poles.

meaning: controversial or argumentative in nature
mnemonic: "Pole" + "Mical" (like 'magical'): in a polemical discussion, words can feel like weapons in a magical battle of ideas, where every point is contested.
hinglish: "Pole" + "Mical": ek polemical discussion me, har baat ek dusre ke khilaf hoti hai, jaise ek jadoo ki ladaai.

meaning: a person with knowledge in multiple fields
mnemonic: Poly -> 'Polly' + Math: imagine a parrot named Polly who knows math, showcasing her polymath abilities by solving complex equations.
hinglish: Poly -> 'Polly' + Math: socho ek parrot hai jiska naam Polly hai jo math kar sakti hai, yeh uski polymath qualities dikhata hai.

meaning: excessive self-importance or arrogance
mnemonic: "Pompeii" + "City": the city of Pompeii was known for its grandeur, but the pomposity of its citizens made them less likable; they thought too highly of themselves.
hinglish: "Pomp" + "City": jab kisi sheher mein sab log sirf apne aap ko bada samajhte hain, toh woh pomposity ka udaharan hai.

meaning: heavy, awkward, and slow-moving
mnemonic: Pond + Er + Us: Imagine a pond so heavy with mud that it becomes ponderous and hard to cross.
hinglish: Pond + Er + Us: Jab ek ganda pond itna bhari ho jaye ki uska paar karna mushkil ho, tab wo ponderous kehlata hai.

meaning: to be a sign or warning that something is likely to happen
mnemonic: Port + End: if you see a port at the end of your journey, it may portend a safe arrival or trouble ahead; thus, it becomes a sign of what’s to come.
hinglish: Port + End: agar aap kisi port par jaa rahe hain, ye portend karta hai ki aapka safar khatam hone wala hai — ek sanket hai ki aap ghar aa rahe hain.

meaning: the act of behaving in a way to impress or mislead others, often through exaggerated gestures or poses
mnemonic: Post + Urge: when someone has a strong urge to impress, they often resort to posturing to appear more important.
hinglish: Post + Urge: jab kisi ko impress karne ki taqat hoti hai, toh wo aksar posturing karta hai taaki wo zyada important lage.

meaning: having a strong effect or influence
mnemonic: Pot + Tent: a tent made of strong material can withstand powerful storms, making it potent against harsh weather.
hinglish: Pot + Tent: ek strong tent har tarah ke mausam ka samna kar sakti hai, isliye wo potent hoti hai.

meaning: not securely held or in position; dangerously likely to fall or collapse
mnemonic: Pre + Carious (curious): if you’re curious about climbing a precarious ledge, that’s dangerous and could lead to a fall.
hinglish: Pre + Kharab: agar tum kisi precarious situation mein ho, to bahut kharab ho sakta hai.

meaning: to cause something to happen suddenly or prematurely
mnemonic: Pre + Sip + Itate: when you sip something too quickly, it can precipitate a spill all over your clothes.
hinglish: Pre + Sip + Ikate: jab aap paani ko jaldi jaldi pee lenge, to wo aapke haath se gir kar jaldbazi karne jaise spill ho jayega.

meaning: dangerously high or steep
mnemonic: "Pre" (before) + "cipit" (tip): if you stand before the tip of a precipice, it's a dangerously high drop; the precipitious edge is not for the faint-hearted.
hinglish: "Pre" (pehle) + "cipit" (nicha): agar aap ek precipitious cliff ke pehle khade hain, to yeh khatarnak upar hai; yeh precipitious edge bechaini bhari hai.

meaning: to prevent something from happening
mnemonic: Pre + Clue: if you preclude someone from solving a mystery, you take away their clue, making it impossible to find the answer.
hinglish: Pre + Clue: agar aap kisi ko clue nahi dete, to woh kisi chiz ko preclude kar raha hai, jaise kisi paheli ko suljhanay se roknah.

meaning: advanced or mature beyond one's age
mnemonic: "Pre" + "Cocoa" (cocoa typically represents maturity in flavor): A precocious kid is like pre-cocoa, showing maturity in understanding things much before others do.
hinglish: "Pre" + "Cocoa": ek precocious bachcha aise hota hai jaise pre-cocoa, jo dusre bachchon se pehle hi samajhdaari dikhata hai.

meaning: a difficult or challenging situation
mnemonic: Pre + Dick + A + Ment: imagine a guy named Dick who is constantly stuck in a messy situation; thus, he is always in a predicament.
hinglish: Pre + Dikkat + Ment: jab aapko kisi mushkil mein padna padta hai, tab aapko dikkat hoti hai, jo aapki predicament hoti hai.

meaning: a preference or special liking for something
mnemonic: Pre + Dilection: having a pre-existing liking, she had a predilection for chocolate desserts over any other sweet.
hinglish: Pre + Dilection: uski pehle se hi pasand thi, isliye uska chocolate desserts ke liye predilection tha.

meaning: to suggest or represent beforehand
mnemonic: Pre + Figure: if you 'pre' (before) 'figure' (represent), you can prefigure what will happen later.
hinglish: Pehle + Chitra: agar aap 'pehle' (before) 'chitra' (figure) banate ho, toh aap us cheez ka 'prefigure' kar rahe ho.

meaning: to think out or plan an action beforehand, especially a crime
mnemonic: "Pre" (before) + "Meditate" (to think): when you premeditate, you think about an action beforehand, like planning a test strategy days before the exam.
hinglish: "Pehle" (before) + "Meditate" (sochna): jab aap premeditate karte hain, toh aap kisi kaam ko pehle se soch kar tayyar karte hain jaise kisi exam ke liye pehle se tayyari karna.

meaning: to predict or foretell a future event
mnemonic: Pre + Sage: a wise old sage can often presage future events, predicting what is to come.
hinglish: Pre + Sage: ek budhi aaj ke din ki baatein sunke kal ka sab kuch pre-sage kar sakta hai.

meaning: having or showing knowledge of events before they take place
mnemonic: "Pre" (before) + "scient" (science): having a scientific knowledge that allows one to foresee events — her prescient understanding of future trends helped her succeed.
hinglish: "Pre" (pehle) + "scient" (vigyaan): aise vigyaan se jo kisi cheez ka pehle se hi pata de, uski prescient soch ne use samay se aage badh diya.

meaning: to recommend a treatment or medication
mnemonic: "Press + Scribe": when you press a doctor, they will write you a prescription; thus, to prescribe means to recommend a treatment.
hinglish: "Press + Karo + Scribe": jab aap doctor ko press karte hain, woh aapke liye dawa likhte hain, isliye prescribe ka matlab hai kisi treatment ko recommend karna.

meaning: overstepping due bounds; taking liberties
mnemonic: "Presume" -> "Presume to Jump": when you presume too much, you jump to conclusions without thinking; his presumptuous comments showed a lack of respect.
hinglish: "Presume" + "Jump": jab aap kisi cheez ko bina soche samjhe assume karte hain, toh aap kehte hain ki aap presumptuous hain, jaise usne bina puchhe hi sab kuch keh diya.

meaning: attempting to impress by affecting greater importance or merit than is actually possessed
mnemonic: Pretend + Tious: When someone is pretentious, they are pretending to be something they are not, showing off qualities or achievements that they do not truly possess.
hinglish: Pretend + Tious: Jab koi aisa dikhawa karta hai ki wo kuch khaas hai, wo pretentious hai.

meaning: to prove more powerful or superior; to win or succeed
mnemonic: Pre + Veil: If you 'pre'pare well, you can 'veil' (cover) your fears and prevail in any situation.
hinglish: Pre + Veil: Agar aap 'pre' preparation karte hain, toh aap 'veil' (chhupana) kar sakte hain apne darr ko aur jeet sakte hain.

meaning: to speak or act in an evasive way; to lie or mislead
mnemonic: Pre + Varicate: when you pre-emptively vary your story, you prevaricate by avoiding the truth.
hinglish: Pre + Varicate: jab aap pehle se hi apni kahani ko badalte hain, tab aap prevaricate karte hain.

meaning: of the best quality; excellent
mnemonic: Prime -> Prime Cuts: prime refers to high-quality meats, just like prime cuts from a steak are the best available.
hinglish: Prime -> Prime Cuts: prime ka matlab hai behtareen, jaise prime cuts mein sabse achhe tukde hote hain.

meaning: in its original condition; unspoiled or clean
mnemonic: "Pre" (before) + "Scene" (sight): imagine a beautiful scene before it has been touched by pollution — that's a pristine environment.
hinglish: "Pre" (pehle) + "Scene" (manzar): socho ek manzar jo kabhi nahi badla — wahi hai ek pristine jagah.

meaning: the quality of having strong moral principles; honesty and decency
mnemonic: "Pro" (for) + "Bity" (beauty): to be for beauty, one must have probity, as true beauty lies in honesty.
hinglish: "Pro" (sahi) + "Bity" (beauty): agar aap sahi beauty chahte hain, toh aapko probity yani imandari rakhni padegi.

meaning: a natural inclination or tendency towards something
mnemonic: Pro + Clivity (climb): like climbing a slope, you show a proclivity when you tend to lean towards something naturally — she had a proclivity for climbing mountains.
hinglish: Pro + Clivity (kharij hone ki taraf): jab aap kisi cheez ki taraf naturally jhukte hain, to wo aapki proclivity hoti hai — uski adventure ki proclivity ne use har baar naye naye jagah explore karne par majboor kiya.

meaning: characterized by excessive spending or wastefulness
mnemonic: "Prodigy" + "Gull": a prodigal is like a prodigy who fools everyone like a gull, wasting resources instead of saving them — the prodigal wasted all his wealth.
hinglish: "Prodigy" + "Gull": ek prodigal aadmi hai jaise ek prodigy jo sabko behkakar apni daulat kharch kar deta hai — usne apni sampatti barbaad kar di.

meaning: remarkably great in extent, size, or degree
mnemonic: Prodigy + Cious: a prodigious person is as amazing as a prodigy, showcasing extraordinary abilities.
hinglish: Prodigy + Cious: ek prodigious musician itna talented hota hai ki sab uski kala dekh kar hairaan reh jaate hain.

meaning: having a high degree of skill or competence
mnemonic: "Pro" (for) + "Fish" (the fish): if you want to catch fish like a pro, you have to be proficient in fishing techniques.
hinglish: "Pro" (professional) + "Fish" (machhli): agar aap machhli pakadne mein professional banna chahte hain, toh aapko usme proficient hona padega.

meaning: wasteful and extravagant in the use of resources
mnemonic: "Pro" (for) + "Fligate" (fligate sounds like 'flag it'): if you flag it for being wasteful, it's likely because someone is being profligate with their money.
hinglish: "Pro" (for) + "Fligate" (fligate sounds like 'flag it'): agar aap kisi ke kharch karne ke tareeqe ko flag karte ho, to wo zaroor profligate hai.

meaning: having deep insight or understanding
mnemonic: Pro + Found: when something is found to be profound, it means you have discovered its deep significance.
hinglish: Pro + Found: jab aapko kisi cheez ki gehraiyon ka pata chalta hai, to wo profound hoti hai.

meaning: deep insight or knowledge
mnemonic: Pro + Fund + Ity: when you invest in knowledge, you gain a profound understanding, leading to profundity in thoughts.
hinglish: Pro + Fund + Ity: jab aap gyaan mein paisa lagate hain, toh aapko gahrayi se samajh milta hai, jo profundity hai.

meaning: excessively abundant; overflowing
mnemonic: "Profuse" -> "Pro Fuse": when you fuse together numerous flowers in a garden, they create a profuse display.
hinglish: "Pro" + "Fuse": jab aap bahut saare phool milaate hain, to woh profuse (bahutayat) dikhte hain.

meaning: to increase rapidly in number or amount
mnemonic: Pro + Lifera(te): when a pro chef cooks, the dishes seem to proliferate as guests keep asking for more.
hinglish: Pro + Lifera(te): jab ek pro chef khana banata hai, to guests aur bhi khane ki maang karte hain aur khana proliferate ho jaata hai.

meaning: excessively verbose; using more words than necessary
mnemonic: "Pro" + "Lix" (licks): the professor licks his finger and flips through pages, making his lecture prolix with unnecessary details.
hinglish: "Pro" + "Lix" (licks): professor apne lecture ko itna badhakar likhta hai ki sabko samajh nahi aata, wo prolix ho jata hai.

meaning: to multiply or spread ideas, beliefs, or organisms
mnemonic: Prop + Agate: if you propagate good ideas, they can spread like precious stones, just like agate.
hinglish: Prop + Agate: agar aap achchhe vichar ko propagate karte hain, to wo jaise agate ke patthar ki tarah fail jaate hain.

meaning: a natural inclination or tendency to behave in a certain way
mnemonic: Propensity -> 'Propensity for Activity': he had a propensity for activity, always engaging in various sports and hobbies.
hinglish: Propensity + 'दुनिया में हैंसी चीज़ों की': उसे जोखिम उठाने का propensity था, जो उसे हमेशा रोमांचक अनुभवों में ले जाता था.

meaning: foretelling events as though by divine inspiration
mnemonic: "Prophet" -> "Prophet-ic": a prophet shares prophetic insights about future events, guiding people with foresight.
hinglish: "Prophet" + "Ick": prophet ki baatein hamesha sahi hoti hain, kyunki unki bhavishyavani prophetic hoti hai.

meaning: to appease or pacify someone, especially a deity or spirit
mnemonic: Pro + Pity + Ate: the villagers had to 'pro' (for) 'pity' their angry gods and 'ate' (offer) sacrifices to propitiate them.
hinglish: Pro + Pity + Ate: gaon waalon ko gusse mein aaye devtaon ke liye 'pro' (khaas) 'pity' (daya) dikhakar 'ate' (bali dene) padte hain taaki unhein shant kar sakein.

meaning: likely to produce a successful result
mnemonic: Prophet + Tious: a prophet is likely to predict propitious events that lead to success, just like favorable weather for a wedding.
hinglish: Prophet + Anukul: ek prophet aise anukul mahaul ki bhavishyavani karta hai jisse shaadi ki tarikh ko koi samasya nahi hoti.

meaning: the state or quality of being proper or suitable; appropriateness (सदाचार / उचितता)
mnemonic: "Pro" (for) + "priety" (purity): if you act for purity and appropriateness in a situation, you are observing propriety.
hinglish: "Pro" (sahi) + "priety" (safai): agar aap kisi situation mein sahi aur safai se behave karte hain, toh aap propriety ka palan kar rahe hain.

meaning: lacking in imagination or creativity; dull
mnemonic: "Prose" + "Sick": if your writing is just prosaic, it might make readers feel sick from boredom, lacking excitement.
hinglish: "Prose" + "Sick": agar tumhara likhne ka style prosaic hai, to logon ko woh badhkar sick lag sakta hai.

meaning: occurring by fortunate chance; lucky
mnemonic: "Provide" + "Essential": providential moments provide essential help at the right time, like when you find a lost item just in time.
hinglish: "Provide" + "Saanik": jab kisi ne zaroorat ke waqt madad provide ki, toh wo providential hota hai, jaise kisi ne zaroori kaam ke liye waqt par madad ki.

meaning: relating to a province; limited in perspective
mnemonic: "Pro" (for) + "Vincial" (vinculum/bond): He was so focused on provincial matters that he couldn't see beyond his local bonds.
hinglish: "Pro" (for) + "Vincial" (bandhan): Uska provincial soch unhe baaki cultures ko samajhne se rokti hai.

meaning: intended to provoke a reaction, often by being controversial or stimulating
mnemonic: Pro + Vocative: think of someone who is pro at provoking others, especially with provocative comments that ignite discussions.
hinglish: Pro + Vocate: jo log samvaad ko provoke karte hain, unka kehna hota hai ki unhe provocative baatein karni aati hain.

meaning: exceptional skill or ability in a particular activity
mnemonic: "Pro" (in favor of) + "Wrest" (to struggle): one who excels in wrestling shows great prowess in the sport.
hinglish: "Pro" (favor) + "Wrest" (kushti): jo log kushti me maharat rakhte hain, unhe prowess kaha jaata hai.

meaning: a person authorized to act on behalf of another
mnemonic: Proxy -> 'Pro' (for) + 'See': a proxy is someone who acts for you, essentially a professional who can see to your needs in your absence.
hinglish: Pro + See: proxy ek aisa vyakti hai jo aapki taraf se kaam karta hai jab aap maujood nahi hote.

meaning: acting with or showing care and thought for the future
mnemonic: Prude + Dent: a prude avoids risky behavior, making prudent choices to secure their future.
hinglish: Prude + Dent: ek prude aadmi risk se door rehkar samajhdaar decisions leta hai, isliye wo prudent hai.

meaning: having or showing excessive interest in sexual matters
mnemonic: Purr + Riant: a cat that purrs might be seen as overly fond of petting, hinting at a prurient interest in affection — similar to a person who is excessively curious about sexual matters.
hinglish: Purr + Riya: ek billi jo purr karti hai, usko zyada pyaar chahiye hota hai, jaise kisi vyakti ko prurient chizo mein zyada ruchi hoti hai.

meaning: childishly silly or trivial
mnemonic: Pew + Rile: pews in a church may be filled with people, but if someone tells puerile jokes, they will rile (annoy) the serious congregants.
hinglish: Pew + Rile: church ki pews par agar koi childish jokes kare, toh adults ko wo zaroor rile karega.

meaning: eager or quick to argue or fight; combative
mnemonic: "Pug" + "Nacious" (nasty): The pug dog is known for being pugnacious, always ready to fight with other dogs, reflecting a combative nature.
hinglish: "Pug" + "Nacious" (nasty): Pug dog ka swabhav hamesha pugnacious hota hai, dusre dogs se ladne ke liye tayar rehta hai.

meaning: showing great attention to detail or correct behavior
mnemonic: "Puncture" + "Lious" (like 'luxurious'): when you're punctilious, you puncture every detail to make it luxurious — you don't overlook anything.
hinglish: "Puncture" + "Lious" (jaise 'luscious'): jab aap punctilious hote hain, toh aap har detail ko puncture karke luscious bana dete hain — aap kuch bhi nahi chhodte.

meaning: a feeling of doubt or unease
mnemonic: "Qualm" -> "Calm": when in doubt, you can't be calm; thus, a qualm is the uneasy feeling that disrupts your peace.
hinglish: "Qualm" -> "Kalam": jab aapko koi baat kahne mein kalam (doubt) aata hai, tab aapko qualm mehsoos hota hai.

meaning: a state of uncertainty or perplexity
mnemonic: "Quandary" -> "Can Dread": when facing a difficult decision, you can dread making a choice, placing you in a quandary.
hinglish: "Kya Andar Hai": jab aapko kisi faisle ka samna karna ho, toh aap keh sakte ho, 'Kya andar hai,' jo aapko quandary me daal deta hai.

meaning: a state or period of isolation to prevent the spread of disease
mnemonic: "Quar" + "Ant" -> "Cure Ant": to cure an ant, you might need to quarantine it from the rest of the colony to prevent disease spread. — During the pandemic, quarantine became a common term for isolating individuals to prevent further contagion.
hinglish: "Kwar" + "Ant": jab ek ant ko bimari se bachana hota hai, toh usko quarantine karna padega, baaki ants se door rakhna padega. — Pandemic ke dauran, logon ko quarantine mein rahna pada taaki virus na phail sake.

meaning: to reject or suppress completely
mnemonic: Quash -> 'Crash': when you crash a party, you quash the fun and excitement. — The landlord quashed the party noise complaints by imposing strict rules.
hinglish: Quash -> 'Kash': jab aap kisi ka kaam kash kar dete ho, tab aap usay quash karte ho. — Usne sabhi mukadme quash kar diye kyunki sabhi jhoot the.

meaning: complaining in a petulant or whining manner
mnemonic: Quarrel + Us: when people quarrel, they often sound querulous, whining about their grievances in an annoying manner.
hinglish: Kya + Rula: jab koi koi baar baar shikayat karta hai, voh kuch aisa hi lagta hai — bilkul querulous.

meaning: to argue or raise objections about a trivial matter
mnemonic: "Quibble" -> "Quick Bible": if you quickly argue about little details in the Bible, you are quibbling instead of understanding the bigger message.
hinglish: "Quibble" -> "Kya Bilkul": jab aap choti choti baaton par argument karte hain, toh aap 'kya bilkul' karke quibble kar rahe hote hain.

meaning: inactive or at rest; quiet
mnemonic: Quiet + Ascent: when things are quiet, they can appear to be at rest or in a quiescent state, like a calm hill without any movement.
hinglish: Quiet + Ascent: jab sab kuch quiet hota hai, toh wo quiescent hota hai, jaise ek shaant pahaadi par kuch nahi hota.

meaning: having peculiar or unexpected traits
mnemonic: "Query" + "Key": if you query a key, you might find its quirky shape unusual, just like quirky things often surprise us.
hinglish: "Kya" + "Key": agar aap ek ajeeb key ko dekhenge, toh wo aapko quirky lagegi, jaisa ki quirky cheezen hamesha anokhi hoti hain.

meaning: extremely idealistic; unrealistic and impractical
mnemonic: "Quix" (quick) + "otic" (exotic): His quick and exotic ideas were so quixotic that they could never be realized in reality.
hinglish: "Quick" + "Exotic": Uske quick aur exotic ideas itne quixotic hain ki wo kabhi sach nahi ho sakte.

meaning: extreme or fundamental; relating to the basic nature of something
mnemonic: Rad + Ical: think of a radical transformation that takes a 'rad'ical turn — the changes are fundamental, not superficial.
hinglish: Rad + Ical: jab koi cheez itni 'rad'ical hoti hai, toh woh asli aur maujoodah halaton se bohot alag hoti hai.

meaning: light-hearted teasing or banter
mnemonic: Ray + Lery: like a ray of sunshine, raillery brings light-hearted laughter to conversations.
hinglish: Ray + Lery: jaise ek roshni ki kiran, raillery doston ke beech hasi mazak laati hai.

meaning: to talk or write in a lengthy, wandering manner without a clear focus
mnemonic: Ramble -> Ram + Ble: Imagine a ram that just keeps wandering around bleating, never staying on topic, just like when someone rambles.
hinglish: Ram + Bolo: Socho ek ram hai jo sirf badi-badi baatein kar raha hai bina kisi mudde par ruke, waise hi koi ramble karta hai.

meaning: a consequence or result, especially one that is unwelcome or unexpected
mnemonic: "Ram" + "If I Cation" (if I create a situation): if I create a new plan, the ramification may change how things work out for everyone involved.
hinglish: "Ram" + "If I Cation": agar main koi nayi situation banaun, toh uska ramification sabki zindagi par asar karega.

meaning: growing or spreading unchecked; unrestrained
mnemonic: "Ramp" + "Ant": imagine an ant climbing up a ramp at full speed, spreading everywhere like a rampant infestation. — The ant's movement was so rampant that it covered the entire picnic area.
hinglish: "Ramp" + "Chut": socho ek chutki si chidiya ramp par chadh rahi hai, bina kisi rok-tok ke, jaise ek badi badhkar hoti hai. — Uski chidiya ki chhalang itni rampant thi ki sab kuch chhup gaya.

meaning: having an insatiable appetite for greed or excess
mnemonic: Rapacious -> 'Ravage A Cereal': imagine a ravenous creature ravaging a field of cereal grain, symbolizing a rapacious desire for more than enough.
hinglish: Rape + Cereal: ek bhookha aadmi cereal ko aise khata hai jaise voh rapacious hai, kabhi bhi khush nahi hota.

meaning: based on or in accordance with reason or logic
mnemonic: "Rat" + "Ion": Imagine a rat on a diet, choosing healthy food options like an ion of energy, illustrating a rational choice for its health.
hinglish: "Rat" + "Iyon": Socho ek rat kaise samajhdar faisle le raha hai, healthy khana khake — voh ek rational (यथार्थ) faisla hai.

meaning: to cause severe and extensive damage to something
mnemonic: "Ravage" -> "Rage of the wave": a wave that rages can ravage the shore, causing great destruction.
hinglish: "Ravage" -> "Raja ki rage": jab raja gussa hota hai, woh apne dushmanon ko nash kar deta hai, unko ravage karta hai.

meaning: to withdraw or renounce a statement or belief
mnemonic: 'Re' (again) + 'Cant' (sing): if you recant, you are singing again but this time withdrawing your earlier tune or statement.
hinglish: 'Re' (dobara) + 'Cant' (gaana): jab aap recant karte hain, aap apne pehle kehne wale gaane ko dobara sunne se inkaar karte hain.

meaning: to summarize or restate the main points
mnemonic: Re + Cap + I + Tulate: to 'rehash a cap' — after discussing all the details, it's time to recapitulate the key takeaways, just like putting on a cap after a long day.
hinglish: Re + Cap + I + Tulate: 'Re-cap karna' ka matlab hai kuchh important baatein phir se batana — meeting ke baad humne key decisions ko recapitulate kiya.

meaning: a person who lives a solitary life and tends to avoid other people
mnemonic: "Re" + "Close": a recluse is someone who chooses to live 're' (again) 'close' (shut) to other people, avoiding social interactions.
hinglish: "Re" + "Close": ek recluse woh hai jo dusre logon se 're' (phir) 'close' (band) rehkar akela jeeta hai.

meaning: to restore friendly relations or resolve a conflict
mnemonic: Re + Con + Cile: to 'reconnect' a 'con' (as in a situation where there was a conflict) with 'cil' (as in to bring together), they had to reconcile their differences.
hinglish: Re + Con + Cile: jab do doston ki baat nahi banti, toh unhe apni baatein karke 'reconcile' karna padta hai.

meaning: little known or obscure; difficult to understand
mnemonic: "Re" + "Con" + "Dite" (re-conceal date): when someone tries to re-conceal a date, it becomes recondite, hidden from everyone's understanding.
hinglish: "Re" + "Con" + "Dite": jab koi kisi date ko phir se chupana chahta hai, wo recondite ban jaata hai, sabke samajh se door.

meaning: a source of help or support in a difficult situation
mnemonic: Re + Course: if you take a wrong course in life, you may need recourse to set things right with help.
hinglish: Re + Koshish: jab aapko koi mushkil samasya ho, toh aapko kisi doosre tarike ya sahare ki zaroorat padti hai, yeh hai recourse.

meaning: the return of a condition after a period of inactivity or remission
mnemonic: Re + Crude + Scent: when a scent becomes crude again, it's like a recrudescent odor returning after a period of freshness.
hinglish: Re + Kharab + Scent: jab ek kharab smell phir se aati hai, tab wo ek recrudescent badboo hoti hai.

meaning: inspiring fear or respect through being impressively powerful or capable
mnemonic: Redoubt -> Redoubt(able): a redoubt is a stronghold, so someone or something that is redoubtable is as strong and fearsome as a fortified place, inspiring respect.
hinglish: Redoubt + Able: ek redoubt jaise majboot sthaan se, redoubtable vyakti samne aate hi respect paate hain.

meaning: no longer needed or useful; superfluous
mnemonic: "Red" + "Undone": if something is redone unnecessarily, it becomes redundant — his repeated stories felt redundant to the listeners.
hinglish: "Red" + "Undone": agar koi cheez baar-baar ki ja rahi hai, to wo redundant hoti hai — uski kahaniyan baar-baar sunne se redundant lagne lagi.

meaning: to purify or improve something by removing unwanted elements
mnemonic: Re + Fine: if you want to make something fine again, you should refine it — just like how the chef refines his recipe to make it perfect.
hinglish: Re + Fine: agar aap kisi cheez ko phir se achha banana chahte hain, toh aapko use refine karna padega — jaise chef apni recipe ko refine karta hai perfect banane ke liye.

meaning: to throw back light or heat; to think carefully about something
mnemonic: "Reflect" -> "Re-flect" (again + bend): when you reflect, you bend light back to where it came from, just like a mirror reflects your image.
hinglish: "Re" (dobara) + "Flect" (modna): jab aap sochne ke liye waqt lete hain, to aap apni soch ko dobara modte hain, yaani aap soch-vichar karte hain.

meaning: to prove a statement or theory to be wrong or false
mnemonic: Refute -> Re-fute (feet): when you argue against someone's claim, you metaphorically kick their argument away, thus you refute it.
hinglish: Re + Fute: jab aap kisi ke argument ko ghalat sabit karte ho, toh aap uska 'fute' (foot) maarte ho, isliye aap refute karte ho.

meaning: to return to a previous, less advanced state
mnemonic: Re +gress (go): when you regress, it's like going back to where you started, losing the progress you've made.
hinglish: Re + jao (go back): agar aap seekhna band kar dete hain, toh aap pichhe jaane lagte hain, joh regress kehata hai.

meaning: to say something again or a number of times, typically for emphasis
mnemonic: "Re" (again) + "Iterate" (repeat): when you reiterate your point, you are repeating it again for clarity.
hinglish: "Re" (dubara) + "Iterate" (do baar): jab aap kisi baat ko reiterate karte hain, toh aap usay do baar kehte hain taaki sab samajh saken.

meaning: to assign to a lower position or rank
mnemonic: Re + Legate (delegate): when you relegate someone, you are essentially delegating them to a lesser role or position, as if they no longer hold important status.
hinglish: Re + Lagana (lagana = to apply): jab aap kisi ko neeche karte hain, to yah unhe unki pehle ki position se 're lagana' jaisa hota hai.

meaning: to become less severe or intense
mnemonic: "Re" (again) + "Lent" (to give): when you relent, you are giving in again to someone's request, showing a less severe attitude.
hinglish: "Re" (dobara) + "Lent" (dena): jab aap relent karte hain, to aap kisi ki maang ko dobara maan lete hain, jaise aap kam kar dete hain.

meaning: to give up or surrender something voluntarily
mnemonic: Re + Link + Wish: when you relinquish something, you are wishing to re-link it, but you let it go instead.
hinglish: Re + Link + Wish: jab aap kuch chhodte hain, toh aap usse phir se link karne ki ichcha karte hain, par aap ise chhod dete hain.

meaning: great enjoyment or delight
mnemonic: Relish -> 'Relish the Dish': when you eat something delicious, you relish every bite, enjoying it fully.
hinglish: Relish -> 'Relish Karo': jab tum kisi mazedaar khane ka swad lo, tab tum uska relish karte ho.

meaning: worthy of attention; extraordinary
mnemonic: "Remark" + "able": if something is remarkable, you can remark on it because it's so impressive — like her remarkable talent.
hinglish: "Remark" + "able": agar koi cheez remarkable hai, toh aap us par remark kar sakte hain kyunki wo itni prabhavshali hai.

meaning: intended to correct or improve
mnemonic: Remedy -> 'Rem' (to fix) + 'Edi' (like edit): if you edit a mistake, you are taking remedial action to correct it.
hinglish: Remedy: agar koi galti hai, to usse ‘rem’ karke ‘edi’ (edit) karna zaroori hai, jo remedial hai.

meaning: located a long distance away; distant
mnemonic: Remote -> Remote Control: when you use a remote control to operate a device from a distance, you are engaging with something remote, not close.
hinglish: Remote -> Remote Control: jab aap remote control se TV chalaate hain, tab aap kuch door se operate kar rahe hote hain, jo remote hai.

meaning: payment or compensation received for services or work done
mnemonic: Re + Muneration (remuneration sounds like remuneration): when you work hard, you expect to receive your remuneration as a reward for your efforts.
hinglish: Re + Munafa: jab aap kaam karte hain, to aap apne mehnat ka munafa ya remuneration lena chahte hain.

meaning: to cause to become; to make
mnemonic: Render -> 'Re' (again) + 'Ender' (to create): when you render a scene, you recreate it again like an artist rendering a new masterpiece.
hinglish: Re + 'Ender': jab aap kisi scene ko render karte hain, aap usay phirse naya roop dete hain jaise ek artist ek sundar painting banata hai.

meaning: to fail to fulfill a promise or obligation
mnemonic: "Renegade" + "negate": when a renegade negates his promises, he reneges on his commitments. — He had to renege on his promise to attend the meeting.
hinglish: "Renegade" + "negotiate": jab ek renegade apne negotiations ko khatam kar deta hai, wo renege karta hai apni baaton se. — Usne meeting mein aane ka vaada renege kiya.

meaning: to formally give up or reject a claim, right, or belief
mnemonic: "Renounce" -> "Renounce your Bounce": if you renounce your bounce, you are giving up on something fun and lively, which reflects the act of renouncing.
hinglish: "Rena" (to live) + "Nau" (new): jab aap kuch purana tyag karte hain aur naya shuru karte hain, to aap us cheez ko renounce kar rahe hain.

meaning: a consequence or effect, often negative, of an action or event
mnemonic: Re + Percussion: when you hit a drum (percussion), it creates a sound that resonates, just like the repercussions of actions can resonate through a community.
hinglish: Re + Pariksha: agar aap pariksha me ache nahi karte, toh uska bura parinaam (repercussion) bahut bura ho sakta hai.

meaning: a collection of works or skills that a person is prepared to perform
mnemonic: Re + 'Pet' + 'War': When a pet is ready for a war, it shows all its tricks in its repertoire of skills.
hinglish: Re + 'Pet' + 'War': Jab ek pet jang ke liye tayar hota hai, toh wo apne skills ki poori repertoire dikhata hai.

meaning: to restore or refill something to its former level or state
mnemonic: "Re" + "Plenish" (to fill): When you replenish supplies, you refill or restore them to their full amount, just like filling a glass back to the brim.
hinglish: "Re" + "Plenish" (bharnay ka): Jab aap apne khana-pina ki cheezen replenish karte hain, to aap unhein phir se bharte hain, jaise ek glass ko phir se bharna.

meaning: to express disapproval or disappointment
mnemonic: "Re" (again) + "Proach" (approach): when you reproach someone, you approach them again to express your disappointment about their actions.
hinglish: "Re" (phir se) + "Proach" (koi approach karna): jab aap kisiko reproach karte hain, toh aap phir se unke paas jaakar unki galtiyon par nafrat dikhate hain.

meaning: a morally unprincipled person
mnemonic: "Reprobate" -> "Repro (criticize) + bate (to lessen)": A reprobate is someone who is criticized for their immoral actions, and their character is lessened because of it.
hinglish: "Repro" (criticize) + "bate" (kam karna): A reprobate aadmi ko log criticize karte hain kyunki uska charitra kami se bhara hota hai.

meaning: to refuse to accept or support something
mnemonic: "Re" (again) + "Pudiate" (pudgy): if someone has a pudgy figure, you might repudiate unhealthy eating habits and start exercising to lose weight.
hinglish: "Re" (dobara) + "Pudiate" (mohtaaz): agar koi aadmi mohtaaz hai toh woh dobara aise behtar habits ko aswikar karega, jaise ki unhealthy food se repudiate karna.

meaning: causing a strong feeling of disgust or aversion
mnemonic: "Repug" + "Nant": when something is so bad it makes you want to fight back against it — a repugnant sight or smell.
hinglish: "Repug" + "Nant": jab koi cheez itni ghatiya hoti hai ki aap uske khilaf ladna chahte hain — ghinauna dikhayi deta hai.

meaning: to feel bitterness or indignation at having been treated unfairly
mnemonic: Re + Sent: when you 're-sent' a letter after being ignored, you might feel resentment towards the person for not acknowledging it.
hinglish: Re + Sent: jab aap kisi ko 'dobara bhejte' hain jo aapki baat nahi sunti, toh aap us par naraz ho sakte hain.

meaning: something that remains after a part is taken, disposed of, or subtracted
mnemonic: "Res" + "Idual" (Residual): when you cook, if there are leftovers, those are the residual snacks that remain after serving.
hinglish: "Res" + "Idual" (अवशेष): jab aap party ke baad kuch khane ke liye chhode, woh residual snacks hote hain.

meaning: able to recover quickly from difficult conditions
mnemonic: Resilient -> 'Resilient' + 'Silly': a silly rubber band can stretch and snap back, just like a resilient person bounces back from tough times.
hinglish: Resilient + Silly: ek silly rubber band har baar kheeche jane par wapas apni shape mein aa jaata hai, jaise ek resilient aadmi mushkil samay se bahar aa jaata hai.

meaning: determined and unwavering in purpose
mnemonic: "Resolve" + "Loot": A thief must be resolute to loot a bank without getting caught; he can't waver in his decision.
hinglish: "Resolve" + "Loot": Chori karne wale ko resolute hona padta hai, warna wo pakda jayega.

meaning: to make a firm decision or determination
mnemonic: Re + Solve: if you resolve a problem, you are willing to 're-solve' it by finding a solution.
hinglish: Re + Solve: jab aap kisi samasya ko suljhaate hain, tab aap usay 'phir se suljha' rahe hote hain.

meaning: capable of finding quick and clever ways to overcome difficulties
mnemonic: Resource + Full: if you are full of resources, you are resourceful; she was so resourceful that she could fix anything with what she had.
hinglish: Resource + Full: jab aap resources se bhare hote hain, tab aap resourceful hote hain; usne apne paas maujood saman se har samasya ka hal nikaala.

meaning: impatient or difficult to control
mnemonic: Rest + tive: when you want to rest but can't, you become restive, unable to stay calm.
hinglish: Rest + tive: jab aap aaram nahi kar paate, toh aap restless ya restive ho jaate hain.

meaning: to take revenge or respond to an attack
mnemonic: "Retaliate" -> "Retail a T8": imagine a store manager who got angry and wants to retaliate against a bad review by offering a discount — he will 'retail' (sell) some items at a 'T8' (great) price to win customers back.
hinglish: "Retaliate" -> "Retail a T8": socho ek dukaan ka malik jo bura review sunke badla lena chah raha hai, wo customers ko 'T8' (badi) chhoot dekar waapas laana chahta hai, isliye wo 'retail' karega aur badla lega.

meaning: not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily
mnemonic: "Reticent" -> "Retreat in Silence": when someone retreats from speaking, they are being reticent about their thoughts.
hinglish: "Retreat" + "Ke" + "Silent": jab koi apne vichar ko chhupakar chala jaata hai, tab vo reticent hota hai.

meaning: shy or reserved in manner
mnemonic: "Re" + "Tire" (rest): when someone is retiring, they may appear to want to rest from social situations, preferring to withdraw rather than engage.
hinglish: "Re" + "Tire": jab koi insaan retiring hota hai, toh woh social situations se thoda rest lena chahta hai, dusron se door rehna pasand karta hai.

meaning: to reduce or curtail expenses or operations
mnemonic: Retreat + Trench: when you retreat from a trench, you often have to retrench your resources, meaning to cut back on your spending.
hinglish: Retreat + Kachra: jab aap retreat karte hain, toh aapko apne kharchon ko kachra ki tarah retrench karna padta hai.

meaning: an expression of enthusiastic or ecstatic feeling
mnemonic: "Rap" + "Sody" (like 'soda'): when you rap about something sweet like soda, it turns into a rhapsody of joy and excitement. — The singer's rhapsody filled the concert hall with infectious energy.
hinglish: "Rap" + "Sody": jab aap soda ke baare mein rap karte hain, to usme umang bhari hoti hai, jaise ek rhapsody. — Us gaayak ki rhapsody se sab log khush ho gaye.

meaning: the art of persuasive speaking or writing (often exaggerated)
mnemonic: "Rate" + "Horror": if you rate a horror story, your rhetoric might sound exaggerated and dramatic — just like persuasive speech.
hinglish: "Rate" + "Horror": agar aap kisi horror kahani ko rate karte hain, toh aapki rhetoric zyada dramatik aur bhaavuk lag sakti hai.

meaning: strictness or severity in discipline or treatment
mnemonic: Rigor -> Rigorous: a rigorous workout means strict and severe training that tests your limits.
hinglish: Rigor + Rigorous: ek rigorous training programme ka matlab hai kaafi strict aur kathor training jo aapki limits ko test karta hai.

meaning: strong and healthy; vigorous
mnemonic: "Robust" -> "Rob's Bust": if Rob is strong and healthy, he has a robust physique that impresses everyone.
hinglish: "Rob" + "Bust": agar Rob itna mazboot hai, toh uski body dekh kar sab hairaan reh jaate hain.

meaning: basic or simple; not fully developed
mnemonic: Rude + Mentality: having a rude or basic mentality means your understanding is rudimentary, just like a novice.
hinglish: Rude + Mentality: jab kisi ki soch sirf rudimentary ho, toh uski soch rude hoti hai, bina gahrayi ke.

meaning: to think carefully and for a long period about something
mnemonic: "Room" + "inate" (innate): When you ruminate, you take a moment in your mind’s room to let your innate thoughts settle and grow, just like cows chew cud.
hinglish: "Room" + "inate": Jab aap ruminate karte hain, to aap apne dimaag ke room mein sochne ka samay lete hain, jaise gaayen cud chaat kar sochti hain.

meaning: regarded as sacred and inviolable
mnemonic: "Sacred" + "Sanctuary": a sanctuary is a sacred place that is sacrosanct, protected from any harm or intrusion.
hinglish: "Sacred" + "Sanctuary": ek sanctuary itna sacred hota hai ki wo sacrosanct hai, jise kisi bhi harm se bachaya jata hai.

meaning: deriving pleasure from inflicting pain on others
mnemonic: Sad + Dick: a sadistic person finds joy in making others suffer, much like someone named Dick who enjoys inflicting sadness.
hinglish: Sad + Dastak: ek sadistic aadmi dusre logon ko takleef dekar khushi mehsoos karta hai, jaise ek dastak (knock) se kisi ko darana.

meaning: having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment
mnemonic: Sagacious -> 'Sage' + 'Cious' (like delicious): a sage is often wise and gives sagacious advice that is as pleasing as a delicious meal.
hinglish: Sage + Cious: sage jaisa samajhdar vyakti hamesha aise sujhav deta hai jo aapki madad karte hain.

meaning: health-giving; favorable to health
mnemonic: "Salute" + "Brio" (vitality): when you salute the healthful qualities of your food, you ensure a salubrious lifestyle.
hinglish: "Salute" + "Briya" (स्वास्थ्य): jab aap swasthya ki taraf salute dete hain, toh aap apni zindagi ko salubrious bana lete hain.

meaning: beneficial, producing good effects
mnemonic: Salute + 'ary' (to): when you salute a good habit, it has a salutary effect on your life.
hinglish: Salute + 'ary': jab aap achhe aadat ko salute karte hain, toh uska aapke jeevan par labhकारी asar hota hai.

meaning: making a show of being morally superior to others
mnemonic: Sanctuary + Monious (bounteous): a sanctuary is a holy place, and being sanctimonious is like being overly bounteous in your display of holiness, often hypocritically, as he was in his judgment of others.
hinglish: Sanctuary + Monious: ek sanctuary, jahan sab kuch dharmik hai, par aisa koi insan jo dusron ki dharmikta par ungli uthata hai, sanctimonious hota hai.

meaning: a penalty or punishment imposed on an individual or entity, or approval for an action
mnemonic: Sanctuary + Action: a 'sanction' can mean giving a legal permit (action) for an activity just like allowing someone to enter a sanctuary.
hinglish: Sanctuary + Action: 'sanction' ka matlab hota hai kisi kaam ko karne ki anumati dena, jaise kisi sanctuary mein pravesh ki anumati dena.

meaning: cheerfully optimistic or positive
mnemonic: "Sang" (sing) + "Wine": when you sing with a glass of wine in hand, you're feeling sanguine about life, enjoying the moment with optimism.
hinglish: "Sang" (sang) + "Wine": jab aap doston ke saath wine pee kar gaate hain, tab aap khush aur sanguine feel karte hain.

meaning: mocking or criticizing through humor and exaggeration
mnemonic: "Sati" (like "satiate") + "rical" (like "critical"): when you satiate your need for humor, you enjoy satirical content that is critical of society.
hinglish: "Sati" (satiate) + "rical" (critical): jab aap apni hasi ki zarurat ko satiate karte hain, tab aap vyangyaatmak (satirical) cheezein dekhte hain jo samaj par tanav karte hain.

meaning: barely sufficient in amount or quantity
mnemonic: Scant -> Scanty Ant: if you have scant food, it's like a 'scanty ant' trying to carry a crumb — there's not enough to sustain it.
hinglish: Scant + Ant: agar khana scant hai, toh ek choti si 'scant' ke liye bhi kaafi nahi hai.

meaning: harshly critical or scornful
mnemonic: "Scathe" + "ing": when you scathe someone, you're being harshly critical, just like a scathing comment can burn.
hinglish: "Scathe" + "ing": jab aap kisi ko scathe karte hain, toh aap unhe nindak ke roop mein ghamraha karte hain, jaise ek scathing comment se unka dil dukhta hai.

meaning: a division or split, especially in a religious context
mnemonic: "Schism" -> "Ski+Sim": Imagine a ski competition where two teams are so divided in strategy that they clash, causing a schism in their approach to winning.
hinglish: "Ski" + "Sim": Skiing ki competition mein do teams itni alag ho gayi ki unka approach jeetne ke liye ek schism bana diya.

meaning: sparkling or shining brightly; brilliantly clever or lively
mnemonic: Scintilla -> 'Cinderella': just like Cinderella sparkles at the ball, a scintillating person shines brightly in conversation.
hinglish: Chamak + Dhaar: jaise Cinderella ka ball mein chamakna, waise hi scintillating logon ki baatein chamakti hain.

meaning: the feeling or expression of contempt or disdain
mnemonic: Score + N: scoring someone negatively implies you look at them with scorn. — She had a scornful attitude towards his poor decision-making.
hinglish: Score + N: score kisi ki taraf se negative mark karne ka matlab hai ki us par tirkash karna. — Usne uski bekaar ki soch par tirkash se dekha.

meaning: diligent and careful in doing things thoroughly and according to rules
mnemonic: "Screw + Pull": if you screw something up, you must pull it together with scrupulous attention to detail to fix it properly.
hinglish: "Screw + Pull": agar aapne kaam me ghalti ki hai, toh usay theek karne ke liye aapko scrupulous hona padega.

meaning: showing dedication and diligence in work or effort
mnemonic: Said + Diligently: a sedulous person is someone who said they'd work diligently on their tasks.
hinglish: Said + Dilse: sedulous log woh hote hain jo dil se kaam karne ka vaada karte hain.

meaning: gratifying one's own desires without restraint
mnemonic: Self + Indulge: when you indulge yourself too much, you become self-indulgent, like a child who always wants candy.
hinglish: Self + Indulge: jab aap khud ko khush karne ke liye zyada indulge karte hain, tab aap self-indulgent ho jaate hain.

meaning: causing a strong reaction or excitement; extraordinary
mnemonic: "Sense" + "Nation": the 'sense' of excitement is so powerful that it creates a 'nation' of fans, leading to sensational events.
hinglish: "Sense" + "Nashon": jab koi event itna zyada 'sense' ya 'nashon' deta hai, toh woh sensational ban jaata hai.

meaning: expressive of or appealing to sentiment, especially the tender emotions
mnemonic: "Sentiment" -> "Senti Mental": someone who is overly mental about their feelings can be described as sentimental; they easily get emotional.
hinglish: "Senti" + "Mental": jo log apne jazbaton ke liye zyada sochte hain, unhein sentimental kaha jaata hai.

meaning: occurring by chance in a happy or beneficial way
mnemonic: "Serendipity" -> "Serene Dip": when you take a serene dip in the pool, you might serendipitously find a friend swimming nearby.
hinglish: "Serene" + "Dip": jab aap ek shaant paani mein doobte hain, aapko serendipitously apna dost mil sakta hai.

meaning: calm, peaceful, and untroubled
mnemonic: Serene -> See Rain: if you see rain while sitting peacefully in a garden, the atmosphere feels serene.
hinglish: See + Rain: agar aap baarish dekh rahe hain aur aapka man shaant hai, toh wo pal bahut serene hoga.

meaning: to cut off or separate
mnemonic: "Sever" -> "Serve her": If you serve her too much, you might need to sever ties with her when she takes advantage.
hinglish: "Sever" -> "Sewa karna": Jab aap kisi ko zyada sewa karte hain, toh kabhi kabhi aapko unse sambandh sever (khatam) karna padta hai.

meaning: a thing that is not what it is purported to be; a false display
mnemonic: Sham -> 'Sham' (scam): a sham is like a scam where the reality is disguised, just as a facade covers the truth.
hinglish: Sham + 'Sham' (dhokha): yeh agar sham hai toh yeh sirf ek dhokha hai jo asli nahi hai.

meaning: to avoid or neglect a duty or responsibility
mnemonic: Shirk -> 'Shirk away': When you shirk away from your responsibilities, you are avoiding them instead of facing them.
hinglish: Shirk + 'Shirk away': Jab aap apni zimmedariyon se shirk karte hain, tab aap unse door bhag rahe hote hain.

meaning: having or showing sharp powers of judgment; astute
mnemonic: Shrewd -> 'Shrewd' + 'Dude': a shrewd dude always knows how to profit from every situation.
hinglish: Shrewd + Dude: ek shrewd dude hamesha har situation se faida uthata hai.

meaning: a high-pitched and piercing sound
mnemonic: Shrill -> 'Shrill' (sound): the shrill noise of a baby crying can pierce through the loudest of conversations.
hinglish: Shrill -> 'Shreel' (sharp sound): jab bachche ka shreel roshni se roye, sab log chakkar khate hain.

meaning: a job or position requiring little or no work, often providing income
mnemonic: "Sign a Cure" -> (implying ease): securing a position that requires no effort is like having a job where you just sign your name for a cure and get paid without working hard.
hinglish: "Sign + a Cure": ek aisi position jisme sirf apna naam likhna hota hai aur paisa milta hai, woh hai sinecure.

meaning: having many curves and turns; winding
mnemonic: "Sin" + "Uous": if you take a sinuous route to avoid a straight path, you might feel guilty but you’ll definitely enjoy the journey.
hinglish: "Sin" + "Uous": agar aap sinuous rasta lete hain, toh aap seedha nahi ja rahe hote, lekin safar ka mazaa zaroor le rahe hote hain.

meaning: to move around the edge of something or avoid discussing a topic directly
mnemonic: "Skirt" -> "Scurry Around It": when you skirt a problem, you scurry around it rather than facing it, much like how you might skirt around a puddle on the sidewalk.
hinglish: "Skirt" -> "Ski + Kart": jab aap kisi baat ko ski karke kart karte hain, tab aap usse seedha nahi bolte, balki usse ghoom kar nikalte hain.

meaning: nervous or easily frightened
mnemonic: "Skittish" -> "Skittles Dish": if someone has a dish of Skittles and they are too jumpy to pick one, they are skittish about trying new things.
hinglish: "Skit" + "Dish": agar kisi ke paas ek skit ka dish hai aur wo woh dekhkar ghabra raha hai, toh wo skittish hai.

meaning: deceitful behavior or trickery
mnemonic: Skull + Dug: imagine someone digging a grave for a skull, representing deceit and trickery; thus, it embodies the concept of skullduggery in political schemes.
hinglish: Skull + Dug: jab koi politician election ke liye khud ko khudayi karke skull ki tarah dheela kar deta hai, to woh skullduggery kar raha hota hai.

meaning: the action of making false spoken statements that damage a person's reputation
mnemonic: "Slander" -> "Slender and Under": if you make someone’s reputation slender (thin) and push them under (down), you are committing slander.
hinglish: "Slander" -> "Sundar aur Zameen ke Neche": agar aap kisi ko sundar (achha) naam se neeche (bura) dikhate hain, toh aap slander kar rahe hain.

meaning: small in degree or amount
mnemonic: "Slight" -> "Slightly Light": when something is slightly off, it means it is not heavy or significant. A slight change in the recipe made the cake taste light.
hinglish: "Slight" -> "Slightly Light": jab kuch thoda sa badalta hai, toh wo zaroorat se zyada bhaari ya ahm nahi hota. Isliye, slight change se cake halka ho gaya.

meaning: careless, untidy, or unkempt in appearance or habits
mnemonic: "Slo" (slow) + "venly" (cleanly): if you're slow to clean, you will appear slovenly and unkempt.
hinglish: "Slo" (slow) + "venly" (saaf): agar aap dheere saaf karte hain, toh aapki appearance slovenly ho jati hai.

meaning: slow-moving or inactive
mnemonic: Slush + Ick: when you're feeling sluggish, your energy is like slush — thick and icky, making you want to stay still.
hinglish: Slaash + Ick: jab aap sluggish hote hain, aapki energy itni low hoti hai ki aap kuch nahi karna chahte, bas 'slaash' se lete rehte hain.

meaning: not affected by alcohol; clear-headed
mnemonic: Sow + Burr: imagine a farmer sowing seeds in a sober mood while avoiding any distractions, as he needs to focus on his work.
hinglish: Sow + Burr: kisan bina kisi shor sharabe ke beej bone ke liye sober hai, taki wo apne kaam par dhyan de sake.

meaning: a speech delivered by a character alone on stage, revealing their thoughts
hindi: एक पात्र द्वारा मंच पर अकेले दिए गए भाषण, जो उनके विचारों को प्रकट करता है
mnemonic: Solus (alone) + Loquy (speaking): a soliloquy is when a character speaks their thoughts out loud when they are alone on stage.
hinglish: Solus (akela) + Loquy (bolna): soliloquy tab hota hai jab ek kirdar akela hote hue apne vichar zor se bolta hai.

meaning: drowsy or sleepy
mnemonic: Som + No + Lent: when you’re somnolent, it feels like no energy is lent to you, making you sleepy.
hinglish: Som + No + Lent: jab aap somnolent hote hain, toh aapko lagta hai ki aapki energy ko koi nahi udhaar de raha hai, aur aap neend mein hain.

meaning: having a high degree of complexity or refinement
mnemonic: "Sofa" + "Stated": Imagine a person sitting on a luxurious sofa and stating their refined knowledge of art and culture — it captures the essence of sophisticated.
hinglish: "Sofa" + "State": Luxury sofa par baith kar unhone parishkrit (sophisticated) thoughts bayaan kiye.

meaning: a deceptive or fallacious argument or reasoning
mnemonic: "Sofa" + "Tree": imagine sitting on a sofa under a tree, where you can craft fancy arguments that sound good but have no real substance—just like sophistry.
hinglish: "Sofa" + "Tari": ek sofa par baithe hue kisi tar ke neeche, aise arguments bana rahe ho jo sirf achhe lagte hain par asli nahi—yehi hai sophistry.

meaning: inducing sleep; drowsy
mnemonic: Sopor + Ific: if something is soporific, it means it is so calming that it can put you to sleep, like a soothing lullaby.
hinglish: Sopor + Ific: agar kuch soporific hai, toh wo itna shaant hai ki aapko neend aayegi, bilkul ek sukhad geet ki tarah.

meaning: involving ignoble actions and motives; arousing moral distaste and contempt
mnemonic: Sore + Did: if someone did something sore (injurious or painful) to another, it might be a sordid act that causes moral outrage.
hinglish: Sore + Did: agar kisi ne kisi ko sore (dard) diya hai, toh woh ek sordid kaam hai jo moral nafrat ko janm deta hai.

meaning: vibrations that travel through the air or another medium and can be heard
mnemonic: "Sound" -> "Sow + Und": When you sow (plant) seeds, you hope they make a sound (grow) in the garden — the sound of nature's growth.
hinglish: "Sow + Und": Jab aap beej boya, aap umeed karte hain ki wo sound (dhwani) ban kar ugte hain.

meaning: thinly dispersed or scattered
mnemonic: "Spar" + "ce": when resources are scarce, like in a sparse area, you have to spar for every bit of food.
hinglish: "Spar" + "ce": jab khana kam ho, tab humein sparse area me khane ke liye spar karna padta hai.

meaning: marked by simplicity, frugality, or avoidance of luxury
mnemonic: Spartan -> 'Sparse Tan': living with a sparse tan suggests a simple and unadorned life, just like the spartan way.
hinglish: Spar + Tan: spar tan ka matlab hai aise jeena jisme shaan-shaukat nahi hoti, jaise ki Spartan jeevan.

meaning: seemingly plausible but actually wrong or misleading
mnemonic: Specious -> 'Specious' Sounds like 'Spacious': just because a room looks spacious doesn't mean it’s practical — similar to how a specious argument may seem valid but lacks real substance.
hinglish: Specious -> 'Spacious': Bahar se spacious lagta hai magar andar se bhut chhota hai, waise hi ek specious argument achha lagta hai par asal mein galat hota hai.

meaning: to form opinions or conjectures without firm evidence
mnemonic: Speculate -> Spec + Ulate (like 'speculate the future'): when you look ahead and guess what might happen, you speculate about future events.
hinglish: Spec + Ulate: jab aap aage dekh kar sochte hain ki kya ho sakta hai, tab aap estimate karte hain, yani speculate karte hain.

meaning: a person who spends money extravagantly and irresponsibly
mnemonic: Spend + Thrift: if you spend without thriftiness (care), you become a spendthrift and end up broke.
hinglish: Spend + Thrift: agar aap bina soch-samajh ke kharch karte hain, toh aap spendthrift ban jaate hain aur paise khatam kar lete hain.

meaning: occurring at irregular intervals; not continuous or steady
mnemonic: Sporadic -> 'Sporadically Active': when you exercise sporadically, you do so at irregular intervals, not consistently.
hinglish: Sporadic -> 'Sporadically Act': jab aap sporadically act karte hain, toh aap kabhi-kabhi hi kuch karte hain, regular nahi.

meaning: not genuine, false or misleading
mnemonic: "Spoon" + "Furious": when you eat with a spoon and someone is furious about the food being fake, you realize they are talking about spurious ingredients.
hinglish: "Spoon" + "Furious": jab aap ek spoon se khana kha rahe hote hain aur koi us food ke fake hone par furious hota hai, toh aap samajh jaate hain ki wo spurious hai.

meaning: to reject or disdain something or someone disdainfully
mnemonic: "Spurn" -> "Sponge Burn": When you get a burn from a sponge, you might spurn (reject) using it again to prevent more pain.
hinglish: "Spoon" + "Turn": Jab koi aapko spoon se khana dene ki koshish kare aur aap usay spoon se turn kar de, tab aap usay spurn kar rahe hain.

meaning: to waste something, especially money or time, in a reckless manner
mnemonic: "Squander" -> "Squad under": if your squad is under pressure, don’t squander your resources or they will be wasted in vain efforts.
hinglish: "Squad + Under": agar aapka squad under pressure hai, toh aapko apne resources squander nahi karne chahiye, warna sab kuch vyarth ho jayega.

meaning: sedate, respectable, and unadventurous
mnemonic: "Stay" + "Id": when you stay idle, you often seem staid, lacking excitement or adventure.
hinglish: "Stay" + "Id": jab aap stay karte hain aur idhar-udhar nahi jaate, tab aap ka behavior staid hota hai, bina excitement ke.

meaning: loyal, reliable, and hardworking person
mnemonic: Stall + Wart: imagine a stall that has a wart, but it's so sturdy it withstands storms, just like a stalwart person stands firm in support.
hinglish: Stall + Wart: socho ek stall hai jisme wart hai, lekin woh itna mazboot hai ki har muskil mein khada rehta hai, jaise stalwart insaan hamesha support deta hai.

meaning: to stop or restrict the flow of a liquid
mnemonic: Stanch -> Stun a Ranch: if you stun a ranch animal, you might need to stanch the blood flow from its wounds.
hinglish: Stanch -> Stun karna: agar aap kisi jaanwar ko stun karte hain, toh aapko uska khoon rokna padega.

meaning: firmly loyal or constant; unwavering
mnemonic: "Steady" + "Fast": being steady like a rock and moving fast towards your goals means you are steadfast in your determination.
hinglish: "Steady" + "Fast": jab aap ekdum steady aur tez hain apne maqsad ki taraf, tab aap steadfast hain.

meaning: to originate from; to result from
mnemonic: "Stem" -> "Stem the problem" + "From" (origin): when you stem a situation, you go to the root from where it has originated, just like how issues often stem from underlying causes.
hinglish: "Stem" (jhaadi) + "From" (se): jab koi samasya hoti hai, toh wo aksar kisi jhaadi se utpann hoti hai, jaise kaam ka pressure stress ko utpann karta hai.

meaning: strict or harsh in manner or behavior
mnemonic: "Stern" -> "Turn": when you turn a strict eye towards someone, you are being stern; a stern expression can stop misbehavior.
hinglish: "Stern" -> "Turn": jab aap kisi par kadak nazar daalte hain, to aap stern hai; teacher ka stern chehra students ko sambhalne par majboor karta hai.

meaning: to mark someone or something with disgrace or infamy
mnemonic: "Stigma" + "tize": when you stigmatize someone, you create a stigma around them, marking them as inferior or disgraceful.
hinglish: "Stigma" + "tize": jab aap kisi ko stigmatize karte hain, tab aap unke liye ek stigma banate hain, unhe kalankit karte hain.

meaning: the act of being stingy or frugal
mnemonic: "Stint" -> "Stingy": being stinting means you are acting stingy with your resources; he was stinting on the funds needed for the event.
hinglish: "Stint" + "Kanjus": jab koi vyakti khud ke liye bhi kharch nahi karta, tab woh stinting hota hai, jaise usne party ke liye paise kharch karne se mana kar diya.

meaning: the endurance of pain or hardship without the display of feelings and without complaint
mnemonic: "Stow" + "Ick": When you stow away your emotions like a bad smell, you become stoic and unfazed by difficulties.
hinglish: "Stow" + "Ikk": Jab aap apne emotions ko ikattha kar lete hain, toh aap stoic ban jaate hain aur muskilat se nahi darte.

meaning: having or showing little emotion; impassive
mnemonic: Stole + Lid: if someone stole your favorite lid and you remained stolid, it means you felt no emotion about it.
hinglish: Stole + Lid: agar koi aapka pasandiada lid chura le aur aap bina kisi bhavna ke rahain, toh aap stolid hain.

meaning: conflict or struggle
mnemonic: Strife -> Strife is a Knife: like a knife cuts relationships, strife can cut through peace and create conflict.
hinglish: Strife -> Strife is a Knife: jaisa chaku rishte todta hai, waisa hi strife aman ko todti hai.

meaning: strictly controlled or enforced
mnemonic: String + Gent: if a gentleman has stringent manners, he is strict and always follows the rules.
hinglish: String + Gent: ek gentleman agar stringent hai, toh voh hamesha niyam ka paalan karta hai.

meaning: calm and restrained; not aggressive or intense
mnemonic: Sub + Dude: a subdued dude is calm and quiet, not causing a scene.
hinglish: Saab + Dude: jab saab dude zyada nahi bolta, wo subdued hota hai.

meaning: based on personal opinions, interpretations, feelings, or beliefs rather than external facts
mnemonic: Sub + Jective: when you subjectively evaluate something, it’s like putting your personal 'subject' (yourself) first in the 'jective' (objective) analysis, thus it becomes subjective.
hinglish: Sub + Jective: jab aap kisi movie ko subjective taur par judge karte hain, toh aap apne 'subject' (apne vichar) ko pehle rakhte hain aur isliye wo subjective ban jata hai.

meaning: lower in rank or position
mnemonic: Sub + Ordinate: think of 'sub' as under and 'ordinate' like order — a subordinate is someone who is under someone else in the order of things.
hinglish: Sub + Ordinate: 'sub' ka matlab neeche hota hai aur 'ordinate' ka matlab order — ek subordinate voh hota hai jo kisi aur ke neeche order me hota hai.

meaning: obediently submissive
mnemonic: Sub + Serve + Ent: being subservient means you are always ready to serve others without question, like a waiter at a restaurant.
hinglish: Sub + Serve + Ent: subservient hone ka matlab hai aap hamesha doosron ki seva karne ke liye tayaar hote hain, jaise ek waiter restaurant mein.

meaning: to become less intense or severe
mnemonic: "Sub" (under) + "Side" (to the side): when the noise and chaos subside, they go under and to the side, leaving peace behind. — The loud arguments eventually began to subside, creating a tranquil atmosphere.
hinglish: "Sub" (sab) + "Side" (side): jab sab kuch side ho jaata hai, to shor kam ho jaata hai. — Jab dono dost ladte hain, to baad mein unki baatein dheere dheere subside ho jaati hain.

meaning: to provide evidence to support or prove the truth of something
mnemonic: Substance + Stain: a stain on a fabric can substantiate the claim of a spill, proving that something was spilled.
hinglish: Sub + Stain: ek daag kisi kapde par substantiate kar sakta hai ki kuch gira hai, jisse yeh sabit hota hai.

meaning: to include or absorb something into a larger category
mnemonic: "Sub" (under) + "Sume" (sum): when you sum different numbers, they get subsumed into a single total. The total subsumes all the individual values.
hinglish: "Sub" (sabka) + "Sume" (samaana): sabkuch milakar ek category mein sama jaata hai, jaise sab species ek genus ke andar subsume hote hain.

meaning: delicate and understated; not obvious
mnemonic: "Sub" (under) + "Tle" (till): when you plant a seed subtly under the soil, it grows quietly without making a fuss, just like subtle hints in a conversation.
hinglish: "Sub" (sab) + "Tle" (chhoti): jab aap sabse chhoti si baat ko bhi dhyan se samajhte hain, toh wo sukhmadi (subtle) hoti hai.

meaning: to undermine the authority or power of an established system or institution
mnemonic: Sub -> 'Under' + Vert -> 'Invert': to subvert a system means to turn it upside down from underneath.
hinglish: Sub -> 'Neeche' + Vert -> 'Ghumana': kisi vyavastha ko subvert karna ka matlab hai usay neeche se ghumana ya ulatna.

meaning: existing or occurring at or on the surface; not deep or serious
mnemonic: Super + Fish + Al: a fish only swims near the surface of the water, indicating a superficial understanding of the ocean's depths.
hinglish: Super + Fish + Al: ek machhli sirf paani ke upar tarah karti hai, jo sirf superficial samajh dikhata hai.

meaning: excessive or unnecessary; not needed
mnemonic: "Super" + "Flu" (like a lot of flu): when you have a superfluous amount of information, it's like having too much flu — it's overwhelming and unnecessary.
hinglish: "Super" + "Flu": jab aapke paas superfluous details hoti hain, toh wo itni adhik hoti hain ki samajhna mushkil ho jaata hai.

meaning: to take the place of or replace something
mnemonic: Super + Seed: when a super seed is planted, it grows to supersede all other plants in the garden, dominating the space.
hinglish: Super + Seed: ek super beej jab boya jaata hai, toh woh baaki sab beejon ko supersede karke sabse bada ped ban jaata hai.

meaning: to replace or take the place of something or someone
mnemonic: Supplant -> 'Supa' (super) + 'Plant': when a super plant grows in your garden, it can supplant the old plants and take over their space.
hinglish: Supa + Plant: jab ek super paudha aapke bagiche mein aata hai, woh purane paudhon ka sthanapann kar leta hai.

meaning: bending and moving easily; flexible
mnemonic: "Supple" -> "Supper": after a nice supper, one feels relaxed and their body becomes more supple, ready for a stretch.
hinglish: "Supper" + "Lachila": achi supper ke baad, aapki body aur bhi lachili aur supple ho jaati hai.

meaning: to earnestly request or beg for something
mnemonic: Supplicate -> Sup + Pleat: after a long day, you might 'sup' (eat) your dinner while you 'pleat' (fold) your hands in prayer, as you supplicate for blessings.
hinglish: Sup + Prarthana: dinner khate waqt aap apne haath prarthana ke liye jor kar rakhte hain, jise aap supplicate kar rahe hain.

meaning: to put an end to something, often by force
mnemonic: "Suppress" -> "Succeed in Pressing": to suppress an idea is to succeed in pressing it down, making it less visible or heard; the authorities chose to suppress dissent.
hinglish: "Daba" + "na": jab aap kisi cheez ko daba dete hain, toh aap usse chhupane ki koshish karte hain, jaise ki unhone protest ko daba diya.

meaning: an excessive amount of something; overindulgence
mnemonic: 'Surf' + 'It': if you surf the web too much, you might have a surfeit of information that overwhelms you.
hinglish: 'Surf' + 'It': agar tum internet par bohot zyada surf karte ho, toh tumhare paas information ki ek surfeit ho sakti hai jo tumhe overwhelm kar deti hai.

meaning: to overcome a difficulty or obstacle
mnemonic: "Sur" + "Mount": when you surmount a mountain, you climb over it successfully. — After weeks of training, he managed to surmount the steep hill during the marathon.
hinglish: "Sur" + "Mount": jab aap kisi pahaad ko surmount karte hain, toh aap us par chadh jaate hain. — Usne itna practice kiya ki wo marathon ke dauran kathin pahaad ko surmount kar gaya.

meaning: kept secret, especially because it would not be approved of
mnemonic: Surreptitious -> 'Surreptitious' sounds like 'Sir, Reptitious': imagine a sneaky student trying to copy homework while the teacher, Sir, is busy — that's a surreptitious act.
hinglish: Sir + Reptitious: teacher sir ke saamne chori se copy karna ek surreptitious kaam hota hai.

meaning: a person appointed to act for another; a substitute
mnemonic: "Surrogate" -> "Surrogate Mother": a surrogate is like a mother who carries a baby for someone else, acting as a substitute.
hinglish: "Surrogate" -> "Sura aur Gati": jab ek aurat kisi aur ke liye bacha paida karti hai, woh surrogate hoti hai, jaise ek sura aur gati ka kaam karna.

meaning: to have a belief or impression that someone is guilty of something without certain proof
mnemonic: Sus + Pect: when you suspect someone, you think something is 'suspect' about them — like having a 'suspect' alibi.
hinglish: Sandeh + Karna: jab tum kisi par sandeh karte ho, to tumhe lagta hai ki uska kuch 'sandeh' hai.

meaning: to cheat or defraud someone of money or property
mnemonic: "Swim" + "Dull": if you swim in dull waters, you might get swindled by a trickster lurking below the surface. — The con artist tried to swindle unsuspecting tourists out of their money.
hinglish: "Swim" + "Dull": agar aap dull paani mein tairenge, toh aapko koi chori karne wala swindle kar sakta hai. — Con artist ne tourists se paisa chori karne ki koshish ki.

meaning: concise, accurate overview or summary
mnemonic: Syn + Optic: think of a synoptic summary as a clear vision (optic) that captures the essence of a topic in a few words.
hinglish: Syn + Optic: ek synoptic summary se humein kisi topic ki saaf nazar (optic) milti hai, jo kuch hi shabdon mein uska saar deti hai.

meaning: understood or implied without being stated
mnemonic: "Tacit" -> "Tactile Sit": when you sit silently in a discussion, your tacit agreement is understood without words.
hinglish: "Tactic" + "Sit": jab aap baith kar bina kuch kahe kisi baat se sahmat hote hain, toh yeh tacit samajh aata hai.

meaning: reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little
mnemonic: "Tacit" + "Turn": when you turn taciturn, you stop speaking, becoming quiet and uncommunicative; a taciturn person says little.
hinglish: "Taksi" + "Turn": jab aap taksi me baithte hain aur zyada nahi bolte, tab aap taciturn hote hain.

meaning: the ability to say and do the right thing in a difficult situation
mnemonic: "Tact" -> "Tactician": a tactician knows how to maneuver through tricky situations with skill and sensitivity — showing tact.
