hinglish: "Tact" -> "Tactician": tactician wo hota hai jo mushkil situations ko samajhkar sahi tarike se samjhaata hai — isse hum tact kehte hain.

meaning: relating to or along the tangent; only slightly or indirectly related to a main point
mnemonic: Tangential -> Tangent + Essential: the tangential points are not essential but merely touch the main idea lightly; his remarks were tangential to the discussion.
hinglish: Tangential -> Tangent + Essential: tangential baatein mudde se zaroori nahin hoti, jaise usne jo kaha woh mudde se tangential tha.

meaning: able to be touched or perceived; real or concrete
mnemonic: Tang + Ible: if something is tangible, you can 'tang' (touch) it, so it becomes real and tangible.
hinglish: Tang + Ible: agar kuch tangible hai, toh aap use 'tang' (touch) kar sakte hain, yani wo haqeeqat hai.

meaning: provoking interest or desire
mnemonic: Tantalus -> 'Tan-tall-us' (a tall tan man): the tall tan man held an enticing piece of fruit just out of reach, making the scene tantalizing for those who wanted it.
hinglish: Tan + Tall + Us: woh tan tall aadmi ek lajawab khana leke chalay gaye, jo sabko tantalizing laga.

meaning: equivalent in value, significance, or effect
mnemonic: Tan + Amount: a tan amount of money is equivalent to a certain value; in the same way, something tantamount means it has equal significance.
hinglish: Tan + Amount: agar aapne tan amount ke liye koi chiz kaam nahi ki, toh wo aur chiz waisa hi hai jaise aapne kuch nahi kiya — wo tantamount hai.

meaning: to lose luster or shine, typically due to oxidation or exposure
mnemonic: "Tarn" (like 'turn') + "Ish" (as in 'ish, it's not great'): when you turn something over, if it’s not polished, it might tarnish, just like how my old jewelry has tarnished over the years.
hinglish: "Tarn" (जैसे 'turn') + "Ish" (जैसे 'ish, ये सही नहीं है'): jab aap kisi cheez ko palatate hain aur wo chamakdar nahi hai, wo tarnish ho jaati hai, bilkul jaise meri purani jewelry ka rang khatam ho gaya hai.

meaning: boring and repetitive; lacking in interest
mnemonic: Ted + ious: imagine a person named Ted who makes everything tedious by repeating the same story, causing everyone to lose interest.
hinglish: Ted + iaus: socho Ted kitna ubau hai kyunki wo hamesha wahi boring kahani sunata hai, sabko ninda aa jaati hai.

meaning: excessive confidence or boldness; audacity
mnemonic: "Temer" (to be bold) + "ity" (state of): his temerity showed he was in a state of boldness to defy the rules.
hinglish: "Himmat" (courage) + "ity": uski himmat ki wajah se usne sabki soch ko badal diya, voh temerity dikhata hai.

meaning: a person's state of mind or emotional condition, often relating to their mood
mnemonic: "Temp" + "Her": if you don't keep your temperature in check, your temper can get hot, causing you to lose control.
hinglish: "Temp" + "Her": agar aap apne temperature ko control nahi karte, toh aapka temper gussa ho sakta hai.

meaning: characterized by strong emotions or turbulent behavior
mnemonic: "Tempest" -> "Temp + Test": when the weather is tempestuous, it's like a test of your patience in a storm, reflecting strong emotions. Thus, his tempestuous behavior led to chaos in the meeting.
hinglish: "Temp" + "Test": jab mausam vi(k)shobhaatmak hota hai, to yeh aapki sabr ki test hoti hai, aur uska vi(k)shobhaatmak vyavhar meeting me hungama kar deta hai.

meaning: relating to worldly as opposed to spiritual affairs; secular
mnemonic: Temp + Oral: if you have a temporal problem, it’s probably a time-related issue you need to discuss orally.
hinglish: Tempor + Oral: agar aapke paas time se sambandhit koi masla hai, toh aapko us par baat karni hogi.

meaning: capable of being maintained or defended against attack or criticism
mnemonic: "Ten" + "Able": if you have ten reasons, your argument is able to stand strong — it is tenable.
hinglish: "Ten" + "Able": agar aapke paas das wajah hain, toh aapka tark mazboot hai — yeh tenable hai.

meaning: expressing a particular viewpoint, often biased or slanted
mnemonic: "Tend" + "Tension": when you tend to a situation with tension, you present a tendentious viewpoint that favors one side. The tendentious debate only highlighted the polarized opinions.
hinglish: "Tend" + "Tension": jab aap kisi mudde ko tension ke saath tend karte hain, toh aapka nazariya tendentious ho jata hai. Uski tendentious baatein sabko alag alag taraf kheench rahi thi.

meaning: not certain or fixed; provisional
mnemonic: "Tent" + "ative": a tent is often set up as a temporary shelter, much like tentative plans that are not yet finalized.
hinglish: "Tent" + "ative": jaise ek tent sirf temporary hota hai, waise hi tentative plans bhi pakke nahin hote hain.

meaning: a very weak or insubstantial connection
mnemonic: Tenuous -> 'Ten' + 'U' (you): if you have only ten friends and only one is reliable, your connection with the rest is tenuous and weak.
hinglish: Ten + U (tum): agar aapke bas dus dost hain aur unme se sirf ek hi sacha hai, to baaki ke sath aapka sambandh tenuos hai.

meaning: moderately warm; lukewarm
mnemonic: Tepid -> 'Tepid Temperature': when water is tepid, it's at a tepid temperature, just warm enough to be uninviting.
hinglish: Tepid -> 'Tepid Thanda': jab paani tepid hai, tab wo na to garam hai na thanda, bas bekaar sa hai.

meaning: concise and to the point; using very few words
mnemonic: "Terse" -> "Curse": When you curse someone, you often do it tersely, using few but impactful words.
hinglish: "Terse" -> "Taar" (wire) + "Saa": jab aap kisi ko terse jawab dete hain, jaise ek taar ki tarah seedha aur sidhe baat karna.

meaning: complete and detailed; not superficial
mnemonic: Thorough -> 'Through' + 'Oar': a thorough investigation goes through every detail like a rower using an oar to navigate every inch of the water.
hinglish: Thorough -> 'Thora' + 'Rukh': thorough ka matlab hai ki study me thoda bhi rukh nahi chhoda, sab kuch dhyan se dekha hai.

meaning: easily frightened; shy or lacking confidence
mnemonic: Timid + Timorous: a timid person often feels timorous in new situations, causing hesitation and fear.
hinglish: Timid + Timorous: ek timid ladki har naye situation me timorous mehsoos karti hai, jisse uska dar badh jata hai.

meaning: a long, angry speech or rant
mnemonic: "Tire Aid" -> "Tired of Aid": when someone is tired (angry) of receiving aid or help, they express their frustration in a long tirade.
hinglish: "Tire Aid" -> "Tired Aid": jab koi madad se thak gaya hota hai, toh wo apne gusse ka izhaar lambi tirade mein karta hai.

meaning: something that represents or stands for something else
mnemonic: "Token" -> "Toke on": When you toke on a joint, it often symbolizes a chill vibe, much like how a token represents a sentiment or idea.
hinglish: "Token" -> "Toka on": Jab tum kisi dost ko koi chhota sa tohfa dete ho, toh wo unke liye ek 'token' hota hai unki dosti ka.

meaning: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy
mnemonic: Torp + Or: like 'torn' and 'bore', when you're bored to tears, you feel torpor and just want to do nothing.
hinglish: Torp + Or: jab aap itne bore hote hain ke kuch nahi karte, tab aap susti ya torpor me hote hain.

meaning: full of twists and turns; not straightforward
mnemonic: "Torture" + "Us": a tortuous journey can feel like it's torturing us with its endless twists and turns.
hinglish: "Tortu" + "Aas": tortuous raste par chalna aisa lagta hai jaise tortu se aise hi aas lag rahi hai.

meaning: to publicize or promote something aggressively
mnemonic: Tout -> 'Shout': when you shout about something, you are trying to tout its greatness to others — in this case, the product.
hinglish: Tout + 'Shout': jab aap kisi cheez ke baare mein shout karte hain, tab aap uske fayde ko tout kar rahe hote hain — jaise ek salesman apni product ka prachar karta hai.

meaning: easily managed or controlled
mnemonic: Track + Table: a table that tracks your progress is tractable, meaning it's easy to follow and manage.
hinglish: Track + Table: jab ek table tumhare kaam ko track karta hai, toh wo sugam hota hai aur aasan hai samajhna.

meaning: peaceful and calm
mnemonic: "Tranquil" -> "Train Cool": to keep a train running smoothly, everything must be tranquil around it, just as a peaceful environment helps maintain calmness.
hinglish: "Train" + "Cool": jab train ko sahi se chalana ho, to aas-paas ka maahaul tranquil hona chahiye, tabhi to sab kuch cool rahega.

meaning: to go beyond the limits of something
mnemonic: "Trans" (across) + "Send": when you send something across, you transcend boundaries. Her achievements transcend the limits of what was thought possible.
hinglish: "Trans" (paar) + "Send": jab aap kuchh paar bhejte hain, tab aap boundaries ko paar karke transcend karte hain. Uski success ne sabhi limits ko paar kar diya.

meaning: an act that goes against a law or moral code
mnemonic: Trans + 'gress' (to step): when you transgress, you step beyond the acceptable limits, violating a rule.
hinglish: Trans + 'gress' (chhalang lagana): jab aap transgress karte hain, aap niyam se aage chhalang lagate hain, jo galat hota hai.

meaning: lasting for a very short time
mnemonic: "Trans" + "ient" (like 'transient'): Think of a train that is transient, stopping only briefly at a station before moving on, just like transient moments that quickly pass.
hinglish: "Trans" + "ient": Ek train jo kuch hi der ke liye rukti hai, waise hi transient lamhein bhi jaldi guzarti hain.

meaning: lasting for a very short time
mnemonic: "Transit" + "Story": a story that passes through quickly, just like a transitory event that doesn't last long.
hinglish: "Transit" + "Kahani": ek kahani jo jaldi guzar jaati hai, jaise transitory pal kabhi rukhte nahi hain.

meaning: a formal and systematic written discourse on a subject
mnemonic: Treat + Ease: a treatise is a detailed, formal discussion that makes it easy to understand complex topics, much like receiving a treat to ease the mind.
hinglish: Treat + Ease: ek treatise ek vyavasthit aur formal likha hua samarthan hai jo mushkil vishayon ko samajhne me aasaan banata hai.

meaning: concise and forcefully expressive
mnemonic: "Trench" -> "Trench Coat": a trench coat is not only stylish but also sharp — just like trenchant remarks that cut through nonsense.
hinglish: "Trench" + "Kant" (sharp): trench coat pehn kar jab woh bolti hai, uski baatein har ek point par trenchant hoti hain.

meaning: of little value or importance
mnemonic: "Try Fling" -> (attempting to throw): if you try to fling something that is trifling, it likely won't matter much.
hinglish: "Try Fling" -> (kuch fenkna): agar aap kuch trifling (nirmaan) cheez fenk rahe ho, toh wo zyada maayne nahi rakhti.

meaning: of little importance or value
mnemonic: Trivial -> 'Trivia' + 'Al': if something is trivial, it's like trivia — small, inconsequential facts that are of little importance.
hinglish: Triv + Al: jab koi baat trivial hoti hai, to wo baat trivia ki tarah hai, jo itni maayne nahi rakhti.

meaning: aggressively defiant or eager to fight
mnemonic: "Truck + You Lent": imagine a truck driver who is truculent, ready to fight if someone tries to take his truck, making him aggressive and combative.
hinglish: "Truck + Tu Lent": socho ek truck driver hai jo ugrat bhav se kehta hai, 'kya tumne mera truck udhar liya?,' voh truculent hai.

meaning: cloudy or opaque, especially due to stirred-up sediment
mnemonic: Turb + id: think of 'turbine' making water muddy — if a turbine spins too fast, it stirs up sediment and makes the water turbid.
hinglish: Turb + id: jab paani mein turbine ghoomega, tab paani dhundhla ho jaayega, yani turbid hoga.

meaning: characterized by disorder or confusion
mnemonic: Turbulent -> Turbulence + Ten: Ten ships were caught in turbulent waters, struggling against the chaotic waves.
hinglish: Turbu + Lent: Jab baarish ho aur hawa tez ho, tab sab kuch turbu (अव्यवस्थित) ho jaata hai.

meaning: swollen and distended, especially due to excessive fluid
mnemonic: Turgid -> Tur+Gid (Tur = swollen, Gid = something that is expanded): The plants looked turgid after the rain, as they were swollen with water.
hinglish: Tur + Gid: baarish ke baad paudhe turgid ho gaye, kyunki unme paani bhara hua tha.

meaning: moral depravity or corruption
mnemonic: Turpitude -> 'Turbid Attitude': a turbid attitude reflects moral confusion and turpitude in character.
hinglish: Turbid + Attitude: ek turbidity se bhara attitude dikhata hai ki uski turpitude kitni hai.

meaning: present everywhere; widespread
mnemonic: "You be quick to us" -> ubiquitous: when you see something as common as smartphones, you think, 'you be quick to us' because they are everywhere.
hinglish: "You be quick to us" -> ubiquitous: aaj kal smartphones itne ubiquitous hain ki har jagah dikhte hain.

meaning: existing beyond what is obvious or admitted; intentionally hidden
mnemonic: Ulterior -> 'Ultra' + 'Near': an ulterior motive is often something ultra (beyond) the surface, lurking near the truth, hidden from view.
hinglish: Ulterior -> 'Ultra' + 'Near': ulterior iraade aksar kuch ultra (par) hote hain, jo sachai ke nazdeek chhupay hote hain.

meaning: a feeling of annoyance or displeasure caused by perceived insult or injury
mnemonic: "Um" + "Brag": if you brag too much, some may take umbrage at your arrogance. — She took umbrage when he boasted about his achievements.
hinglish: "Um" + "Bhaag": agar aap bahut zyada bhaag-dod karte hain, to kuch log umbraj le sakte hain. — Usne woh baat sun kar umbrage liya jab usne dekha ki uski mehnat ko nahi samjha gaya.

meaning: not embellished or decorated; plain
mnemonic: "Un" + "Adorned": when something is unadorned, it is without adornments or decorations, making it plain and simple.
hinglish: "Un" + "Adorned": jab cheez sadi hoti hai, toh usme koi sundarta ya sajawat nahi hoti, bilkul sadi hoti hai.

meaning: pure, without any mixture or adulteration
mnemonic: Un + Alloyed: when you unmix metals, you get unalloyed gold, which is pure and valuable.
hinglish: Un + Alloyed: jab aap metals ko unmix karte hain, toh aapko shuddh sona milta hai, jo ki unalloyed hai.

meaning: to sell goods or services at a lower price than a competitor
mnemonic: "Under" (beneath) + "Cut": if you cut prices beneath your competitors, you're undercutting them. — The store undercut the prices of all its competitors to attract more customers.
hinglish: "Under" (neeche) + "Cut": jab aap kisi aur ki price se neeche price rakhte hain, toh aap unhe undercut kar rahe hain. — Usne apne competitors ki prices ko undercut kiya taaki zyada customers aayein.

meaning: to weaken or damage something gradually or indirectly
mnemonic: Under + Mine: if you dig under a mine, you undermine its stability and integrity.
hinglish: Under + Mine: agar aap kisi mine ke neeche khudai karte hain, toh aap uski stability ko undermine kar dete hain.

meaning: to emphasize or highlight something
mnemonic: "Under" + "Score": If you underscore a text, you put a line under it as if to give it a higher score or importance.
hinglish: "Under" + "Score": Agar aap kisi baat par underscore karte hain, to aap us par zaroori jor dete hain, jaise uski ahmiyat badh jaati hai.

meaning: having a restrained or subtle quality; not overly elaborate or showy
mnemonic: "Under" (beneath) + "Stated" (expressed): when something is understated, it is expressed in a way that is beneath the usual level of extravagance, making it subtly appealing.
hinglish: "Under" (neeche) + "Stated" (kaha gaya): jab kuch understated hota hai, toh yeh uske express hone ka tareeqa hota hai jo aam tor par uncha nahi hota, jo ise subtle aur appealing banata hai.

meaning: applicable to all cases; general or common
mnemonic: "Universe" + "Al": the universe holds everything in a universal embrace, just like this idea applies to all.
hinglish: "Vishva" + "Al": vishwa mein sabke liye universal haq hai, jaise sab logon ko ek saath samajh aata hai.

meaning: never done or known before; without previous example
mnemonic: "Un" (not) + "precedent" (example): without a previous example, the new policy was unprecedented in its approach to education reform.
hinglish: "Un" (nahi) + "precedent" (pichla udaharan): naya kanoon pichle udaharan ke bina tha, isliye yeh abhootpoorv tha.

meaning: to untangle or resolve a complex issue
mnemonic: Un + Ravel: if you 'un' ravel a tangled thread, you are trying to unravel it, just like trying to solve a complex situation.
hinglish: Un + Ravel: jab aap kisi bhool bhulaiya ko suljhaane ki koshish karte hain, tab aap uss masle ko unravel kar rahe hote hain.

meaning: lacking moral principles; not honest or fair
mnemonic: Unscrupulous -> 'Unscrupulous' + 'Croup': in a game that is unscrupulous, players act like croupiers who cheat others out of their bets.
hinglish: Unscrupulous -> 'Uns' (not) + 'Scrupulous' (careful): jab log unscrupulous hote hain, wo kisi bhi tarah se jaise bhi ho, sahi ya galat nahi karte.

meaning: inappropriate or improper behavior or actions
mnemonic: "Un" (not) + "Seemly" (proper): if something is unseemly, it's not proper or appropriate, like rude behavior at a wedding.
hinglish: "Un" (nahi) + "Seemly" (sahi): jab koi vyakti kisi shaadi par bekaar ki baatein karta hai, toh uska vyavhaar avicharpoorn ya unseemly hota hai.

meaning: to scold or criticize someone sharply
mnemonic: Up + Braid: if you 'up' someone's 'braid', you're pulling on their hair in frustration—essentially upbraiding them for their mistakes.
hinglish: Up + Braid: agar aap kisi ke baalon ko 'up' karte hain, toh aap unhe gussa dikhate hain—aise hi aap unhe upbraid kar rahe hain.

meaning: sophisticated, cultured, and suave
mnemonic: "Urban" -> "Urbane": An urbane person is like someone from a city—polished and sophisticated, mingling effortlessly at social events.
hinglish: "Urban" (sheher ka) + "Urbane": sheher ka aadmi hamesha shisht aur sophisticated hota hai, jaise gala ke beech uski urbane adaayen sabki nazar pakad leti hain.

meaning: designed to be useful or practical rather than attractive
mnemonic: "Utility" + "Tarian" (like 'terrain'): a utilitarian approach is all about making the most of the terrain for utility, prioritizing function over form.
hinglish: "Utility" + "Tarian": utilitarian design ka matlab hai, jab aap sab kuch utility ke liye karte hain, na ki sirf sundarta ke liye.

meaning: completely or absolutely
mnemonic: "Utter" + "ly" (like): something is so complete that it's hard to say anything more — she was utterly taken aback by the news.
hinglish: "Utter" (bilkul) + "ly" (tarah se): usne bilkul hi nahi socha tha ki aisa hoga, wo utterly hairaan ho gayi.

meaning: to waver in mind, will, or feeling; to be indecisive
mnemonic: "Vaccine" + "Late": if you vacillate about getting the vaccine, you might be late to protect yourself against illness.
hinglish: "Vaccine" + "Late": agar aap vaccine lene mein hichkichaate hain, toh aap bimar hone se bachne ke liye late ho sakte hain.

meaning: lacking thought or intelligence; empty-headed
mnemonic: "Vacuum" + "us": a vacuum leaves us with nothing, just like a vacuous person lacks substance or depth in thought.
hinglish: "Vacuum" + "hums": vacuum banane se hum kuch nahi sochte, jaise koi vacuous aadmi bina gyaan ke hota hai.

meaning: a farewell speech, especially given at a graduation ceremony
mnemonic: "Valet" + "Dictate": a valet says goodbye when you leave his service; similarly, a valedictory speech is a farewell address. — The valedictory speech is always emotional as it signifies the end of a journey.
hinglish: "Valet" + "Dictate": jab valet aap se vida le raha hota hai, wahi tarah valedictory speech bhi ek vida ka bhashan hota hai. — Valedictory speech har graduation mein hota hai, jab students apne dosto ko goodbye bolte hain.

meaning: bravery in the face of danger or difficulty
mnemonic: Val + Or: if you have value (val) in your actions, you show valor by facing danger.
hinglish: Sahas + Ka: jab aap kisi mushkil mein sahas (sahas) dikhate hain, tab aap valor dikhate hain.

meaning: to defeat or overcome in battle or conflict
mnemonic: "Vanish" + "Quish" (squish): when you squish your enemy, you vanquish them, making them vanish.
hinglish: "Van" + "Quish" (squish): jab aap dushman ko squash karte hain, tab aap unhe vanquish karte hain.

meaning: lacking flavor, zest, or interest; dull
mnemonic: Vap + ID: if something is vapid, it’s like a bad 'ID' that has no character or flavor, making it dull and forgettable.
hinglish: Vap + ID: agar kuch vapid hai, to wo aisa hai jaise 'ID' jisme koi khasiyat ya maza nahi hai, bas bekar hai.

meaning: open to bribery; corrupt
mnemonic: "Vein" + "All": if your veins are all clogged with greed, you are venal, willing to sell your integrity for money.
hinglish: "Vein" + "Sab": agar aapke veins sab paisa ke liye bhare hain, to aap venal hain, matlab aap apni integrity bechne ke liye tayyar hain.

meaning: to regard with great respect or reverence
mnemonic: Vene + Rate: if you rate something highly, you venerate it, showing deep respect.
hinglish: Vene + Rate: jab aap kisi cheez ko high rate dete hain, tab aap uska adhik aadar karte hain.

meaning: truthfulness or accuracy
mnemonic: Veracity -> Very + Accurate: when you are very accurate in your statements, it shows your veracity.
hinglish: Very + Accurate: jab aapki baatein bahut accurate hoti hain, toh aapki satyata (veracity) sabit hoti hai.

meaning: excessively wordy; using more words than necessary
hindi: बोलचाल में अधिक शब्दों का प्रयोग करना
mnemonic: "Verb" + "ose" (like 'rose'): if you add too many verbs to a sentence, it becomes verbose, just like a rose with too many petals can appear messy.
hinglish: "Verb" + "ose" (jaise 'rose'): agar aap ek sentence mein bahut saare verbs daal dete hain, toh woh verbose ho jata hai, jaise ek rose jismein zyada petals ho jate hain toh woh behad khubsurat nahi lagta.

meaning: the appearance of being true or real
mnemonic: Veri + Similar: the closer something is to being similar to the truth, the higher its verisimilitude; like an actor who convincingly portrays a historical figure.
hinglish: Veri + Similaar: jab koi cheez sachai se itni milti julti hai, toh uska verisimilitude bahut zyada hota hai, jaise ek actor jo asal character ki tarah act karta hai.

meaning: used for emphasis, often to highlight a true or genuine instance
mnemonic: Veri -> Very + Table: when something is very true, it's a veritable fact, like a very reliable table of contents.
hinglish: Very + Table: jab kuch bohot sacha hota hai, to woh ek veritable fact hota hai, jaise ek very reliable table of contents.

meaning: able to adapt or be adapted for many different functions or activities
mnemonic: Versa + Tile: think of a tile that can fit in various places in your house — a versatile tile can work in the kitchen or bathroom.
hinglish: Versa + Tile: ek tile jo har jagah fit ho sakti hai, jaise versatile tile har jagah kaam aati hai.

meaning: energy, enthusiasm, or vigor in expression or action
mnemonic: "Ver" + "Vibe": when you have a good vibe, you carry a natural verve that energizes everyone around you; her verve lit up the room.
hinglish: "Ver" + "Aap": jab aap mein verve hoti hai, aapki aakarshan aur utsah dekh kar sabko pasand aata hai; uski verve ne sabka dil jeet liya.

meaning: relating to a body part that has become functionless or reduced during evolution
mnemonic: 'Vest' + 'igial': when a vest becomes too small, it’s reduced to a vestigial piece of clothing that no longer fits.
hinglish: 'Vest' + 'igial': jab vest itni chhoti ho jaati hai ki woh sirf ek darshani avashisht hai, to woh vestigial ho jaata hai.

meaning: a feeling of annoyance or frustration
mnemonic: Vex + Action: when someone takes action to annoy you, it leads to vexation as you feel irritated.
hinglish: Vex + Action: jab koi aise action kare jo aapko pareshan kare, toh aapko vexation hoti hai.

meaning: capable of working successfully; feasible
mnemonic: "Viable" -> "Vibe Able": if a project has a good vibe, it is able to succeed, making it a viable option.
hinglish: "Vibe" + "Able": jab kisi project ki vibe achi hoti hai, toh wo pura hone ke liye capable hota hai, isliye wo viable hota hai.

meaning: keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties
mnemonic: Vigilant -> 'Vigil' + 'Ant': like an ant on guard, always alert and vigilant to avoid danger.
hinglish: Vigil + Ant: ek 'ant' hamesha 'vigilant' hoti hai, jo khud ko khatre se bachaane ke liye hamesha satark rahti hai.

meaning: to speak or write about in an abusively disparaging manner
mnemonic: "Vile" + "ify": when you vilify someone, you make them seem vile or despicable in the eyes of others — like turning a reputation to something disgusting.
hinglish: "Vile" + "karna": jab aap kisi ko vilify karte hain, to aap unhe itna badnaam kar dete hain ke log unhe kharab samajhne lagein.

meaning: extremely poisonous or harmful
mnemonic: "Virus" + "Relentless": a virus that is relentless in its attack is virulent and can be extremely harmful — just like a virulent pathogen.
hinglish: "Virus" + "Relentless": ek virus jo kabhi nahi rukta, wahi virulent hota hai aur bahut khatarnaak hai.

meaning: a person with original ideas about what the future will or could be like
mnemonic: "Vision" + "ary": a person who sees beyond the present into the future is a visionary, like an artist painting a future world.
hinglish: "Vision" + "ary": jise aane wale kal ki tasveer dikhai deti hai, wahi ek visionary hai, jaise ek kalpana shilpi.

meaning: the state of being strong, active, and full of energy
mnemonic: "Vital" + "ity": if you want to live a vital life, you need that extra vitality to keep moving and energizing your day.
hinglish: "Vital" + "ity": agar aapki zindagi mein vitality hai, toh aap har kaam se bharpoor energy se bhare hote hain.

meaning: to spoil or impair the quality or efficiency of something
mnemonic: Vicious + Hate: a vicious attitude can vitiate a person's reputation, making it seem faulty or corrupt.
hinglish: Vicious + Hate: ek vicious attitude kisi ki reputation ko vitiate kar deta hai, isay kharab ya galat dikhata hai.

meaning: full of energy and life; lively
mnemonic: "Viva" (long live) + "Cious" (curious): when someone is vivacious, they live life curiously and energetically, making every moment vibrant.
hinglish: "Viva" (जीवंत) + "Cious" (जिज्ञासु): jab koi vyakti vivacious hota hai, toh wo zindagi ko jijiवंतता se jeeta hai aur har pal ko chamkila banata hai.

meaning: loudly and insistently vocal; expressing opinions in a forceful manner
mnemonic: Vocal + Ferocious: a vociferous protest can be as ferocious as a lion's roar, demanding to be heard above the noise.
hinglish: Vocal + Ferocious: vociferous log hamesha shor machate hain, jaise ek sheri ki roar.

meaning: liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse
mnemonic: "Vol" + "Tile": Just like a tile can easily slip or break if not laid down correctly, a volatile situation can change unexpectedly. The weather can be volatile, shifting from sunny to stormy in an instant.
hinglish: "Vol" + "Taal": Jaise ek taal (musical beat) beech-beech mein badalta hai, waise hi volatile situation kabhi bhi badal sakti hai.

meaning: characterized by a ready and continuous flow of words; talkative
mnemonic: "Vole" (a type of rodent) + "Uble" (like 'able'): a voluble person is able to speak a lot, just like a vole is always scurrying around, making noise.
hinglish: "Bola" (spoke) + "Uble" (like 'able'): baat karne ke liye voluble aadmi hamesha bola laga hota hai, jo kabhi rukta nahi.

meaning: to decrease gradually in size, amount, or intensity
mnemonic: Wane -> 'When' + 'ane' (airtight): when the light gets tight and dimmer, it starts to wane.
hinglish: Wane -> 'Wahan' + 'ane': jab din ke ant me roshni wahan aane lagti hai, to wo kam hone lagti hai, yaani wane ho rahi hai.

meaning: lacking or deficient in some way
mnemonic: Want -> 'Wanting' for something: When you are wanting for something, it means you lack it or desire it.
hinglish: Want + Ting: Jab aap kisi cheez ki kami mehsoos karte hain, toh aap us cheez ke liye wanting hote hain.

meaning: justified or deserved
mnemonic: "Warrant" + "ed": like being awarded a warrant, it means something was justified; the police action was warranted in the dangerous neighborhood.
hinglish: "Warrant" + "ed": jaise kisi ko warrant diya jata hai, waise hi koi cheez jab warranted hoti hai, toh wo justified hoti hai; police ka action warranted tha jab area mein khatara tha.

meaning: difficult to control or predict due to unusual or perverse behavior
mnemonic: Way + Word: when someone goes off the 'way' of normal behavior, their actions can be quite 'wordy' or unpredictable, much like a wayward individual.
hinglish: Way + Word: jab koi 'way' se hato aur 'word' nahi maane, to wo bigda hua hota hai, jaise ek wayward bachcha.

meaning: feeling or showing tiredness, especially as a result of excessive exertion
mnemonic: Wear + Y: when you're so tired you feel like your energy has worn away, you become weary.
hinglish: Wear + ए: jab aap itne thake hue hote hain ki aapka energy 'wear' ho gaya ho, tab aap weary hote hain.

meaning: to persuade someone to do something through flattery or coaxing
mnemonic: "Wheedle" -> "We'd a little": when you'd do a little coaxing or flattery to get what you want, you might wheedle someone into agreeing.
hinglish: "Wheedle" -> "We'd a little": jab aap thodi si baatein karke kisi se kuch chahte hain, tab aap usse wheedle kar rahe hote hain.

meaning: playfully quaint or fanciful, especially in an appealing and amusing way
mnemonic: Whim + Sical: whimsically unique, just like a whimsical character that dances through a story filled with playful adventures.
hinglish: Whim + Sical: ek manmohak kahani mein kaisa bhi ajeeb aur pyara character ho sakta hai, jaise whimsical kahaniyan.

meaning: deliberately done or decided; intentional
mnemonic: Will + Full: when you are 'will full', you are intentionally doing something; he was willful in breaking the rules.
hinglish: Will + Full: jab aap 'will full' hote hain, toh aap jaanbujh kar kuch kar rahe hote hain; uski jaanbujhkar ki gayi ghalti ke liye usay saja mili.

meaning: cleverly deceitful; sly
mnemonic: Wily -> 'Wildly' + 'Sly': a wily person acts wildly clever to deceive others and get what they want.
hinglish: Wily -> 'Wild' + 'Chalak': wily aadmi hamesha chalak hota hai aur doosron ko dhokha dene ki koshish karta hai.

meaning: having or showing a feeling of vague or regretful longing
mnemonic: Wish + Full: when you are full of wishes that never came true, you feel wistful about what could have been.
hinglish: Wish + Fal: jab aap un cheezon ki khwahish rakhte hain jo kabhi poori nahi hui, to aapko wistful mehsoos hota hai.

meaning: to resist or endure successfully
mnemonic: With + Stand: if you stand strong and face challenges, you can withstand any adversity.
hinglish: With + Stand: agar aap mazbooti se khade rahenge, to aap kisi bhi kathinai ka saamna kar sakte hain.

meaning: expressing or conveying a strong sense of misery or distress
mnemonic: Woeful -> 'Woeful Trail': imagine a sad hiker on a woeful trail, lamenting the loss of joy in their journey.
hinglish: Woh + Foul: woh ek aisi khoobsurat jagah par hai jahan sab kuch foul (bura) hai, bilkul woeful hai.

meaning: having or showing a dislike of or prejudice against people from other countries
hindi: विदेशियों के प्रति नफ़रत या पूर्वाग्रह
mnemonic: Xeno -> 'Xeno' (sounds like 'zero') + 'Phobia' (fear): A person with a xenophobic attitude has a 'zero' tolerance for foreigners and is afraid of them.
hinglish: Xeno + Phobia: jise foreigners se dar ho, usko xenophobic kehate hain, kyunki uski foreign logon ke prati 'zero' tolerance hai.

meaning: to produce or provide; to surrender or give way
mnemonic: "Yield" -> "Field Yield": when you cultivate a field, it yields crops during harvest time — yield means to produce.
hinglish: "Kheti" + "Yield": kheti karne par kisan apne khet se anaj yield karte hain.

meaning: having or showing great enthusiasm or passion
mnemonic: Zeal + Us: When we are zealous, our enthusiasm brings zeal to us and everyone around us.
hinglish: Utsaah + Us: Jab hum zealous hote hain, to hamara utsaah hum sabko prerna deta hai.

meaning: the highest point or peak
mnemonic: "Zen" + "It": when you achieve zen, you are at the peak of peace and happiness — the zenith of your joy.
hinglish: "Zen" + "It": jab aap shaanti aur khushi ke zen par hote hain, toh aap apne jeevan ke zenith par hain.
